why.pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg; one has offered to buy it. Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg; one has offered to buy it, and the offer was made publicly so that refusing it would look like hoarding.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reading the Egg — which the main quest's archivists could — would resolve or destroy them. Reading the Egg — which the main quest's archivists could — would resolve or destroy them, and every claimant tribe knows which outcome it is betting on.

places.hook: They did not move — the dead trunk is still the centre of the village

places.name: The Lit Fen
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 315 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A fen where the water itself lights at night from Hist-flower fall.
why.siteAdvantages: Still water directly downstream of a hero Hist's grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the villages come to look, once a year. Nobody; the villages come to look, once a year, on a night fixed by the Tsoko stones rather than by the fen.
why.pressures: It only lights while the tree above flowers, which is a diagnostic nobody wants to need. It only lights while the tree above flowers, which is a diagnostic nobody wants to need — and this year the light came late and stopped early.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree failing would put the fen out. The tree failing would put the fen out, and the fen going out is how the district would learn of it, weeks before the grove admitted anything.

places.hook: Still water directly downstream of a hero Hist's grove

places.name: The Raw Hold
places.whySiteWon: island in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 113 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Blackguard crew hiding in the interior because nowhere else will have them.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep, off every route, with one boat exit.
why.occupantsMotive: Criminals with no ledger and no discipline. Criminals with no ledger and no discipline, most of them three generations out of Blackrose and unable to work anywhere their descent is known.
why.pressures: They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need. They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need, which is the pattern that has finished every raw hold before this one.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village retaliation would finish them within a year. A village retaliation would finish them within a year, and the interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.

places.hook: Deep, off every route, with one boat exit

places.name: Many-Ways
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 38 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that grew as a junction of walkways rather than around a centre.
why.siteAdvantages: Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them. Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them — the junction is the village's whole capital.
why.occupantsMotive: Walkway-keepers who charge for maintenance and argue about who owes what.
why.pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns, and the keepers have begun charging tolls that the tribes using the arms consider extortion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route. Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route, and the tribe in question has started surveying its own alternative rather than keep paying.

places.hook: Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them

places.name: The Pulled Field
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 151 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A grave-stake field where stakes were pulled by looters, raising what the stakes were holding.
why.siteAdvantages: An old village's burial ground, now cut off from any living village.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights, and nothing else. Bog blights, and nothing else — which is why the field has become a training ground the grave-singers send apprentices to, quietly.
why.pressures: The stakes are still being pulled because the grave goods are real. The stakes are still being pulled because the grave goods are real, and the looters are not outsiders but the heirs of the village that abandoned it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking the field would settle it — a deed, not a battle. Restaking the field would settle it — a deed, not a battle — and would settle who the grave goods belong to, which is why nobody local has done it.

places.hook: An old village's burial ground, now cut off from any living village

places.name: The Carriers' Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 91 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A staging post on the route by which the bones of Argonians who died away from the Hist are brought back to the dirt.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the river route meets the interior walking route. Where the river route meets the interior walking route, at the last point a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, who are a recognised profession and a slightly feared one. Carriers, who are a recognised profession and a slightly feared one, paid by the family and never by the village, so their loyalty is always to the dead.
why.pressures: The 4E produced more distant dead than the route can carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: A backlog is already visible in the racks. A backlog is already visible in the racks, and a second season's backlog would force the carriers to choose which families' dead go first — a power no one wants them to have.

places.hook: Where the river route meets the interior walking route

places.name: The Eaten Meer
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 22 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer the forest took: root has replaced stone in about half the structure.
why.siteAdvantages: Nobody defended it and the ground is soft, so the roots won.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever lives in a warm dry hollow. Whatever lives in a warm dry hollow — and, twice a year, the tenders from the clan-tended meer, who come to see what stone becoming root looks like.
why.pressures: It is still settling and floors give way. It is still settling and floors give way, so the treasure-hunting outfits price it as unworkable and the tribes have stopped arguing about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing will change it — it is becoming root, and that is the interior's answer to stone. Nothing will change it — it is becoming root, and that is the interior's answer to stone, which the restarted-work heretics cite as the counter-argument to their own project.

places.hook: Nobody defended it and the ground is soft, so the roots won

places.name: The Choked Spire
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 183 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An older spire that fell in and took its line with it.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands on the route it used to serve, which is why it is still a landmark.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; a shrine at the base gets offerings anyway. Nobody; a shrine at the base gets offerings anyway, left mostly by Waykeepers who will not admit to believing a line can be prayed open.
why.pressures: The line beyond it has been unreachable for a century. The line beyond it has been unreachable for a century, and the villages it served have reorganised their trade around Helstrom instead.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reopening it would restore a route to the deep basin. Reopening it would restore a route to the deep basin, halve the porter relay's traffic, and give the Waykeepers a second terminus they have not asked for.

places.hook: It stands on the route it used to serve, which is why it is still a landmark

places.name: The Open Spire
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A working rootworm-line exit where the root layer vents to the surface.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise the spire could break through without flooding.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers and the porters who meet the line here. Waykeepers and the porters who meet the line here, in an arrangement where neither party can price the other out because neither can work without them.
why.pressures: It is the only exit on this side of the basin and everyone knows it. It is the only exit on this side of the basin and everyone knows it, so the Waykeepers' restricted service is the most valuable faction reward in the interior.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would strand the whole eastern line. A collapse would strand the whole eastern line, and the collapsed spire two days north is what that looks like a century later.

places.hook: A firm rise the spire could break through without flooding

places.name: Ash-Fence
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 206 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.tended-xanmeer-pilgrim-way (+0.91).

why.founding: A village burned in the century of uprisings and never rebuilt.
why.siteAdvantages: It stood on the only firm ground on this reach, which is why the burners came. It stood on the only firm ground on this reach, which is why the burners came — and why nobody has been able to leave the ground unused since.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; a bone-carriers' camp visits.
why.pressures: The neighbouring tribes disagree about who burned it. The neighbouring tribes disagree about who burned it: one says the Legion under Mallicius, one says a rival tribe used the burning as cover.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settled account would let someone rebuild. A settled account would let someone rebuild, and there is firm ground here for a village of two hundred in a district that has none to spare.

places.hook: It stood on the only firm ground on this reach, which is why the burners came

places.name: The High Root
places.whySiteWon: gorge in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 173 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An aerial root that bridged two hammocks and was made walkable rather than cut down.
why.siteAdvantages: Twenty metres up, over ground that floods completely.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the nearest village maintains the rope line. Nobody; the nearest village maintains the rope line, because the alternative is a half-day round the flooded ground and their fish spoils in that time.
why.pressures: The root is alive and is slowly moving. The root is alive and is slowly moving, and the rope line has been re-rigged three times to follow it.
why.wouldChangeIf: It will eventually be too steep to walk, and everyone knows the year. It will eventually be too steep to walk, and everyone knows the year — the village has already started arguing about whether to build a walkway instead.

places.hook: Twenty metres up, over ground that floods completely

places.name: The Basin Line
places.whySiteWon: gorge in interior swamp (danger band 4), 123 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A rope crossing rigged by an expedition that did not come back for it.
why.siteAdvantages: It spans a whitewater reach nothing else crosses.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Nobody — the expedition's gear is still cached at the far anchor, which is the strongest evidence anyone has about where they went.
why.pressures: The rope is old and there is no way to test it but to use it. The rope is old and there is no way to test it but to use it, and the guides price a client's insistence on crossing it accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Someone re-rigging it would open the route again. Someone re-rigging it would open the route again and would put the dead treasure-hunters' camp within a day of the basin guides' shelter.

places.hook: It spans a whitewater reach nothing else crosses

places.name: The Stepped Roof
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer whose terraces are the region's only climbing wall.
why.siteAdvantages: Standing stone above the flood, with the interior intact and sealed.
why.occupantsMotive: None on the roof; plenty below it. None on the roof; plenty below it, which is the whole design of the reward: the climb is safe and the temptation at the top is not.
why.pressures: The route up is easier than the route down. The route up is easier than the route down, and the terrace collects what climbers abandoned rather than carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. Nothing — unless the tending tribe decides that climbing counts as entering, which is a ruling the heretic-stone dispute could force.

places.hook: Standing stone above the flood, with the interior intact and sealed

places.name: The Ripple Spire
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 184 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon gives Middle Argonia pinnacled mountains that come apart at a ripple; this is the one close enough to a route that people have repeatedly tried to climb it.
why.siteAdvantages: A root-and-mudstone spire standing clear of the canopy on a ridge end — in a region with almost no long sightlines, it is one of the only things that reads at distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. Two climbers' caches and a great deal of abandoned gear say who has tried.
why.pressures: The debris fan at the base has both old falls and one from this season; the route was marked, then deliberately unmarked by someone.
why.wouldChangeIf: It will fall. The interesting question is whether anyone is on it.

hardConstraints: a debris fan at the base
places.hook: A root-and-mudstone spire standing clear of the canopy on a ridge end — in a region with almost no long sightlines, it is one of the only things that reads at distance

places.name: The Quiet Camp
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 332 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Unbound Root staging camp for work on a nearby tree.
why.siteAdvantages: Close enough to the target root line and far enough from any village.
why.occupantsMotive: Cultists staging, not raiding — this is a work camp with a doctrine. Cultists staging, not raiding — this is a work camp with a doctrine, and the doctrine is that a tree severed from the collective can be spoken to alone.
why.pressures: The nearest village has noticed the traffic. The nearest village has noticed the traffic and has said nothing, because the two households who noticed first are being paid.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exposure moves them deeper. Exposure moves them deeper, and the gallery cell they are supplying would lose its method-testing site with a season's work still to do.

places.hook: Close enough to the target root line and far enough from any village

places.name: Cut-and-Carried
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 241 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribe whose tree died carried a root fragment two days' walk and replanted it — the Lilmoth precedent, done by villagers.
why.siteAdvantages: New ground chosen for the cutting's sake: spring water, shelter, no old roots to compete.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe raising a tree the way others raise a clutch. A tribe raising a tree the way others raise a clutch, with a tending rota that has replaced every office the old tree supported.
why.pressures: The cutting speaks faintly and only to two of them, which is beginning to be a political fact. The cutting speaks faintly and only to two of them, which is beginning to be a political fact: those two are young and neither wanted the standing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the cutting failed they would have nothing left to be. If the cutting failed they would have nothing left to be, and the Hist-less refuge two days away has already offered to take them, which they find unbearable.

places.hook: New ground chosen for the cutting's sake: spring water, shelter, no old roots to compete

places.name: The Milking Shed
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 490 m from the nearest route; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A daril operation that needs live venomous stock, constant heat and no neighbours.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep interior warmth and total isolation — the three requirements met at once. Deep interior warmth and total isolation — the three requirements met at once, on ground too poor to interest any tribe.
why.occupantsMotive: Fermenters who are half chemists and half snake-keepers.
why.pressures: Their product ruins people in four cities and they know their buyers by name. Their product ruins people in four cities and they know their buyers by name, and one of those buyers is now buying more than the cities can consume.
why.wouldChangeIf: A raid would move the trade, not end it. A raid would move the trade, not end it — the stock is the asset, and it walks.

places.hook: Deep interior warmth and total isolation — the three requirements met at once

places.name: The Sunk Well
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 607 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, remote, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer's ceremonial well shaft, now the only way into its flooded lower halls.
why.siteAdvantages: A vertical shaft in stone that has not moved in an age.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the shaft is the entrance to something that is. Nothing living; the shaft is the entrance to something that is, and the divers who work it go in pairs and come out alone often enough to be notable.
why.pressures: The water is rising and the entrance ledge is nearly submerged. The water is rising and the entrance ledge is nearly submerged, which will shortly turn a difficult dive into an impossible one.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry season opens two more chambers. A dry season opens two more chambers and would bring every treasure outfit in the interior to a ruin the tenders consider consecrated.

places.hook: A vertical shaft in stone that has not moved in an age

places.name: The Bared Flat
places.whySiteWon: oxbow in firm lowland (danger band 3), 570 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.rootworm-burrow-dead (+1.22).

why.founding: A shallow bed that empties in the dry season and exposes everything ever lost in it.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide shallow basin with a seasonal outlet.
why.occupantsMotive: Scavengers, in season; nothing, out of it. Scavengers, in season; nothing, out of it — and the same four families each year, who treat the window as inherited property.
why.pressures: The exposure window is short and competitive. The exposure window is short and competitive, and last year two of the families arrived early and drained a channel to widen it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter cycle would close the window entirely. A wetter cycle would close the window entirely and would end an income four households have built their year around.

places.hook: A wide shallow basin with a seasonal outlet

places.name: The Sap Wallow
places.whySiteWon: oxbow in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 165 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A natural sap pool used for sanctioned communion, licensed by the nearest tree-minder.
why.siteAdvantages: Where a hero Hist's roots surface in a hollow and fill it.
why.occupantsMotive: A tender who controls dose and turn. A tender who controls dose and turn, appointed by the tree-minder and answerable to the grove rather than to the users.
why.pressures: Unlicensed users come at night; the tender knows and mostly allows it. Unlicensed users come at night; the tender knows and mostly allows it, on the calculation that a policed wallow becomes a starblossom hollow.
why.wouldChangeIf: Overuse would produce another Miredance. Overuse would produce another Miredance, which is two days away and is the argument the tender uses on anyone who wants the dose raised.

places.hook: Where a hero Hist's roots surface in a hollow and fill it

places.name: Starblossom Hollow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 117 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A wallow used for the other kind of dreaming, without a tree's permission.
why.siteAdvantages: A cold hollow where starblossom grows thickly.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody official; users, and someone who sells to them. Nobody official; users, and someone who sells to them, who is from the licensed stage and is not supposed to be here at all.
why.pressures: The tree-minders regard it as theft of a rite. The tree-minders regard it as theft of a rite, and have twice asked the assembly to name it, which would make it prosecutable and popular.
why.wouldChangeIf: A crackdown would move it, not end it. A crackdown would move it, not end it — the plant grows in every cold hollow in the district and the hollows are not countable.

places.hook: A cold hollow where starblossom grows thickly

places.name: The Pull
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tidal delta (danger band 3), 272 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A narrows where the wet-season flow becomes lethal for a fortnight.
why.siteAdvantages: The only crossing on this reach, and the pinch is why.
why.occupantsMotive: None; the nearest village posts a watch in season. None; the nearest village posts a watch in season, unpaid, on a rota that the two poorest households do most of.
why.pressures: The watch is not always posted. The watch is not always posted, and the years it lapses are the years the village has men working the porter relay instead.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bridge would solve it and no one will pay. A bridge would solve it and no one will pay — the four villages that would use it each hold that the crossing benefits the others more.

places.hook: The only crossing on this reach, and the pinch is why

places.name: The Unmade Work
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 203 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.tended-xanmeer-clan-north (+1.29).

why.founding: A xanmeer taken apart by its own builders at the Duskfall rather than abandoned.
why.siteAdvantages: The stone was carried away, so what remains is the plan, not the building.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The heretic-stone village quarries it and is condemned for that. Nobody. The heretic-stone village quarries it and is condemned for that, and the condemnation has not stopped a single cart.
why.pressures: It is the clearest physical evidence of the renunciation, and the restarted work is using it. It is the clearest physical evidence of the renunciation, and the restarted work is using it — so the monument to the taboo is being eaten by the taboo's breach.
why.wouldChangeIf: Rebuilding on it would be the loudest possible statement. Rebuilding on it would be the loudest possible statement, and the Helstrom assembly has avoided visiting for eleven years rather than have to respond to one.

places.hook: The stone was carried away, so what remains is the plan, not the building

places.name: The Fenlord's Reach
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 214 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-deep-throat (+0.74).

why.founding: An Ayleid fenlord's tomb in ground the marsh has kept sealed.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep basin; no route, no neighbours, no witnesses. Deep basin; no route, no neighbours, no witnesses — and the marsh has kept the seal wet, which is why the stone has not moved.
why.occupantsMotive: The tomb's own occupants. The tomb's own occupants, undisturbed since before the Duskfall and unrelated to anything the interior tribes recognise as dead.
why.pressures: It is intact, which is why nothing that has entered has come out. It is intact, which is why nothing that has entered has come out; two antiquarian parties are known to have gone in and the second went looking for the first.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing.

places.hook: Deep basin; no route, no neighbours, no witnesses

places.name: One-Rise
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 165 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Six households on the only ground for two kilometres that stays dry in the wet season.
why.siteAdvantages: A single flood-high rise, entirely occupied.
why.occupantsMotive: Farmers who cannot expand and will not leave. Farmers who cannot expand and will not leave, working back-swamp rice that only exists because the rise splits the flood.
why.pressures: Every neighbour wants shelter on their rise in the wet season and they cannot house them. Every neighbour wants shelter on their rise in the wet season and they cannot house them, and the refusals are remembered longer than the floods.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter decade would make them a refuge camp instead of a hamlet. A wetter decade would make them a refuge camp instead of a hamlet, and the households already know which of them would have to go.

places.hook: A single flood-high rise, entirely occupied

places.name: Greenspring
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 128 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Founded at the Panther fork on springs that are genuinely drinkable — a rare enough thing here to found a village on.
why.siteAdvantages: Fork of two channels, clean water, and the last firm ground before the Helstrom approach.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe that has made itself indispensable as the interior's last friendly stop. A tribe that has made itself indispensable as the interior's last friendly stop, and charges nothing for water and a great deal for everything else.
why.pressures: Everyone who goes to Helstrom passes through, including people the tribe would rather not host. Everyone who goes to Helstrom passes through, including people the tribe would rather not host — cult couriers, tappers, and the Veiled Reed's factors.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the springs soured the village would move within a season. If the springs soured the village would move within a season, and the Helstrom approach would lose its only guaranteed clean water in a day's radius.

places.hook: Fork of two channels, clean water, and the last firm ground before the Helstrom approach

places.name: The Far Shelter
places.whySiteWon: islet in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 398 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The second night's shelter on the basin crossing, kept stocked by the guides themselves.
why.siteAdvantages: The one piece of defensible dry ground at the right distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Whoever is crossing; a caretaker in season. Whoever is crossing; a caretaker in season, paid jointly by the guides in a levy that has never once been collected in full.
why.pressures: Stocks get taken by people who do not replace them. Stocks get taken by people who do not replace them, and the guides have started marking the crates so that they know whose clients did it.
why.wouldChangeIf: An unstocked shelter costs lives and everyone knows it. An unstocked shelter costs lives and everyone knows it, which is why the guides at the gate camp price the second night higher than the first.

places.hook: The one piece of defensible dry ground at the right distance

places.name: Gate-Side Camp
places.whySiteWon: islet in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 722 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The camp where basin guides wait for hire outside the Helstrom gate.
why.siteAdvantages: Just outside the gate — inside is D0 and the guides are not welcome to loiter there.
why.occupantsMotive: Guides who price by the day and by the route. Guides who price by the day and by the route, and who will refuse a route outright rather than negotiate it — the refusal is the profession.
why.pressures: Guides die, and the camp's roster is visibly shorter than it was. Guides die, and the camp's roster is visibly shorter than it was; the basin has not got worse, but the traffic has got heavier and less experienced.
why.wouldChangeIf: The main quest's expedition hires from here. The main quest's expedition hires from here, and a hiring on that scale would empty the camp of everyone competent for a season.

places.hook: Just outside the gate — inside is D0 and the guides are not welcome to loiter there

places.name: The Roost
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A dead standing grove that hackwings have used for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead timber with clear flight lines — everything a roost needs.
why.occupantsMotive: The flock. The flock, which has used this grove long enough that the beast-keepers' grandparents complained about the same birds.
why.pressures: They take from the beast-keepers' young stock and the keepers want them gone. They take from the beast-keepers' young stock and the keepers want them gone; the tribe that owns the grove takes hackwing feathers for its own rites and does not.
why.wouldChangeIf: Culling the roost would end a real nuisance and a real spectacle. Culling the roost would end a real nuisance and a real spectacle, and would cost that tribe the only feather source it recognises as legitimate.

places.hook: Dead timber with clear flight lines — everything a roost needs

places.name: Crown of the First Line
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 241 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The ancestor terrace of a tribe that buries high because the ground drowns.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest hammock crown in the district.
why.occupantsMotive: Grave-singers who visit; nobody lives here. Grave-singers who visit; nobody lives here, and the tribe considers residence on the crown a form of trespass on its own ancestors.
why.pressures: Bone-thieves and antiquarians; the tribe patrols in response. Bone-thieves and antiquarians; the tribe patrols in response, and the patrol is now a standing duty that takes four adults out of the fields.
why.wouldChangeIf: A flood reaching the crown would be read as a judgement. A flood reaching the crown would be read as a judgement, and the tribe has already been told twice by a Nisswo that it is coming.

places.hook: The highest hammock crown in the district

places.name: Green-Moss Hammock
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 454 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'island' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village on a tree-island that has never flooded in memory.
why.siteAdvantages: A raised hammock with big timber, dry storage and its own spring.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe rich in dry storage in a region that has almost none. A tribe rich in dry storage in a region that has almost none, and richer still in the obligations that storing other people's grain creates.
why.pressures: They store other villages' seed grain and the obligations that come with it. They store other villages' seed grain and the obligations that come with it, and have begun charging in labour rather than in kind, which is how a store becomes a lordship.
why.wouldChangeIf: A theft or a rot in the store would ruin four villages at once. A theft or a rot in the store would ruin four villages at once, and the tribe has no way to insure against it except by holding more.

places.hook: A raised hammock with big timber, dry storage and its own spring

places.name: The Bled Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 450 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribal Hist industrially tapped by an outside operation during the Imperial century and never allowed to close.
why.siteAdvantages: Close to a navigable channel — which is why it was chosen and why it is still worked.
why.occupantsMotive: A tapping crew who are not local and a village that has to watch. A tapping crew who are not local and a village that has to watch, under a concession issued by an authority that has not existed for a century.
why.pressures: The village feels every cut; the crew is armed and licensed by a lapsed authority. The village feels every cut; the crew is armed and licensed by a lapsed authority, and sells to the same city fence the sap poachers use.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending the tapping is a quest-shaped act with a village that would owe the player. Ending the tapping is a quest-shaped act with a village that would owe the player, and would put the fence's whole interior supply on the poachers alone.

places.hook: Close to a navigable channel — which is why it was chosen and why it is still worked

places.name: Helstrom
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'helstrom' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Survivors of the Battle of Argonia withdrew to the one place outsiders could not follow, and the grove kept them.
why.siteAdvantages: Spring-fed firm ground inside the Hist forest; every interior route ends here and none passes through.
why.occupantsMotive: An assembly of interior naheesh and tree-minders who receive and redistribute rather than rule. An assembly of interior naheesh and tree-minders who receive and redistribute rather than rule, and whose authority ends at the point where a tribe stops sending a delegate.
why.pressures: The basin outside the gates is lethal and the city depends on escorted traffic through it; the throne has been empty for centuries.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the interior tribes stopped sending delegates, Helstrom would be a grove with a market in it. If the interior tribes stopped sending delegates, Helstrom would be a grove with a market in it — and the convocation's attendance is already falling, publicly and countably.

reachedVia: escorted boat convoy from Alten Corimont
places.hook: Spring-fed firm ground inside the Hist forest; every interior route ends here and none passes through

places.name: The Restarted Work
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 182 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribe that decided the Duskfall renunciation of stone was a mistake and began building again.
why.siteAdvantages: An unfinished xanmeer terrace they did not have to quarry — the stone was already cut and abandoned mid-build.
why.occupantsMotive: Builders who believe permanence is owed to their descendants; a naheesh who says so publicly. Builders who believe permanence is owed to their descendants; a naheesh who says so publicly, and who has been refused a place at the convocation twice for saying it.
why.pressures: Every neighbouring tribe treats them as heretics, and the Nisswo have opinions. Every neighbouring tribe treats them as heretics, and the Nisswo have opinions — but the village trades normally, because nobody will refuse cut stone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Completion would force the interior to decide whether the taboo is law. Completion would force the interior to decide whether the taboo is law, and the assembly at Helstrom has no procedure for deciding anything of the kind.

places.hook: An unfinished xanmeer terrace they did not have to quarry — the stone was already cut and abandoned mid-build

places.name: The Set-Aside Hut
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 301 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribal exile living precisely at the distance their sentence specifies.
why.siteAdvantages: The measured edge of their tribe's territory, marked by a totem they may not pass.
why.occupantsMotive: One exile serving a term that has an end date they intend to reach. One exile serving a term that has an end date they intend to reach, and who has kept a tally on the totem that is now the most reliable calendar in the district.
why.pressures: Their family leaves food at the totem and does not cross it. Their family leaves food at the totem and does not cross it, and the youngest of them has started crossing it, which nobody has yet reported.
why.wouldChangeIf: The sentence ends in four years and they are counting. The sentence ends in four years and they are counting — and the village that sentenced them has changed naheesh twice since and may not honour it.

places.hook: The measured edge of their tribe's territory, marked by a totem they may not pass

places.name: The Talker
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 231 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Someone who went into the basin and stayed.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry root hollow with water and no neighbours. A dry root hollow with water and no neighbours, which in the basin is a survivable site and explains why they have lasted this long.
why.occupantsMotive: One person, in communion with something, possibly a tree, possibly not.
why.pressures: They are becoming harder to talk to each year. They are becoming harder to talk to each year, and what they say now is in the cadence the sap-touched village uses, which they have never visited.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing; they will die here. Nothing; they will die here — but what they know about the basin's routes is worth more than anything in the region's caches.

places.hook: A dry root hollow with water and no neighbours

places.name: Needle-Crown, the Agaceph Hist
places.whySiteWon: spring head in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 625 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: One of the very old trees of the deep basin; the Agaceph are its people and its shape.
why.siteAdvantages: Spring-head firm ground with landings on three channels.
why.occupantsMotive: Tree-minder, sap-speaker and root-herald, all hereditary. Tree-minder, sap-speaker and root-herald, all hereditary, and all three offices currently held by one family, which the neighbouring tribes have noticed.
why.pressures: Pilgrim traffic it did not ask for and cannot refuse. Pilgrim traffic it did not ask for and cannot refuse, camped at the sap road a half-day out and arriving faster than the grove can feed them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Withdrawal — the main quest's premise — would end its tribe as a culture. Withdrawal — the main quest's premise — would end its tribe as a culture, and the Agaceph's three landings would close the district's fastest route with it.

places.hook: Spring-head firm ground with landings on three channels

places.name: First-Rain Trunk
places.whySiteWon: island in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 311 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Named in interior recitation as the tree that stood at the first rain after the Duskfall.
why.siteAdvantages: An island in still water, so the fire that took its northern half never crossed to the grove.
why.occupantsMotive: A very small vigil of tenders who expect to see it die. A very small vigil of tenders who expect to see it die, and who have refused every offer of help that came with a condition attached.
why.pressures: It is dying, slowly, and no cutting from it has ever taken. It is dying, slowly, and no cutting from it has ever taken, including the one the cut-and-carried tribe was given and could not raise.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its death would produce the largest Mnemic Egg in the province — which several factions already want. Its death would produce the largest Mnemic Egg in the province — which several factions already want, and one of which has a camp within a day of the grove.

places.hook: An island in still water, so the fire that took its northern half never crossed to the grove

places.name: No-Tree Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 609 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A settlement of the Hist-less who could not stay in the cities and would not be taken in by tribes.
why.siteAdvantages: Ground nobody claims because no tree's roots reach it — which is exactly the point.
why.occupantsMotive: People with no communion, no naming rite and no soul-return, organising all three for themselves. People with no communion, no naming rite and no soul-return, organising all three for themselves — badly, publicly, and with a growing body of precedent.
why.pressures: The interior tribes regard them as a category error; the League of Open Water regards them as a cause. The interior tribes regard them as a category error; the League of Open Water regards them as a cause, and its coastal money is beginning to arrive.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tree taking them in would dissolve the settlement, and some of them do not want that. A tree taking them in would dissolve the settlement, and some of them do not want that — which is the argument that splits the camp every winter.

places.hook: Ground nobody claims because no tree's roots reach it — which is exactly the point

places.name: Low-Crown, the Paatru Hist
places.whySiteWon: spring head in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 11 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An old tree that grew wide instead of tall in ground too soft to hold a crown.
why.siteAdvantages: A flood-high rise ringed by soft mire that keeps carts, horses and outsiders out.
why.occupantsMotive: The Paatru, who regard height as a discourtesy. The Paatru, who regard height as a discourtesy, and who build nothing above the tree's lowest branch — a rule they apply to visitors' tents as well.
why.pressures: Its people are physically unlike their neighbours and are treated accordingly. Its people are physically unlike their neighbours and are treated accordingly, which is why the Paatru trade through the walkway junction and never in person.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the mire dried, the village would be walkable and would not survive it. If the mire dried, the village would be walkable and would not survive it — the mire is the whole defence and the whole reason the tribe is left alone.

places.hook: A flood-high rise ringed by soft mire that keeps carts, horses and outsiders out

places.name: High-Flower, the Sarpa Hist
places.whySiteWon: spring head in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 126 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Sarpa's tree, tended from the canopy for as long as anyone has counted.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge-end above the flood with clear air for launching.
why.occupantsMotive: Winged Sarpa who consider the ground a burial place. Winged Sarpa who consider the ground a burial place, and who therefore hold their trade, their courts and their hatching entirely above it.
why.pressures: The climb is the only approach and the tribe likes it that way. The climb is the only approach and the tribe likes it that way, so every dealing with the Sarpa happens at somebody else's landing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the crown platforms in a storm would strand the rite for a generation. Losing the crown platforms in a storm would strand the rite for a generation, and the timber to rebuild them has to come from the hammock village two days away.

places.hook: A ridge-end above the flood with clear air for launching

places.name: The Kept Line
places.whySiteWon: isthmus in interior swamp (danger band 5), 70 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribe that has watched one thing for so long that watching it is now their whole identity.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge-end overlooking a sealed xanmeer they will not let anyone approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Hereditary wardens who inherit a post, not a trade. Hereditary wardens who inherit a post, not a trade, and who are therefore fed by a tribe that gets nothing back but the watching.
why.pressures: Nobody alive knows what is inside the thing they are guarding. Nobody alive knows what is inside the thing they are guarding, and the last three generations of wardens have each privately concluded something different.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening it would end the tribe's reason to exist. Opening it would end the tribe's reason to exist, which is why the wardens will fight an antiquarian harder than they would fight a looter.

places.hook: A ridge-end overlooking a sealed xanmeer they will not let anyone approach

places.name: Medusa Wood
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 648 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A stand of drowned forest in the deepest basin water that the tribes name and do not enter.
why.siteAdvantages: The deepest standing water in the interior, over a drowned forest that never rotted.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever is down there, which nobody has described twice the same way. Whatever is down there, which nobody has described twice the same way, and which the tribes name in recitation without ever naming a witness.
why.pressures: The name is old and the stories are older than the name. The name is old and the stories are older than the name, and the drowned timber is the finest in the province, which keeps the argument alive.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. Nothing — though the dredging outfits on the coast have begun asking what a stand of never-rotted forest would be worth lifted.

places.hook: The deepest standing water in the interior, over a drowned forest that never rotted

places.name: The Lost City
places.whySiteWon: summit in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 879 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Built before the Duskfall around the graft the quest plan calls the Root of Accord; unmade from the map rather than destroyed.
why.siteAdvantages: The deepest ground of the basin, where no route goes and the root layer is densest. The deepest ground of the basin, where no route goes and the root layer is densest — the density is not incidental, it is what was grown here.
why.occupantsMotive: No inhabitants — cult expedition, guardians, and whatever the Accord left tending itself. No inhabitants — cult expedition, guardians, and whatever the Accord left tending itself, which has had an age with nothing to do but tend.
why.pressures: The Unbound Root is trying to reach it; the Eye is the only key.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing changes it; it is the endgame and it is static by design.

places.hook: The deepest ground of the basin, where no route goes and the root layer is densest

places.name: The Wading Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 859 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A marsh giant's range, which the tribes route around without discussion.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep water it can stand in and shallow it can feed in.
why.occupantsMotive: One giant, and the birds that follow it. One giant, and the birds that follow it, and a hunting pattern the tribes have mapped precisely enough to route around without a guide.
why.pressures: Its range is expanding toward a walkway route. Its range is expanding toward a walkway route, and the walkway village has begun asking whether killing one is really the offence everyone says it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Moving the walkway costs a season's labour; the alternative is worse. Moving the walkway costs a season's labour; the alternative is worse, and the tribe that would have to fund the move is the one that uses the arm least.

places.hook: Deep water it can stand in and shallow it can feed in

places.name: The Counting Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Knahaten Flu mass grave for the villages that emptied along this reach.
why.siteAdvantages: Flat ground nobody wanted afterwards.
why.occupantsMotive: A memorial keeper from the nearest village. A memorial keeper from the nearest village, a post that carries no pay and an exemption from every other village duty.
why.pressures: The count on the stone is disputed and has been recut twice. The count on the stone is disputed and has been recut twice, each time upward, and each recut has been paid for by a different tribe with a different interest.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recount would restart the argument. A recount would restart the argument, and the Kothringi names that a recount would have to include are the part nobody will raise.

places.hook: Flat ground nobody wanted afterwards

places.name: The Chukka-Sei Ground
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 358 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The trial ground where the interior's young are given their adult name.
why.siteAdvantages: A stretch of genuinely dangerous water and root that can be survived by a prepared adolescent.
why.occupantsMotive: Trial-keepers who set the route each year and will not explain it. Trial-keepers who set the route each year and will not explain it, on the principle that a route that can be described has already been failed.
why.pressures: The trial kills someone every few years and the tribes have decided that is correct. The trial kills someone every few years and the tribes have decided that is correct, which is easier to hold when it is not your clutch's year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A death in the wrong family would force a change. A death in the wrong family would force a change, and the family in question — the Agaceph tree-minders' — has a candidate in the coming season.

places.hook: A stretch of genuinely dangerous water and root that can be survived by a prepared adolescent

places.name: Kaal-Meen's Stone
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 5), 271 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A guide who died bringing a party out of the basin; her clients paid for the stone.
why.siteAdvantages: Where she stopped, on the route she was walking.
why.occupantsMotive: None; passing guides touch it. None; passing guides touch it, and the gate camp's roster is read against her name each season as a way of counting the year's losses.
why.pressures: The route has moved and the stone is now off it. The route has moved and the stone is now off it, so the touching has become a detour that fewer guides make each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing; it will be swallowed. Nothing; it will be swallowed — unless someone moves it, which the guides have discussed and rejected as the second death.

places.hook: Where she stopped, on the route she was walking

places.name: The Ward
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 451 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A miregaunt has stood on this approach for as long as anyone has known the ruin behind it.
why.siteAdvantages: The one dry approach to a sealed xanmeer.
why.occupantsMotive: One miregaunt, which is part of the land and returns when killed. One miregaunt, which is part of the land and returns when killed, and which does not follow beyond the approach it holds.
why.pressures: It is a permanent toll on the route in a currency of lives. It is a permanent toll on the route in a currency of lives, and the hereditary wardens above regard it as an ally they did not have to feed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. It comes back. Nothing. It comes back — but the cavity relic it carries is taken by whoever kills it, and that is the only renewable prize in the district.

places.hook: The one dry approach to a sealed xanmeer

places.name: The Held Mist
places.whySiteWon: sinkhole in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 74 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A hollow that holds its own mist year-round because nothing moves the air in it.
why.siteAdvantages: A deep bowl under closed canopy with a cold spring at the bottom.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing you can see, which is the problem. Nothing you can see, which is the problem, and which the guides handle by refusing the hollow rather than by explaining it.
why.pressures: People go in and come out somewhere else, having lost hours. People go in and come out somewhere else, having lost hours, and two of the wisp-lure stories in the district are probably this place misattributed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing; it is weather. Nothing; it is weather — which is the only reassurance the guides offer and the one their clients least believe.

places.hook: A deep bowl under closed canopy with a cold spring at the bottom

places.name: The Tenders' Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that exists to service the grave-stake fields of six neighbouring tribes.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground with landings, central to the fields it serves and downwind of all of them.
why.occupantsMotive: Grave-singers and stake-carvers who are paid in food and are never invited to anything. Grave-singers and stake-carvers who are paid in food and are never invited to anything, and whose children are not accepted as marriage partners in any of the six tribes they serve.
why.pressures: Bog blights rise when a stake is pulled, and stakes are pulled more often since Umbriel. Bog blights rise when a stake is pulled, and stakes are pulled more often since Umbriel; the village is now turning work away and being blamed for the risings it could not reach.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a neighbouring tribe learned to carve its own stakes, this village would starve. If a neighbouring tribe learned to carve its own stakes, this village would starve — which is why the carving is taught by demonstration and never described.

places.hook: Firm ground with landings, central to the fields it serves and downwind of all of them

places.name: The Lightless Village
places.whySiteWon: gorge in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 420 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that stopped using fire and lamps generations ago and reorganised itself around not being seen.
why.siteAdvantages: Under the densest closed canopy in the province, where the difference between noon and midnight is small.
why.occupantsMotive: People whose eyes have adapted and whose etiquette is entirely acoustic. People whose eyes have adapted and whose etiquette is entirely acoustic, and who conduct trade by leaving goods and counted taps rather than by meeting.
why.pressures: Something in the surrounding dark taught them this and is still out there. Something in the surrounding dark taught them this and is still out there, and the youngest generation has begun to doubt it, which the elders regard as the first stage of the lesson.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single lamp carried in would be an act of violence. A single lamp carried in would be an act of violence, and the guides charge extra to explain that to clients before they arrive rather than after.

places.hook: Under the densest closed canopy in the province, where the difference between noon and midnight is small

places.name: Nine-Trunks
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 184 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village grown where nine root-joined trunks stand in one ring — one tree by the Hist's reckoning, nine by anyone else's.
why.siteAdvantages: The ring encloses firm ground and makes its own stockade.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe that hosts the convocation's overflow and has grown rich on it. A tribe that hosts the convocation's overflow and has grown rich on it, holding pitch-rights it rents to delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp.
why.pressures: Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made them arrogant the other eleven. Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made them arrogant the other eleven, and two neighbouring tribes now camp at Greenspring instead on principle.
why.wouldChangeIf: A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village. A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village, and the falling attendance the Root Talk ground counts publicly is already showing in their rents.

places.hook: The ring encloses firm ground and makes its own stockade

places.name: The Turning House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A rest house kept by the Nisswo on the Helstrom pilgrim road.
why.siteAdvantages: One day's walk from the gate — deliberately the last stop.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo who preach at whoever stops, and feed them either way. Nisswo who preach at whoever stops, and feed them either way — the feeding is the doctrine's proof and the preaching is the price.
why.pressures: The Hist establishment and the Sithis preachers disagree about the interior's soul, politely. The Hist establishment and the Sithis preachers disagree about the interior's soul, politely, and the politeness is maintained because Helstrom's assembly would have to act if it broke.
why.wouldChangeIf: A closure would leave the last day of the road unsheltered. A closure would leave the last day of the road unsheltered, and the pilgrims would arrive at the gate camp instead, which the guides would charge them for.

places.hook: One day's walk from the gate — deliberately the last stop

places.name: The Singer's House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 5), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A grave-singer lives apart from the villages they serve, by custom and by preference.
why.siteAdvantages: Between five villages, on ground none of them claims. Between five villages, on ground none of them claims, which is also why none of them will repair the house.
why.occupantsMotive: A grave-singer and an apprentice who does not want the job.
why.pressures: More staking work since Umbriel than one singer can do. More staking work since Umbriel than one singer can do, and the necropolis village a day away has offered to take the circuit, which the five villages cannot afford.
why.wouldChangeIf: The apprentice leaving would strand five villages' dead. The apprentice leaving would strand five villages' dead, and the apprentice has family at the Hist-less refuge and has been asking about it.

places.hook: Between five villages, on ground none of them claims

places.name: The Minder's House
places.whySiteWon: islet in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tree-minder's house, sited by the tree rather than by the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Within sight and earshot of the tree at all times — the post requires it.
why.occupantsMotive: A tree-minder and a second tender who is always present when the first listens. A tree-minder and a second tender who is always present when the first listens, an arrangement that costs the grove two adults' labour and is never waived.
why.pressures: The two-tender rule is a direct reaction to what exclusive communion did at Lilmoth. The two-tender rule is a direct reaction to what exclusive communion did at Lilmoth, and the minder here trained under someone who was there.
why.wouldChangeIf: A minder who listened alone would be removed. A minder who listened alone would be removed, and the removal would be the district's business within a day — which is the rule's real enforcement.

places.hook: Within sight and earshot of the tree at all times — the post requires it

places.name: Tsoko Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 272 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The delegation camp used during the convocation month and empty the rest of the year.
why.siteAdvantages: Four hundred metres from the convocation ground, on its landings.
why.occupantsMotive: Delegations, in season. Delegations, in season, each of whom brings its own cook, its own water and its own account of why its pitch is where it is.
why.pressures: Precedence disputes about pitch positions are an annual institution. Precedence disputes about pitch positions are an annual institution, and the overflow the nine-trunks village rents has begun to outrank the camp's own back rows.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tribe losing its pitch is a real political event. A tribe losing its pitch is a real political event, and two pitches have gone unclaimed for three years without anyone agreeing to reallocate them.

places.hook: Four hundred metres from the convocation ground, on its landings

places.name: The Sap Road Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 147 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A camp for those walking to a hero Hist to grieve.
why.siteAdvantages: The last water before the grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Mourners, in rotation, who mostly do not talk to each other. Mourners, in rotation, who mostly do not talk to each other, and who leave the camp stocked for the next arrivals as the only sociable act of the walk.
why.pressures: Predators have learned that this camp is quiet and slow. Predators have learned that this camp is quiet and slow, and the grove will not post a watch because a watched mourning is not a mourning.
why.wouldChangeIf: A killing here would close the road for a season. A killing here would close the road for a season, and the Agaceph grove would then have to receive its mourners by water, through landings it does not want used.

places.hook: The last water before the grove

places.name: The Counting Tower
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A ladder tower built to see over the canopy, because nothing else in the interior can.
why.siteAdvantages: The tallest hammock timber for kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: A watcher on rotation from the nearest village. A watcher on rotation from the nearest village, whose real job is to count smoke and boats and report both to the naheesh, not to admire the view.
why.pressures: The scour's finding made flesh — from the ground you can see nothing at all. The scour's finding made flesh — from the ground you can see nothing at all, so the tower's word is the district's only distant information and is trusted further than it should be.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tree died the region would lose its only sightline. If the tree died the region would lose its only sightline, and the vista ledge that would replace it is a day away and closing over.

places.hook: The tallest hammock timber for kilometres

places.name: The Tapping Camp
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 280 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Illicit sap-tappers working trees nobody watches.
why.siteAdvantages: Between three unattended wild Hist, on a creek that gets a boat out.
why.occupantsMotive: Tappers who sell to a city fence and know exactly what they are doing. Tappers who sell to a city fence and know exactly what they are doing, working only wild Hist so that no tribe has standing to complain.
why.pressures: The tree-minders have put a bounty on them. The tree-minders have put a bounty on them, and the bounty is paid in licence-renewal favour, which means the licensed stage's tappers are the ones hunting them.
why.wouldChangeIf: One arrest would name the fence and unroll the trade. One arrest would name the fence and unroll the trade, including the tapped-tree crew, who use the same buyer under a lapsed concession.

places.hook: Between three unattended wild Hist, on a creek that gets a boat out

places.name: The Poling Relay
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in firm lowland (danger band 3), 67 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A relay yard where interior porters hand off loads between poling stages.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the polable water ends and the walking route begins.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, and a yard-keeper who takes a cut of everything. Porters, and a yard-keeper who takes a cut of everything, holding the only covered store between the water and the walking route.
why.pressures: The yard-keeper's cut is the region's standing grievance. The yard-keeper's cut is the region's standing grievance, and the lizard-steed breeders have begun quoting prices that assume it, which makes them complicit.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second yard would break the monopoly. A second yard would break the monopoly, and the only firm ground for one belongs to the village that takes the keeper's rent.

places.hook: Where the polable water ends and the walking route begins

places.name: The Kept Refuge
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 581 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on remote, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A shelter maintained on ground everyone avoids, against the day the tribes have to run again — as they did in 4E 48.
why.siteAdvantages: High, dry, and deliberately remote, with one maintained approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Two caretakers on a rotation nobody envies. Two caretakers on a rotation nobody envies, drawn by lot from the tribes that fund it, for a year each, with no exemption accepted.
why.pressures: Stores are rotated and the register of the one time it was full is read aloud annually. Stores are rotated and the register of the one time it was full is read aloud annually, and the reading is now attended by fewer tribes each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its use would mean something terrible had happened again. Its use would mean something terrible had happened again — and the funding tribes have quietly let two shares lapse, which nobody has announced.

places.hook: High, dry, and deliberately remote, with one maintained approach

places.name: The Fallen Nine
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 194 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A trunk root that died and gave way.
why.siteAdvantages: It is on a route people still use, which is why they still dig at it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the bone-carriers come once a year. Nobody; the bone-carriers come once a year, because four families' dead are under the fall and cannot be recovered to be returned.
why.pressures: The route now goes the long way and costs a day. The route now goes the long way and costs a day, which the porter relay charges for and therefore has no interest in seeing fixed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would restore the route and settle four families' claims. Clearing it would restore the route and settle four families' claims, and would cost the relay yard a quarter of its traffic.

places.hook: It is on a route people still use, which is why they still dig at it

places.name: The Severed Branch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 652 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, remote, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A gallery taken by a cult cell because the roots here reach a tree they intend to sever.
why.siteAdvantages: Isolated, deep, and directly connected to their target.
why.occupantsMotive: Cultists testing a method. Cultists testing a method, working from notes that came out of the staging camp and going back to it with results.
why.pressures: The tree above is beginning to withdraw and the village does not know why. The tree above is beginning to withdraw and the village does not know why, and has begun consulting a tree-minder who will recognise the pattern.
why.wouldChangeIf: Discovery would move them and cost the player the evidence. Discovery would move them and cost the player the evidence — the notes are the only written account of how a severing is actually attempted.

places.hook: Isolated, deep, and directly connected to their target

places.name: The Long Throat
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 219 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on landform, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.fenlord-tomb-deep (+0.74).

why.founding: A single enormous trunk root running toward the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: It is the only dry route toward the deep basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; a guide camp sits at each end. Nobody; a guide camp sits at each end, and the two camps keep a tally of who went in so that the far end knows who to expect.
why.pressures: Anything that enters behind you cannot be passed. Anything that enters behind you cannot be passed, so the guides move parties through in one direction only and wait out the day if the tally is wrong.
why.wouldChangeIf: A branch collapse would make it a trap rather than a route. A branch collapse would make it a trap rather than a route, and would cut the only dry approach to the basin's deep ground.

places.hook: It is the only dry route toward the deep basin

places.name: The Drowned Stair
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 539 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, remote, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.urn-vault-blasphemers (+0.72).

why.founding: A root branch that grew downhill into the water table.
why.siteAdvantages: It short-cuts a full day of surface travel for anyone who can hold their breath.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; divers pass through. Nobody lives here; divers pass through, mostly couriers, because a message that takes a day by surface takes an afternoon by holding your breath four times.
why.pressures: The water level rises in the wet season and drowns the last two landings. The water level rises in the wet season and drowns the last two landings, so half the year the shortcut is a full dive and the couriers charge double.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry decade would make it an ordinary road. A dry decade would make it an ordinary road and would end a courier trade three villages depend on for news.

places.hook: It short-cuts a full day of surface travel for anyone who can hold their breath

places.name: The Underway
places.whySiteWon: ravine in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 17 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The trunk root under Helstrom, opened and kept as a road because the surface route is band 5.
why.siteAdvantages: It goes where no boat can and no road will be built.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who maintain exactly as far as they are paid to. Waykeepers who maintain exactly as far as they are paid to, and who post the paid limit in cut marks so that nobody can claim not to have known.
why.pressures: Beyond the second junction it is not maintained and people still go. Beyond the second junction it is not maintained and people still go, and the Waykeepers have stopped recovering bodies past it, which the assembly has not been told.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers would close the interior's only overland link. Losing the Waykeepers would close the interior's only overland link, and Helstrom's escorted water traffic could not absorb the difference.

places.hook: It goes where no boat can and no road will be built

places.name: Lantern Hollow
