why.founding: Root gallery taken over by growers who needed dark, damp and constant temperature.
why.siteAdvantages: The root layer provides all three for free.
why.occupantsMotive: Growers who are underground by preference and rarely surface. Growers who are underground by preference and rarely surface, selling glowing fungus to every village in the district through a single agent.
why.pressures: Something else uses the deeper branches and they have stopped going there. Something else uses the deeper branches and they have stopped going there, which has cut their best beds out of production and put the price up.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would end the interior's light supply. A collapse would end the interior's light supply, in a region where the nightbound village is the only settlement that would not notice.

places.hook: The root layer provides all three for free

places.name: The Root Talk Ground

why.siteAdvantages: A rare enclosed clearing at the grove's edge, large enough for every interior delegation and their landings.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody, eleven months in twelve; the naheesh and tree-minders of the interior in the twelfth. Nobody, eleven months in twelve; the naheesh and tree-minders of the interior in the twelfth, seated by a precedence order kept at Helstrom.
why.pressures: Attendance is falling and the empty places are counted publicly. Attendance is falling and the empty places are counted publicly, and the two tribes that stopped coming have not been asked why in six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A convocation that failed to reach alignment would end the institution. A convocation that failed to reach alignment would end the institution, and both the Hist-less refuge and the heretic builders are waiting for exactly that.

places.hook: A rare enclosed clearing at the grove's edge, large enough for every interior delegation and their landings

places.name: The Emptied Bore
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 5 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.drawdown-flat-exposed (+1.22).

why.founding: A rootworm bore abandoned when the worm died in it.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry, wide, straight tunnel — extremely rare shelter.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever is currently living in a free tunnel. Whatever is currently living in a free tunnel, which changes every season and is the reason no village has claimed it.
why.pressures: Everyone who passes wants to use it and something is always already in it. Everyone who passes wants to use it and something is always already in it, so the bore has killed more travellers than the weather it shelters from.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would give the region its only dry way-shelter. Clearing it would give the region its only dry way-shelter, and the guides have costed the work twice and cannot agree who would own it afterwards.

places.hook: A dry, wide, straight tunnel — extremely rare shelter

places.name: The Working Burrow
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 167 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A wild rootworm's burrow off a trunk root, which the Waykeepers watch because a wild worm can open or close a line.
why.siteAdvantages: Where soft ground meets the root layer and the worm can turn.
why.occupantsMotive: A rootworm and the small scavenger population that lives off its spoil. A rootworm and the small scavenger population that lives off its spoil — an ecology the Waykeepers can read well enough to predict where the worm will turn.
why.pressures: The Waykeepers want it moved; the local tribe considers it sacred. The Waykeepers want it moved; the local tribe considers it sacred, and the dispute has been at the convocation twice without a ruling.
why.wouldChangeIf: Driving it off would open a shorter root line and start an argument. Driving it off would open a shorter root line and start an argument that would reach Helstrom within a month.

places.hook: Where soft ground meets the root layer and the worm can turn

places.name: The Helstrom Line-Head
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 5), 51 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The interior terminus of the rootworm network, re-authored from the Pass-1 placeholder.
why.siteAdvantages: At the Helstrom gate, where the trunk roots converge.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who run a semi-public service and a restricted one. Waykeepers who run a semi-public service and a restricted one, and who will not confirm to a paying passenger that the restricted network exists.
why.pressures: The restricted network is a faction reward and is guarded as one. The restricted network is a faction reward and is guarded as one, and the interior's tribes have begun resenting a transit system they cannot audit.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers' cooperation closes the interior. Losing the Waykeepers' cooperation closes the interior, which is the single largest piece of leverage any faction holds in this region.

places.hook: At the Helstrom gate, where the trunk roots converge

places.name: The Bleeding House
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 323 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-lantern-hollow (+0.29).

why.founding: A Daedric-worked facility built to harvest a Hist industrially — the Haj Uxith pattern, in the interior.
why.siteAdvantages: Sited on a tree, not on ground: the building is a machine wrapped around a trunk.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever the bargain left behind. Whatever the bargain left behind, still working the machine on a schedule, in a building nobody has authorised anyone to enter for six hundred years.
why.pressures: The tree is still alive and still connected, and its anguish is felt down the root line. The tree is still alive and still connected, and its anguish is felt down the root line — the Agaceph sap-speaker can name the direction and will not.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending it is one of the interior's great deeds. Ending it is one of the interior's great deeds, and would be the first thing in a century that the convocation could agree to reward.

places.hook: Sited on a tree, not on ground: the building is a machine wrapped around a trunk

places.name: The Licensed Stage

why.founding: Licensed tapping done to the tree-minders' rule: one stage, one season, one tree.
why.siteAdvantages: On a tree the assembly designated for it.
why.occupantsMotive: Tappers whose licence is their livelihood and who police poachers themselves. Tappers whose licence is their livelihood and who police poachers themselves, because an unpoliced district loses its licences entirely.
why.pressures: The licence is renewed annually and someone always objects. The licence is renewed annually and someone always objects, most reliably the tribe whose tree carried the stage the previous year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A licence lost would be worth violence. A licence lost would be worth violence, and the last holder to lose one is now selling to the same city fence the poachers use.

places.hook: On a tree the assembly designated for it

places.name: Miredance
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 459 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that took the sap sacrament far past the customary dose and never came back.

why.occupantsMotive: People in permanent low communion who work, trade and speak a beat behind everyone else. People in permanent low communion who work, trade and speak a beat behind everyone else, and who are unusually good at hearing a tree that is unwell.
why.pressures: Their neighbours consider them ruined; their tree does not. Their neighbours consider them ruined; their tree does not, and the tree-minders quietly consult them about the first-rain trunk's decline.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the overflow would sober the village and probably kill several of them. Cutting the overflow would sober the village and probably kill several of them, and would remove the province's only standing example of what overdose looks like.

places.hook: Beside a hero Hist's overflow pool, where sap is free and continuous

places.name: Xal-Ussep
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 445 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-lantern-hollow (+1.46).

why.founding: A xanmeer sealed with its tribe's Hist inside it, alone since the Duskfall.
why.siteAdvantages: A summit site defensible enough that it was never opened.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living but the tree, which is the point. Nothing living but the tree, which is the point: a Hist that has not touched the collective since the Duskfall, and may not know it has ended.
why.pressures: A whole tribe watches it and has never been inside. A whole tribe watches it and has never been inside, and the wardens' post is now the only thing holding that tribe together.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening it releases — or kills — a Hist that has been isolated for an age. Opening it releases — or kills — a Hist that has been isolated for an age, which is the closest thing the province has to a controlled test of the main quest's premise.

places.hook: A summit site defensible enough that it was never opened

places.name: The Coiling Reach
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 773 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A reach where the big snakes den in the root banks.
why.siteAdvantages: Warm root banks above the flood line — ideal denning.
why.occupantsMotive: Snakes, and the hunters who take them for hide. Snakes, and the hunters who take them for hide, working to a season set by the daril fermentary rather than by the snakes.
why.pressures: The hide is worth enough that hunters keep coming and keep dying. The hide is worth enough that hunters keep coming and keep dying, and the fermentary buys venom from the same reach, so a bad year hits both trades at once.
why.wouldChangeIf: Overhunting would clear it in a decade. Overhunting would clear it in a decade, and the fermentary has already begun keeping its own stock against that day.

places.hook: Warm root banks above the flood line — ideal denning

places.name: The Swallow
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 613 m from the nearest route; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: One of the province's very few true sinkholes, in the only ground firm enough to hold a rim.
why.siteAdvantages: A rare karst pocket the hydrology has not flooded away.
why.occupantsMotive: Something that hunts by dropping. Something that hunts by dropping, which is why the rim is fenced and why the fence is on the outside rather than the inside.
why.pressures: The tribes fence the rim and the fence is broken every year. The tribes fence the rim and the fence is broken every year, always from within, which is the detail the tribes do not include when they explain the fence.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would open it into the root layer below. A collapse would open it into the root layer below, and the Waykeepers' second junction is directly beneath it.

hardConstraints: sinkhole landform (11 province-wide — budgeted: 1 in this zone)
places.hook: A rare karst pocket the hydrology has not flooded away

places.name: Sleeps-In-The-Ring

why.founding: The tribe stayed after their tree went to sleep, because leaving would have been abandoning it.
why.siteAdvantages: A pond-ringed rise the tree chose, which is also defensible.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe in a generations-long interregnum, running its own affairs without communion. A tribe in a generations-long interregnum, running its own affairs without communion, and doing it well enough that the neighbours have stopped offering help.
why.pressures: No hatching, no naming, no soul-return; their young leave for Hissmir and mostly do not come back. No hatching, no naming, no soul-return; their young leave for Hissmir and mostly do not come back, and the village's median age is the highest in the district.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tree woke, the village would double in a decade. If the tree woke, the village would double in a decade — and the bereaved village that lost its tree entirely watches them for exactly that reason.

places.hook: A pond-ringed rise the tree chose, which is also defensible

places.name: The Hollow House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 265 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: One household living in a xanmeer antechamber because it was empty and dry.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry stone floor above the flood in a region where dry floors are the scarce good.
why.occupantsMotive: A family with no tribe and no intention of explaining themselves. A family with no tribe and no intention of explaining themselves, who trade at the walkway junction and have never been to the village that tends the ruin.
why.pressures: The tribe that tends the xanmeer knows and has not decided what to do. The tribe that tends the xanmeer knows and has not decided what to do, chiefly because evicting them would require admitting the antechamber was habitable.
why.wouldChangeIf: A decision either way ends the arrangement. A decision either way ends the arrangement, and a ruling that squatting is trespass would apply equally to the fort-dwelling tribe two days east.

places.hook: Dry stone floor above the flood in a region where dry floors are the scarce good

places.name: The Standing Thing
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 343 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Nobody knows what it is or who made it, and the local tribes have four incompatible stories.
why.siteAdvantages: It is where it is; the forest has grown around it without touching it.
why.occupantsMotive: None. None — the four stories each name a different custodian, and none of the four tribes has ever posted one.
why.pressures: Two of the four stories are politically useful and are being pushed. Two of the four stories are politically useful and are being pushed: one makes it Ayleid, which would open a dig, and one makes it pre-Duskfall Argonian, which would close one forever.
why.wouldChangeIf: An authoritative answer would disappoint everyone. An authoritative answer would disappoint everyone, and the Helstrom assembly has declined to hear the question three times.

places.hook: It is where it is; the forest has grown around it without touching it

places.name: Two-Poles
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A hamlet-turned-village on a shallow flat that floods to the floor twice a year and is rebuilt each time.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow flat with good fishing and no competition.
why.occupantsMotive: Families who have decided the rebuild is cheaper than moving. Families who have decided the rebuild is cheaper than moving, and who have made the rebuild a rite, done in three days with the whole village present.
why.pressures: The floods are getting deeper and the piles are getting longer. The floods are getting deeper and the piles are getting longer, and the timber now comes from the hammock village, which charges for it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Two bad years running would end it. Two bad years running would end it, and the households have not agreed where they would go, because the only firm ground nearby is a rise already fully occupied.

places.hook: Shallow flat with good fishing and no competition

places.name: Ux-Aneet
places.whySiteWon: cove in interior swamp (danger band 4), 11 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A working village on the channel that carries Helstrom's traffic.
why.siteAdvantages: Channel edge with a bed firm enough to pile and a bank high enough to land on.
why.occupantsMotive: Polers and provisioners who live off passing convoys. Polers and provisioners who live off passing convoys, on margins set by Helstrom's escort schedule rather than by anything they control.
why.pressures: The convoys are escorted and do not always stop. The convoys are escorted and do not always stop, and the escorts prefer Greenspring, which has cleaner water and a tribe that flatters them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A change in the escorted route would empty it in two years. A change in the escorted route would empty it in two years, and the village has begun courting the pilgrim traffic as a hedge.

places.hook: Channel edge with a bed firm enough to pile and a bank high enough to land on

places.name: The Tsoko Stones
places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 3), 685 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The reckoning by which the interior knows when Hist-Tsoko has come and the convocation is called.
why.siteAdvantages: A clearing with a sightline to the one gap in the canopy that admits the relevant light.
why.occupantsMotive: Readers appointed by the assembly at Helstrom. Readers appointed by the assembly at Helstrom, two of them, who must agree — a rule added after a single reader's error moved a convocation by a month.
why.pressures: The canopy has grown and the sightline is closing; the reading is being disputed. The canopy has grown and the sightline is closing; the reading is being disputed, and the tribes that dispute it are the ones that would rather not attend.
why.wouldChangeIf: A failed reading would postpone the convocation, which has political consequences. A failed reading would postpone the convocation, which has political consequences — and cutting the canopy to save the sightline is itself a contested act.

places.hook: A clearing with a sightline to the one gap in the canopy that admits the relevant light

places.name: The Topmost Chamber
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 488 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, submerged, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.air-pocket-station-basin (+0.62).

why.founding: A xanmeer that subsided into a lake, leaving one chamber above water.
why.siteAdvantages: It sank straight down; the top terrace is a dry island.
why.occupantsMotive: Divers who work it and a lake that does not want them to. Divers who work it and a lake that does not want them to, financed on shares by the living treasure-hunters' outfit a day away.
why.pressures: Everything below the first chamber needs breath and light. Everything below the first chamber needs breath and light, and the outfit has lost two divers rather than admit the second chamber is beyond them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drawdown year would open two more chambers and a rush to loot them. A drawdown year would open two more chambers and a rush to loot them, which the pilgrim-tended terrace's rota would have no standing to stop.

places.hook: It sank straight down; the top terrace is a dry island

places.name: Xal-Irasotl
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 461 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.duskfall-unmade-site (+1.29).

why.founding: The xanmeer of the tribe that still lives beside it, maintained as a monument since the Duskfall.
why.siteAdvantages: On the tribe's own ground, which is why it survived.
why.occupantsMotive: Tenders who sweep it, repair it, and will not let anyone loot it. Tenders who sweep it, repair it, and will not let anyone loot it, on a duty roster that is the tribe's oldest continuous institution.
why.pressures: Treasure hunters do not accept that maintenance means ownership. Treasure hunters do not accept that maintenance means ownership, and the living outfit nearby has twice offered the tribe a share to look away.
why.wouldChangeIf: A generation that stopped tending would turn it into a dungeon. A generation that stopped tending would turn it into a dungeon, which is what happened to the subsumed meer and is why the roster is enforced.

places.hook: On the tribe's own ground, which is why it survived

places.name: The Swept Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 368 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, route, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.burn-scar-village-ash (+0.91).

why.founding: A xanmeer with no surviving tribe, kept by the pilgrims who pass it on the way to Helstrom.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the pilgrim route — the reason it is tended at all.
why.occupantsMotive: No owner; a rota kept by strangers who will never meet each other. No owner; a rota kept by strangers who will never meet each other, each doing a half-day's work because the last one did.
why.pressures: The rota is slipping and the lower terraces are going back to the marsh. The rota is slipping and the lower terraces are going back to the marsh, in step with the falling pilgrim traffic the sap road camp also reports.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tribe claiming it would end the arrangement and probably improve the building. A tribe claiming it would end the arrangement and probably improve the building, and no tribe will claim it because the claim implies the dead here are theirs.

places.hook: Directly on the pilgrim route — the reason it is tended at all

places.name: The Last Camp
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 229 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An expedition camp whose expedition did not return from the xanmeer it was working.
why.siteAdvantages: Three hundred metres from a sealed xanmeer, on the only dry ground. Three hundred metres from a sealed xanmeer, on the only dry ground — which is why the second expedition will camp here too.
why.occupantsMotive: The dead, and their notes.
why.pressures: Their notes are accurate up to the point where they stop. Their notes are accurate up to the point where they stop, and the living outfit has been trying to buy them from whoever brings them out.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second expedition using the notes would get further. A second expedition using the notes would get further, which is exactly what the notes' last page warns against in the writer's own hand.

places.hook: Three hundred metres from a sealed xanmeer, on the only dry ground

places.name: Fortune's Own
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 230 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A working treasure-hunting outfit with a licence from nobody.
why.siteAdvantages: Central to three unopened sites, on a channel they can get a boat out on.
why.occupantsMotive: Hunters who will hire, trade, cheat, or race the player depending on the day. Hunters who will hire, trade, cheat, or race the player depending on the day, financed from the coast and answerable to nobody in the interior.
why.pressures: The tended-xanmeer tribes consider them criminals and are correct. The tended-xanmeer tribes consider them criminals and are correct, and the outfit's response has been to work drowned sites, where no tribe has a tender.
why.wouldChangeIf: A big find would break the outfit up in an argument. A big find would break the outfit up in an argument, and two of the six already have a buyer of their own on the coast.

places.hook: Central to three unopened sites, on a channel they can get a boat out on

places.name: Nothing-Left
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 524 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.barsaebic-sub-city (+0.79).

why.founding: A village under Umbriel's track in 4E 48; everything organic was taken and the buildings were not.
why.siteAdvantages: It stood where it stood; the shadow decided the rest.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The dead did not stay. Nobody. The dead did not stay — which distinguishes it from the walking village in the deep swamp and is the whole of the local theology about why.
why.pressures: The neighbouring villages will not use the ground or the timber. The neighbouring villages will not use the ground or the timber, and the timber is good, seasoned and standing, which makes the refusal expensive and deliberate.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing will be built here again. Nothing will be built here again — though the heretic builders have asked about the stone footings, and were refused by four tribes at once.

places.hook: It stood where it stood; the shadow decided the rest

places.name: Umpholo
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 4), 499 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Maran mission whose priests died of swamp rot within a month of arriving; the last book was gone by 3E 399.
why.siteAdvantages: Built on the only stone outcrop the missionaries could find, which is why the shell survives.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody, for two centuries. Nobody, for two centuries — the interior tribes will not use the outcrop, on the grounds that stone that killed foreigners will kill anyone.
why.pressures: The marsh is eating it at a measurable rate. The marsh is eating it at a measurable rate, and antiquarians from Gideon have begun asking for the last book, which left in 3E 399 and has not been traced.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing; it is a monument to a category of mistake. Nothing; it is a monument to a category of mistake — and it is also the only stone building in the district nobody claims, which the squatters have noticed.

places.hook: Built on the only stone outcrop the missionaries could find, which is why the shell survives

places.name: The Shut Vault
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 325 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-drowned-stair (+0.72).

why.founding: A vault for the dead who may not be staked: heretics, the Hist-less, and one whole tribe.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry stone, sealed, well away from any village.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who holds the register and not the key. A keeper who holds the register and not the key, an arrangement designed so that no single person can be pressured into opening it.
why.pressures: Families want their dead moved out; the register says no. Families want their dead moved out; the register says no, and the register's authority rests on an assembly ruling nobody can now produce.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling on the register would empty half of it. A ruling on the register would empty half of it, and the Hist-less refuge has offered to receive everyone the register denies — which would make the refuge a burial authority.

places.hook: Dry stone, sealed, well away from any village

places.name: The Break
places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 4), 379 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, sightline, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A blowdown from an old storm left one ledge with a view over the canopy.
why.siteAdvantages: The single highest exposed point in the district.
why.occupantsMotive: None; guides bring clients here to orient. None; guides bring clients here to orient, and charge for it, because in this region a bearing is a purchasable good.
why.pressures: The forest is closing the gap and the view has ten years left. The forest is closing the gap and the view has ten years left, and the guides have started arguing about whether cutting to keep it open is theirs to do.
why.wouldChangeIf: When it closes, the district loses its only orientation point. When it closes, the district loses its only orientation point apart from the counting tower, which belongs to a village and is not for hire.

places.hook: The single highest exposed point in the district

places.name: The Sealed Cistern
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 477 m from the nearest route; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.burn-scar-village-ash (+1.26).

why.founding: A xanmeer cistern sealed on purpose with what was in it still inside.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the water table, in stone that has held.
why.occupantsMotive: A voriplasm, and the seal. A voriplasm, and the seal, which was cut by people who expected to be understood and were not.
why.pressures: The seal is stone and stone lasts; the warnings on it have outlasted the language. The seal is stone and stone lasts; the warnings on it have outlasted the language, so the only people who can read them are the antiquarians most likely to break it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Breaking the seal is a choice the world does not force. Breaking the seal is a choice the world does not force — and the breached cistern in the deep swamp is what the other choice looks like twelve years on.

places.hook: Below the water table, in stone that has held

places.name: Still-Waiting
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 285 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: In 4E 48 these families did exactly what the An-Xileel told them to do and withdrew into the interior to wait for the cleansed province they were promised. Nobody has ever told them it is not coming.
why.siteAdvantages: An enclosed clearing on the Umbriel corridor, above flood, chosen in a hurry by people who expected to be there for a season.
why.occupantsMotive: The devout and the stuck, in the same village and no longer sure which they are; the vigil has been kept without a break for a hundred and fifty years.
why.pressures: The purification ground is swept daily and the houses are not; the neighbours find them embarrassing and trade with them anyway.
why.wouldChangeIf: An An-Xileel officer saying the words out loud would end it in an afternoon, which is precisely why none has ever visited.

hardConstraints: ground defensible enough to have been chosen in a panic
places.hook: An enclosed clearing on the Umbriel corridor, above flood, chosen in a hurry by people who expected to be there for a season

places.name: High Crossing
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Four walkway routes forced to meet above ground that floods to chest height.
why.siteAdvantages: The only place the four alignments can share a footing.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who collects for maintenance and sells rope. A keeper who collects for maintenance and sells rope, and who is the only person in the district who knows the true condition of all four arms.
why.pressures: Everyone uses it and nobody wants to pay for it. Everyone uses it and nobody wants to pay for it, and the branching village a day away has the same problem and has started coordinating rates.
why.wouldChangeIf: One arm failing reroutes an entire tribe's traffic. One arm failing reroutes an entire tribe's traffic, most likely the Paatru's, who have no alternative that does not cross their own mire.

places.hook: The only place the four alignments can share a footing

places.name: The Charged Pond
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 286 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.rootworm-burrow-dead (+1.52).

why.founding: A wamasu nesting pond, avoided by everything including the tribes.
why.siteAdvantages: Still, deep, isolated water — nesting conditions.
why.occupantsMotive: A breeding pair and a season's eggs. A breeding pair and a season's eggs, which the coastal egg trade would pay a fortune for and which no interior guide will lead anyone to.
why.pressures: The water is lethal to swim while they are in it, and the route past has to go round. The water is lethal to swim while they are in it, and the route past has to go round, through the marsh giant's expanding range.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it opens a two-hour shortcut and ends a species' nest site. Clearing it opens a two-hour shortcut and ends a species' nest site, and the offering-shrine keepers hold that the flood-staying rite depends on the pair being there.

places.hook: Still, deep, isolated water — nesting conditions

places.name: The Root Fall
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 396 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A spring bursting out of the root layer and falling into a chamber behind the curtain.
why.siteAdvantages: The one place in the region with real vertical relief.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever wants a dry room behind water. Whatever wants a dry room behind water, which in this district has meant, at various times, a cult cell, a smuggler and something nobody has named.
why.pressures: Everyone local knows there is a chamber; not everyone comes back from it. Everyone local knows there is a chamber; not everyone comes back from it, and the village downstream has stopped counting the ones who do not.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry season halves the curtain and exposes the entrance. A dry season halves the curtain and exposes the entrance, which would make the chamber worthless to anyone who wanted it hidden.

places.hook: The one place in the region with real vertical relief

places.name: The Panther Race
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 330 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where the Panther fork drops through a root-choked reach.
why.siteAdvantages: The only fast water in a province of still water.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives in it; a portage crew works beside it. Nothing lives in it; a portage crew works beside it, charging by the hull and running the only registered salvage claim on the reach.
why.pressures: Boats are lost here regularly and the crew profits from it. Boats are lost here regularly and the crew profits from it, and Greenspring downstream receives the wreckage and the survivors and resents both.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cleared channel would end the portage trade. A cleared channel would end the portage trade and would put laden craft within a day of Helstrom's approach, which the escort service has costed and likes.

places.hook: The only fast water in a province of still water

places.name: The Turned Tree
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 691 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A wild Hist with no tribe that went wrong on its own, in ground nobody kept.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep basin, no route, no neighbours to notice for decades.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody speaks for it; the nearest villages maintain a totem line and stay outside it. Nobody speaks for it; the nearest villages maintain a totem line and stay outside it, re-cutting the line outward each year as the ring widens.
why.pressures: It is spreading — the flowering ring is wider each year. It is spreading — the flowering ring is wider each year, and the rate has been recorded by the counting tower's watchers for three generations.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tribe adopting it would either be destroyed or would be the strangest tribe in Argonia. A tribe adopting it would either be destroyed or would be the strangest tribe in Argonia, and the Hist-less refuge has debated exactly that twice.

places.hook: Deep basin, no route, no neighbours to notice for decades

places.name: The Sleeper Under Ash
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 495 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Hist that isolated itself and slept rather than join the collective after the Duskfall.
why.siteAdvantages: A burn scar that never regrew, so the tree stands alone in open ground — rare in the interior.
why.occupantsMotive: None. Pilgrims come to sit, not to speak. None. Pilgrims come to sit, not to speak, and the sitting has become a recognised alternative for anyone refused audience at a hero grove.
why.pressures: Sap-tappers know it cannot object. Sap-tappers know it cannot object, and the poacher camp works it in preference to any tree with a tribe, which the tree-minders know and cannot prove.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it woke, three villages would have to renegotiate who they belong to. If it woke, three villages would have to renegotiate who they belong to, and two of them are currently paying the Agaceph grove for standing they would no longer need.

places.hook: A burn scar that never regrew, so the tree stands alone in open ground — rare in the interior

places.name: The Guide-Lights
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A stretch of basin where the lights lead travellers off the route.
why.siteAdvantages: Between two safe rises, on the only line anyone would walk.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever the lights are. Whatever the lights are, they keep to a line between two safe rises, which is either the cleverest thing in the basin or a coincidence nobody can test.
why.pressures: Guides tell clients the lights are real and to ignore them, and clients follow them anyway. Guides tell clients the lights are real and to ignore them, and clients follow them anyway; the far shelter's stock is what the survivors reach.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. Nothing — and the guides price the crossing on the assumption that one client in twenty will walk off the line regardless of what they were told.

places.hook: Between two safe rises, on the only line anyone would walk

places.name: The Made Ground
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 396 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: Xal-Krona are Argonian behemoths grown by the Hist through sap, 'often created for a reason'. This is the basin where the reason was the Accord — a sap-flooded hollow in the deep interior where the Hist made the Last Warden, and, on the evidence lying in it, did not get it right first time.
why.siteAdvantages: A closed basin fed by deep roots, where sap collects instead of draining — the one place in the interior where a tree could pool enough of itself to make something that size.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. The Warden itself has not been here in an age; it waits in the Lost City, which is what it was made to do. What is here is what was made before it.
why.pressures: The basin still fills each wet season, and what it grows now is smaller, wrong, and short-lived; the Unbound Root have found the place and read it as a recipe.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the consent conditions the Warden was made to test are understood here first, the Lost City confrontation can be resolved by standing down rather than by fighting.

places.hook: A closed basin fed by deep roots, where sap collects instead of draining — the one place in the interior where a tree could pool enough of itself to make something that size

places.name: The Meeruth Station
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 56 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Imperial-era river station on the last navigable reach of the Helstrom approach, abandoned when the concession lapsed.
why.siteAdvantages: A stone quay, a walled yard and a magazine on firm ground — everything a base needs and nothing the marsh can rot.
why.occupantsMotive: Squatters who leave when anyone with a claim arrives. Squatters who leave when anyone with a claim arrives, and who have kept the magazine dry for twenty years without ever being thanked for it.
why.pressures: Both the interior tribes and the Veiled Reed would rather it stayed nobody's. Both the interior tribes and the Veiled Reed would rather it stayed nobody's, because a held station on this reach controls the Helstrom approach outright.
why.wouldChangeIf: A claimant with standing could hold it — which is exactly what quests 30 §24b.5 reserves it for. A claimant with standing could hold it — which is exactly what quests 30 §24b.5 reserves it for, and which would put a fortified quay between Helstrom and the coast.

places.hook: A stone quay, a walled yard and a magazine on firm ground — everything a base needs and nothing the marsh can rot

places.name: Xal-Thuun
places.whySiteWon: summit in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 209 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribe that moved into its ancestors' xanmeer during the Imperial century and never moved out.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls and working vakka mechanisms — the strongest fortification in the interior.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe living in a monument they are technically supposed only to maintain. A tribe living in a monument they are technically supposed only to maintain, and who describe the residence as continuous tending to anyone who asks.
why.pressures: Their neighbours consider inhabiting it close to the stone heresy; the mechanisms still kill people. Their neighbours consider inhabiting it close to the stone heresy; the mechanisms still kill people, mostly their own young, which they do not report.
why.wouldChangeIf: A mechanism failure would open the strongest position in the region to anyone. A mechanism failure would open the strongest position in the region to anyone, and the vakka stones that drive it are the largest cache in the interior.

places.hook: Stone walls and working vakka mechanisms — the strongest fortification in the interior

places.name: Ashen Tower
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 298 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, sightline, region.

why.founding: An Imperial signal tower on the rim, built to talk to Fort Swampmoth by fire and kept lit by the people who now hold neither.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge end with a line to the fort and a line down the road — the only point that has both.
why.occupantsMotive: The two watchers are paid in food by four villages who want warning of raids, not of armies.
why.pressures: The fire code they use was written for legions and now means things it did not mean.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the day the villages decided the Sul-Xan were finished.

places.hook: A ridge end with a line to the fort and a line down the road — the only point that has both

places.name: Bog Iron Workings
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 399 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on hinterland, parent, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-drowned-mule (+0.56).

why.founding: Bog iron forms itself in this ground, and a road that eats iron will pay for it.
why.siteAdvantages: A stagnant iron-rich seep where the ore can be lifted from the mud in cakes.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers are seasonal, come from three villages, and consider the work slightly shameful.
why.pressures: The seep is being worked out; each season's cakes are smaller and further from the path.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned without ceremony, and the province would think better of itself for it.

places.hook: A stagnant iron-rich seep where the ore can be lifted from the mud in cakes

places.name: Bonded Shed
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 70 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.hollow-arch-toll (+0.26).

why.founding: Goods that have been declared but not yet taxed have to sit somewhere lockable, and Gideon's court is the only body that can hold them lawfully.
why.siteAdvantages: On the river landing directly below the city, so a cart can be sealed at the wharf and opened in court.
why.occupantsMotive: The bond-keeper's authority comes from the courthouse and nowhere else, which he mentions often.
why.pressures: Half the bond is Cyrodilic Collections crates and half is what the antiquities fences shipped instead; the labels do not always match.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be looted in a night if the courthouse ever stopped sitting.

places.hook: On the river landing directly below the city, so a cart can be sealed at the wharf and opened in court

places.name: Carries-Them-Home
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 12 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-counted-dead (+0.77).

why.founding: Bones travelling home need stages, and the western route is the longest carry in the province.
why.siteAdvantages: A day's carry from the counted dead and a day from the marsh edge — the spacing is the institution.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers house carriers and take custody of bones overnight, which is an office of enormous trust.
why.pressures: More bones come west than go east, and the imbalance is a political fact everyone notices.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be busier than the road itself if the Chainbreakers ever emptied White Rose.

hardConstraints: one day's carry from the next stage
places.hook: A day's carry from the counted dead and a day from the marsh edge — the spacing is the institution

places.name: Burnt Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 344 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-fig-poachers (+1.00).

why.founding: A village that returned to ground the Legion burned, because it was theirs and because the peat still smoulders and the smoulder keeps outsiders off.
why.siteAdvantages: The one patch inside the burn where the peat burned out completely and left mineral soil.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay to hold the claim; the smoke is a defence they did not have to build.
why.pressures: Sinkholes open without warning where the peat has burned out below; two houses have gone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate the day the underground fire reached their side of the scar — and it is moving.

places.hook: The one patch inside the burn where the peat burned out completely and left mineral soil

places.name: Cartwright's Cross
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 722 m from the nearest route; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.guar-holding-of-the-nine-bells (+0.50).

why.founding: A town grew where the Blackwood Road crosses the north track, because a crossroads is a place where money must stop.
why.siteAdvantages: Level firm ground with a spring, at the one crossing that cannot be bypassed without a day's detour.
why.occupantsMotive: Four families hold the four corners and split the crossing dues, an arrangement older than the courthouse.
why.pressures: Gideon claims the dues are unlawful and collects a tax on the town instead, which everyone finds cheaper than arguing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would decline sharply if the north track were ever bridged upstream.

hardConstraints: a road crossing that cannot be bypassed
places.hook: Level firm ground with a spring, at the one crossing that cannot be bypassed without a day's detour

places.name: Cassian's Holding
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: A Nibenese family took a land grant here five generations ago and, unusually, made it work.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry loam shoulder above the flood line, with the river close enough to lift water and far enough not to take the barn.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because the land is theirs on paper and, by now, in fact; the neighbours accept them and mock the paper.
why.pressures: The grant describes fields that are now river, and the family will not admit it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end in a generation if the heir marries out, which she intends to.

places.hook: A dry loam shoulder above the flood line, with the river close enough to lift water and far enough not to take the barn

places.name: Castle Giovesse
places.whySiteWon: summit in upland hills (danger band 3), 298 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, sightline.

why.founding: A Cyrodiilic ducal seat raised in arm's reach of Gideon's north gate, later used to hold an Empress.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry knoll above the flood line with a clear line to the city gate — the site was chosen to be looked at.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the caretaker families who once did left when the well went bad, and the city tells its children not to go.
why.pressures: Roots in the vaulting; the north range has already gone; treasure-hunters chip at the cell doors.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be reoccupied the moment anyone in Gideon wanted a stone house badly enough — which, post-Duskfall, nobody does.

hardConstraints: within sight of Gideon's north gate
places.hook: A dry knoll above the flood line with a clear line to the city gate — the site was chosen to be looked at

places.name: Claywater Station
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 52 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: A mixed village at the road's water point, where the Imperial well and the Argonian landing serve the same travellers.
why.siteAdvantages: A perennial spring beside a boat channel — the one place the road and the water actually touch on level terms.
why.occupantsMotive: Two communities share it because neither can hold the other's half.
why.pressures: The well is Imperial-built and failing, and repairing it in stone is a thing the Argonian half will not help with.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become one community or two villages within a generation; nobody knows which.

hardConstraints: a perennial spring on the road
places.hook: A perennial spring beside a boat channel — the one place the road and the water actually touch on level terms

places.name: Licensed Dig
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 76 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections refounded at Gideon and immediately needed something to dig, so it licensed the nearest Ayleid ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly below Twyllbek's terrace, on flat ground with cart access to the city.
why.occupantsMotive: The Collections dig to return things; the local hands dig for wages; the fences watch to see what is found.
why.pressures: The permit is Gideon's, the ground is nobody's, and the tribes who might object have not been asked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be shut down in a day if the council ever decided the fences paid better.

places.hook: Directly below Twyllbek's terrace, on flat ground with cart access to the city

places.name: Comes-Back-Slowly
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 269 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-shaking-house (+0.49).

why.founding: Sap does to Argonians what it does, and the fringe villages have nowhere to put someone coming off it; a former user built a house at the edge of the road network deliberately far enough from a tradehouse to make relapse a walk.
why.siteAdvantages: An hour's walk from the nearest place that sells anything, on good water, with a hill between it and the road so that nobody passing hears what goes on inside.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper has done it herself and takes nobody's money; the house runs on what the families of those inside can bring, which is usually food and occasionally nothing.
why.pressures: Two sap traders on the Gideon road consider the house a commercial threat and have said so; it has no protection beyond the fact that hurting it would be unforgivable.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close the day the keeper died, and there is no second keeper — which is the thing the whole fringe worries about and nobody discusses with her.

hardConstraints: an hour's walk from anywhere selling sap or drink
places.hook: An hour's walk from the nearest place that sells anything, on good water, with a hill between it and the road so that nobody passing hears what goes on inside

places.name: Dreams-In-Mud
places.whySiteWon: oxbow in upland hills (danger band 3), 365 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, route; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-cold-lights (+0.27).

why.founding: A wallow of warm clay in a screened hollow, with a hut beside it and a keeper who supplies the herbs — one of the province's rites for people who need an answer that talking cannot produce, and the fringe's only one within reach of the Imperial road.
why.siteAdvantages: A warm clay seep in a hollow ringed by fig, so the place is genuinely silent and genuinely dark for eleven hours in every twenty-four.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper takes no payment for the wallow and considerable payment for the herbs, and is candid about the distinction.
why.pressures: Nibenese visitors have started coming out from Gideon for it as a novelty, which the keeper allows and the neighbouring villages resent; two of the novelty visitors have not come out of the wallow the same as they went in.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be shut by the villages themselves if a Gideon citizen died here, and the keeper knows it and takes them anyway.

places.hook: A warm clay seep in a hollow ringed by fig, so the place is genuinely silent and genuinely dark for eleven hours in every twenty-four

places.name: Fenmarch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 82 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The westernmost Hist stands here, and a village stands where a Hist stands.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm hummock at the marsh's western limit, with the tree already ancient when the village came.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because the tree is here; the tree's westernmost position makes them the province's edge in the way that matters.
why.pressures: Gideon's disputed cutting came from this tree, and Fenmarch's opinion of that is unprintable.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not move. A Hist village is the one Argonian settlement that does not relocate.

places.hook: A firm hummock at the marsh's western limit, with the tree already ancient when the village came

places.name: Fig Market
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 641 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: The marsh's produce and the road's manufactures have to change hands somewhere neither side controls.
why.siteAdvantages: A landing on the last navigable reach with cart ground behind it — boat and cart meet at the same quay.
why.occupantsMotive: The town lives on the spread between the two, and its guild of brokers exists to keep the spread.
why.pressures: Gideon wants the market inside its walls and has tried twice; the brokers pay it not to try a third time.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into a village if the navigable reach silted a kilometre downstream.

hardConstraints: boat and cart access to one quay
places.hook: A landing on the last navigable reach with cart ground behind it — boat and cart meet at the same quay

places.name: Fort Greenditch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 203 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The second of the road forts, built to hold the marsh side of the frontier and emptied with the rest at the Oblivion Crisis.
why.siteAdvantages: A low spur over the marsh edge; good against an army, useless against water, which is what actually came.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody holds it: the ditch flooded, the ground floor with it, and the toll company judged it not worth the pumping.
why.pressures: Something has been using the gatehouse, and the villages have stopped cutting reed on that side.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be as valuable as Swampmoth if the ditch were ever drained — which is a two-season job and a quest.

places.hook: A low spur over the marsh edge; good against an army, useless against water, which is what actually came

places.name: Fort Swampmoth
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 626 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: Built by the Third Empire to hold the only land approach into the province; rumoured emptied when the Legions were recalled at the Oblivion Crisis.
why.siteAdvantages: Commands the Blackwood Road where it leaves the ridge for the flood plain — nothing wheeled passes without being seen.
why.occupantsMotive: The outfit that moved in two centuries ago charges for passage and calls it upkeep; it has a written claim and will show it to you.
why.pressures: Gideon's council would rather the tolls were theirs; the Marsh Charter's people regard a foreign fort held by toll-takers as an insult with a gate.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change hands entirely if the road moved, or if the council ever paid to garrison it properly.

places.hook: Commands the Blackwood Road where it leaves the ridge for the flood plain — nothing wheeled passes without being seen

places.name: Gideon
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'gideon' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Founded where the Blackwood Road out of Leyawiin crosses the one low saddle in the western border belt — the province's only land door.
why.siteAdvantages: A measured 46 m barrier gap flanked by 60–87 m ridges; firm lowland and drinkable spring water on the marsh side; the Onkobra's red clay downstream.
why.occupantsMotive: A civic council in the old Governor's Mansion keeps the courthouse and archive working because paper is the only authority anyone here still recognises, and because Leyawiin trade pays for it.
why.pressures: Monsoon closes the road for months; the archive's writs are honoured nowhere east of the Onkobra; Cyrodilic Collections and the antiquities fences fight over the same crates.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fail if the Blackwood Road silted permanently, or if the disputed Hist cutting in the city gardens took root and made Gideon an Argonian city rather than a filing cabinet.

hardConstraints: river landing for the Onkobra trade
places.hook: A measured 46 m barrier gap flanked by 60–87 m ridges; firm lowland and drinkable spring water on the marsh side; the Onkobra's red clay downstream

places.name: Wintertide Stop
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 233 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on bound, landform, region.

why.founding: The rootworms migrate south to Gideon in wintertide and not otherwise; the stop exists only while they are here.
why.siteAdvantages: A root-layer breach in the clay bank outside the city where the worms surface — marked by red clay because red clay is what is to hand.
why.occupantsMotive: The waykeepers keep the marks and the etiquette; Gideon's carters keep the freight rates.
why.pressures: It is a season, not a service: the quest plan forbids any year-round Gideon root transit, and Gideon's council keeps trying to make it one.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end for good if the potters cut the bank back past the breach.

places.hook: A root-layer breach in the clay bank outside the city where the worms surface — marked by red clay because red clay is what is to hand

places.name: Reckoning House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 17 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, bound.

why.founding: The Synod inherited the Mages Guild's ambitions and sent an outstation to the one city with an archive it could read.
why.siteAdvantages: Inside Gideon's reach but outside its walls, on ground the council leased cheaply to keep them at arm's length.
why.occupantsMotive: They are here to inventory and, quietly, to acquire; the province is a collection to them.
why.pressures: The Whispers house across the marsh is here for the same reason and they do not speak.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be recalled the moment Cyrodiil decided the province was not worth the stipend.

hardConstraints: within a day of a functioning archive
places.hook: Inside Gideon's reach but outside its walls, on ground the council leased cheaply to keep them at arm's length

places.name: Giovesse Lines
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 211 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, sightline.

why.founding: Somebody besieged Castle Giovesse — the fortress that held Empress Tavia — and the banks, ditches and battery positions they cut are still exactly the shape they were, because earth in this province holds its shape far better than stone does.
why.siteAdvantages: The only firm ground within bowshot of the castle's landward face; whoever cut the lines had no choice about where, which is why the works are so legible.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies the lines but scrub and, in the dry months, a herd that shelters in the ditches.
why.pressures: The fringe's farmers have been quarrying the banks for road metal for two centuries and the profile is going; Gideon's records court has an opinion about this and no means of enforcing it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a field within a lifetime at the current rate of quarrying, and the only surviving evidence of the siege would be in the archive.

hardConstraints: firm ground within bowshot of Castle Giovesse
places.hook: The only firm ground within bowshot of the castle's landward face; whoever cut the lines had no choice about where, which is why the works are so legible

places.name: Glenbridge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1064 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Pilgrims from all over Tamriel come to hear the Nisswo read a ruined Sithis xanmeer's decay as the god's sermon; a town grew to feed them.
why.siteAdvantages: A bridged glen on the last easy ground before the bog — the only place the pilgrim road can cross and the only place it can stop.
why.occupantsMotive: The Nisswo stay because the sermon is not finished until the stone is gone; the innkeepers stay because pilgrims eat.
why.pressures: Foreign pilgrims want the ruin preserved; the Nisswo find that blasphemous. Rectavius is still sealed below and the seal is two centuries older than anyone tending it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a season if the xanmeer finally collapsed — which is, theologically, the point.

hardConstraints: within sight of the sermon xanmeer
places.hook: A bridged glen on the last easy ground before the bog — the only place the pilgrim road can cross and the only place it can stop

places.name: Sermon Xanmeer
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1105 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, sightline, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A Merethic Sithis temple deliberately left to decay so that its decay could be read aloud as scripture.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands above Glenbridge on the glen's shoulder, so the whole town can watch the sermon progress.
why.occupantsMotive: The Nisswo read it; the Clutch below them sweeps nothing away, because sweeping would be a lie.
why.pressures: The voriplasm-sorcerer Rectavius is sealed in the lowest chamber, and the seal is part of the structure that is being allowed to fail.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become the province's worst problem the day the sermon reaches the bottom course.

hardConstraints: above Glenbridge, visible from its square
places.hook: It stands above Glenbridge on the glen's shoulder, so the whole town can watch the sermon progress

places.name: Nine Bells Guar Holding
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 361 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-ravine-doors (+0.54).

why.founding: The Blackwood Road runs on guar, and guar have to be bred, broken and rested somewhere within a day of the city.
why.siteAdvantages: Rough grazing too poor for crops and too dry for rice, which is exactly what a guar herd wants.
why.occupantsMotive: The holding sells draught animals to carters and hires out handlers, and its hands are the best-paid labour in the zone.
why.pressures: Rootworm season unsettles the herd badly, and wintertide is the holding's worst month.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would double in size if the road ever ran year-round.

places.hook: Rough grazing too poor for crops and too dry for rice, which is exactly what a guar herd wants

places.name: Hangs-Above-The-Water
places.whySiteWon: gorge in upland hills (danger band 3), 128 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: When the Onkobra gorge floods it fills to within a few metres of the rim, so the people who work the gorge live in it: cut chambers and built galleries on the wall, above the worst water and below the wind.
why.siteAdvantages: The wall itself — dry rock, a constant temperature, and a face that cannot be approached by anything that does not climb.
why.occupantsMotive: Gorge work: netting the fish the narrows concentrate, and taking payment from boats that need a hand through the rapid.
why.pressures: The galleries are reached by ladder and rope, and every year somebody falls; the village argues constantly about whether to cut a stair, which would also let others up.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become an ordinary river village the day the stair was cut, and everyone knows it, which is why the stair is never cut.

hardConstraints: a gorge wall above the flood line
places.hook: The wall itself — dry rock, a constant temperature, and a face that cannot be approached by anything that does not climb

places.name: Hearth House of the Burnt Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 510 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A hearth house raised on the edge of the old burn country because that is where people arrive exhausted.
why.siteAdvantages: The first ground with living trees on the eastern approach out of the burn.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by the burn-scar village downslope as a matter of pride: they of all people know what arriving hungry means.
why.pressures: The burn ground still supports almost nothing, so stocking it costs the village more than it can spare.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be moved further into the burn if anyone ever re-greened it.

hardConstraints: at the edge of the burn ground
places.hook: The first ground with living trees on the eastern approach out of the burn

places.name: Highwater
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 32 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A dry rise in the flood plain will always be built on, because for four months a year it is the only ground there is.
why.siteAdvantages: A flood-high knoll that has never gone under in recorded memory, with landing on three sides in the wet.
why.occupantsMotive: The households here are the flood plain's landlords in the wet season and its equals in the dry.
why.pressures: The rise is small; there is no room to grow, and the third generation is having to leave.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned within a year of a flood that topped it, and the plain would lose its refuge.

hardConstraints: a rise that has never flooded
places.hook: A flood-high knoll that has never gone under in recorded memory, with landing on three sides in the wet

places.name: Hollow Arch
places.whySiteWon: sinkhole in lake & standing water (danger band 2), 70 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, hinterland, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.bonded-shed-of-the-onkobra (+0.26).

why.founding: The Onkobra's narrowest reach near the city was bridged in stone, and whoever holds a bridge in this province holds an income.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock nose on each bank: the only place a stone arch could land without piling.
why.occupantsMotive: Gideon's council farms the toll out annually to the highest bidder, which keeps the rate moving and the bidders unpopular.
why.pressures: The arch is hollow — a repair void the last farmer never filled — and the current one knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bypassed by the ford upstream if the toll ever rose above the price of wet feet.

places.hook: A rock nose on each bank: the only place a stone arch could land without piling

places.name: Keeps-The-Lower-Water
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 87 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-drowned-furrow (+0.66).

why.founding: Gideon's hunting trade needs someone living on the ground it hunts, to say what may be taken and when.
why.siteAdvantages: On the river below the last village, where every boat going upstream must pass the door.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper licenses hunters and takes a share; the villages accept it because he also culls what kills their stock.
why.pressures: The poachers work around him, and he knows exactly who they are.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced by a village office if the Gideon trade ever collapsed.

hardConstraints: on the river at a choke point
places.hook: On the river below the last village, where every boat going upstream must pass the door

places.name: Ladder-To-The-Light
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 167 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: The fig canopy over the lower Onkobra is closed enough that a fringe village cannot see its own river; a stack of platforms and ladders was built to put a lookout above the leaves, and then people found other uses for being up there.
why.siteAdvantages: A single very old fig with a straight bole, standing on firm ground within sight of the road, tall enough to break the canopy by six metres.
why.occupantsMotive: A lookout is paid by three villages to sit up there in the flood season and watch which lanes are open; the rest of the year it is climbed by anyone who wants to.
why.pressures: Every platform is younger than the one below it and the bottom ladder is the oldest thing here; the tree is also, slowly, growing out of the fixings.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the moment the tree died, and there is no second tree of this height within two kilometres.

hardConstraints: a canopy-breaking tree on firm ground
places.hook: A single very old fig with a straight bole, standing on firm ground within sight of the road, tall enough to break the canopy by six metres

places.name: Long Causeway
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in lake & standing water (danger band 2), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: The village answer to the Imperial embankment: a floating timber causeway that rides the flood instead of blocking it.
why.siteAdvantages: Crosses the widest shallow between the Gideon hinterland and the marsh edge, where nothing can be piled.
why.occupantsMotive: Six villages own segments and each maintains its own, so the causeway's quality changes every two hundred metres.
why.pressures: One village's segment is always in dispute and therefore always the worst.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced piecemeal forever — that is how it works.

places.hook: Crosses the widest shallow between the Gideon hinterland and the marsh edge, where nothing can be piled

places.name: Low-Water Fair
places.whySiteWon: spring head in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 55 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: When the water drops, a river bed becomes the widest flat surface in the marsh, and the villages that can only meet by boat can meet on foot.
why.siteAdvantages: A braided reach that dries to firm sand for eight weeks a year and is four metres deep the rest.
why.occupantsMotive: Villages come to settle marriages, debts and boundaries as much as to trade.
why.pressures: Anyone who miscalculates the rise loses their goods, and someone does most years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not exist at all in a wet year — and there have been three.

places.hook: A braided reach that dries to firm sand for eight weeks a year and is four metres deep the rest

places.name: Lower Onkobra Paddies
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 62 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: Rice is the one crop that works in a province that floods, and Gideon eats.
why.siteAdvantages: A terraced flood plain with controllable inflow — the flood is the irrigation, if you own the sluice.
why.occupantsMotive: The families here own the water rather than the land, which is the local form of property.
why.pressures: The sluice was Imperial-built and one gate has jammed open since the Oblivion Crisis; the lower terraces are permanently wet.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worth twice as much with a working gate, which is a repair, not a revolution.

places.hook: A terraced flood plain with controllable inflow — the flood is the irrigation, if you own the sluice

places.name: Lowmere
