places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: The western lake's level swings four metres a year, so its people stopped building on the shore and built on the water instead.
why.siteAdvantages: Sheltered water behind a headland, deep enough never to ground and shallow enough to pole.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay afloat because a rafted village cannot be evicted from land it does not occupy — a point they make often.
why.pressures: Gideon's council has twice tried to tax the lake and twice failed to find the village where it left it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would come ashore only under a threat no council could make.

places.hook: Sheltered water behind a headland, deep enough never to ground and shallow enough to pole

places.name: Marcian's Terrace
places.whySiteWon: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 386 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A Nibenese surveyor called Marcian took a grant of upland shelf nobody wanted because it was the only ground in the fringe where an Imperial crop would grow, and was right — two centuries later the village is Argonian and still called after him.
why.siteAdvantages: Above the fever line and above the flood: on the rim shelf the marsh rules stop applying, the water is clean and the nights are cold enough to keep grain.
why.occupantsMotive: Terrace farmers who can sell dry grain into a province that mostly cannot grow any, at a price that justifies carrying it down a mountain.
why.pressures: Everything has to be carried; the shelf has no water in the dry months but what it stores; and Gideon's assessors treat upland grain as a luxury and tax it accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in one generation if the cisterns failed, and the cisterns are the oldest Imperial thing here.

hardConstraints: upland shelf above the flood and the fever line
stored water for the dry months
places.hook: Above the fever line and above the flood: on the rim shelf the marsh rules stop applying, the water is clean and the nights are cold enough to keep grain

places.name: Mile House of the Eagle
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 91 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A Legion road-house built one march west of Gideon, kept open because the road still needs a place to stop before the gate closes at dusk.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm, drained ground before the road drops to the flood plain; a walled yard big enough for six carts.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper holds an inherited road-warrant nobody has renewed since the Legions left, and produces it unprompted.
why.pressures: Fort Swampmoth's toll-takers stop here too, and the keeper cannot refuse them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close the first year the road did not carry carts.

places.hook: The last firm, drained ground before the road drops to the flood plain; a walled yard big enough for six carts

places.name: Moonmarch Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 290 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.dreams-in-mud (+1.30).

why.founding: The fringe keeps the Argonian calendar on Imperial ground: for one month of the twelve the road villages between Gideon and the Onkobra empty out onto this flat and hold Moonmarch here, and for the other eleven it is a field with post-holes in it.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide dry flat the monsoon leaves alone, close enough to three villages that nobody has to sleep out, far enough from Gideon that the magistracy does not attend.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. The family that holds the ground holds it precisely so that nobody builds on it, and the arrangement is older than the Imperial title that supposedly governs it.
why.pressures: Gideon's clerks have twice tried to license the gathering and twice been told there is nothing here to license; a Nibenese landowner has started grazing the flat out of season to establish use.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a permanent fairground the day anyone put up a roof, which is exactly why nobody has.

hardConstraints: a dry flat that does not flood
within a half-day of three villages
places.hook: A wide dry flat the monsoon leaves alone, close enough to three villages that nobody has to sleep out, far enough from Gideon that the magistracy does not attend

places.name: Moonrack
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Folk alchemy here is a moon-timed craft, and calcining needs a level court laid out to the moons, not to the sun.
why.siteAdvantages: A flat upland shelf with an unobstructed eastern horizon — rare below the rim and worth walking to.
why.occupantsMotive: The two practitioners here sell reagents to Gideon and teach nobody, which is normal.
why.pressures: Their court's alignment is drifting out of true as the shelf slumps, and they are arguing about whether to move.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be rebuilt fifty metres east, entirely, rather than adjusted.

hardConstraints: a level shelf with an open eastern horizon
places.hook: A flat upland shelf with an unobstructed eastern horizon — rare below the rim and worth walking to

places.name: Nine-Arch Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A stage grew where the road crosses the flood plain on a nine-arched viaduct, because the crossing takes longer than the daylight left.
why.siteAdvantages: The viaduct's dry undercroft is the only rain-proof shelter for two hours in either direction.
why.occupantsMotive: The family here sells fuel and fodder and charges for the undercroft, which they do not own.
why.pressures: Four arches have silted solid, so the flood now goes over the road rather than under it twice a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the viaduct failed — and it will.

places.hook: The viaduct's dry undercroft is the only rain-proof shelter for two hours in either direction

places.name: Ninefold
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 646 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A village that exists to rebuild carts, because the road's stone surface destroys wheels made for marsh paths.
why.siteAdvantages: Halfway between the fort and the marsh edge: the exact distance at which the wheels fail.
why.occupantsMotive: Nine families, each with one specialism, refuse to teach each other's trade.
why.pressures: The road surface is breaking up and taking fewer wheels with it, which is bad for Ninefold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a farming village within two generations if the road stone finished failing.

places.hook: Halfway between the fort and the marsh edge: the exact distance at which the wheels fail

places.name: Ninth Milestone House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1026 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-vellum-estate (+0.44).

why.founding: A house built against a Legion milestone by a family who found it easier to name themselves after it than to name the place.
why.siteAdvantages: Nine miles from the gate: the distance a loaded porter covers before wanting to stop.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters and pilgrims are the trade; the family sells water, shade and foot-binding.
why.pressures: The pilgrim traffic to Glenbridge has doubled and the well has not.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced by a bigger house on the same spot, which is how every stop on this road grew.

hardConstraints: on the road at porter-stage distance
places.hook: Nine miles from the gate: the distance a loaded porter covers before wanting to stop

places.name: Onkobra Clay Pits
places.whySiteWon: ravine in firm lowland (danger band 2), 58 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Gideon's red pottery is canon; red pottery means a red clay bank, a water source and a kiln within a cart of the city.
why.siteAdvantages: A cut meander bank exposes the clay in a two-metre seam; the river takes the waste and brings the fuel.
why.occupantsMotive: Four potting families work it in rotation and quarrel about the rotation.
why.pressures: The seam is being undercut by the river it depends on; the wintertide rootworm migration marks its stop with this very clay, and the waykeepers want the bank left alone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move fifty metres upstream, as it has three times before, which is the most Argonian thing about it.

hardConstraints: exposed clay seam at a river bank
places.hook: A cut meander bank exposes the clay in a two-metre seam; the river takes the waste and brings the fuel

places.name: Onkobra Ferry
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The river below Gideon is too wide to bridge and too useful not to cross.
why.siteAdvantages: A double bend slows the current to polling speed, and both banks shelve gently.
why.occupantsMotive: The ferry family has held the crossing four generations and treats the rope as property.
why.pressures: The bonded warehouse opposite would rather load direct and cut them out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the day a bridge is built, which the council proposes every decade.

places.hook: A double bend slows the current to polling speed, and both banks shelve gently

places.name: Onkobra Field Station
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 49 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-kept-terrace (+1.26).

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections needed somewhere to hold specimens between the licensed dig and the boat to Gideon, and a licence pinned to a wall is cheaper than an argument with a magistrate at the quayside.
why.siteAdvantages: On the Onkobra bank where the current is slow enough to land a boat and the bank high enough that the jars survive the monsoon.
why.occupantsMotive: Two scholars and a local assistant who does the actual collecting; they stay because the licence is site-specific and would take two years to move.
why.pressures: Chronically underfunded, half a year behind on its returns, and quietly selling duplicate specimens to pay for lamp oil — which the assistant knows and the scholars think she does not.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close within a season if the licence lapsed, and everything in the jars would end up in a Gideon tradehouse.

hardConstraints: a landable bank on the Onkobra
places.hook: On the Onkobra bank where the current is slow enough to land a boat and the bank high enough that the jars survive the monsoon

places.name: Onkobra Kwama Mine
places.whySiteWon: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 437 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.saddle-fair (+1.18).

why.founding: Dunmer husbandry practised at the far western end of its range, because Gideon will buy eggs and Leyawiin will buy them dearer. The workings themselves changed hands in the 3E uprisings, when the Argonian mine hands took the kwama mines from their Dunmer owners; the husbandry is Dunmer technique kept on by Argonian owners, not Dunmer ownership.
why.siteAdvantages: A limestone shoulder above the Onkobra with dry galleries — the only ground in the west a kwama colony will hold.
why.occupantsMotive: The mining family keeps the queen alive because a dead queen is a dead trade; the Owing hands work it because they were entered in a ledger.
why.pressures: Scribs get out; the colony has been pushed for two hundred years and the eggs are smaller than the ledgers say they should be.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse the year the queen dies, and everyone here knows the date is close.

hardConstraints: dry gallery ground above the river
places.hook: A limestone shoulder above the Onkobra with dry galleries — the only ground in the west a kwama colony will hold

places.name: Open-To-All
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 64 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.xi-tsei-massacre-ground (+1.18).

why.founding: The obligation to shelter a comer is absolute, so villages maintain a house that is nobody's and everybody's.
why.siteAdvantages: Set at the saddle where four paths meet, so the obligation is discharged where it is most needed.
why.occupantsMotive: It is kept by rota; the family whose month it is stocks it and does not attend it.
why.pressures: Foreigners keep trying to pay, which is understood as an insult and forgiven as ignorance.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a scandal if it were ever found empty of fuel.

places.hook: Set at the saddle where four paths meet, so the obligation is discharged where it is most needed

places.name: Hand-Read Halls
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in border mountains (danger band 3), 967 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, region.

why.founding: The Orma were canon-native to Black Marsh and gone by the late Third Era. They built for people with no eyes, and this is the only Orma work in the province substantial enough to still be read — by hand.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry box canyon in the western hills: enclosed, quiet, and acoustically legible, which for its builders was the whole specification.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. A scholars' camp outside has been at it for two seasons and is measuring the wrong things.
why.pressures: Every visitor brings a lamp, and the lamp is exactly what stops the building working.
why.wouldChangeIf: Anyone who put the light out and followed the ridges would find the chamber, which is the whole design of the place and cannot be brute-forced.

places.hook: A dry box canyon in the western hills: enclosed, quiet, and acoustically legible, which for its builders was the whole specification

places.name: Red Cart Yard
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in firm lowland (danger band 1), 20 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Freight changes carriers where the wheeled road ends and the marsh paths begin; somebody organises the change and takes a cut.
why.siteAdvantages: The last hard standing before the ground goes soft — carts cannot go on, porters cannot start earlier.
why.occupantsMotive: The yard master holds the porters' Owing entries, so the labour cannot leave for a better yard.
why.pressures: Two porters have run this year, and the yard master has posted their names.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its purpose if the causeway were ever built to cart standard.

places.hook: The last hard standing before the ground goes soft — carts cannot go on, porters cannot start earlier

places.name: Red Daub Relay
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 474 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent.

why.founding: The province's letters move by running couriers, and a run has to break where the ground changes.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road path meets the marsh path, with red clay daubed on the trees to mark it for people who cannot read.
why.occupantsMotive: The runners hold the relay because the office is inherited and carries the right to refuse a letter.
why.pressures: The council wants the letters read; the runners regard that as the one thing they will not do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse if the running families ever agreed to be paid by the council instead of the senders.

places.hook: Where the road path meets the marsh path, with red clay daubed on the trees to mark it for people who cannot read

places.name: Reedcutters' Bridge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 31 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: A village-built floating timber bridge on the reed road, tolled in reed bundles rather than coin.
why.siteAdvantages: A slow, shallow reach where a buoyant causeway can be moored rather than piled.
why.occupantsMotive: The cutters maintain it themselves and take their toll in the one thing they need and cannot carry far.
why.pressures: Coin-payers are charged more, which foreigners find funny until they understand it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be untied and floated away if a tax-taker ever tried to farm it.

places.hook: A slow, shallow reach where a buoyant causeway can be moored rather than piled

places.name: Ridge Runners' Post
places.whySiteWon: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 498 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: The rim route between Gideon and the north is faster than the road and no cart can use it, so letters go that way and nothing else does.
why.siteAdvantages: A saddle high enough that a runner can see the next saddle — one of the very few places in the province where that is true.
why.occupantsMotive: Runners use it because it halves the time to Stormhold; nobody else uses it because it is a scramble.
why.pressures: One bad section is washing out and the runners argue about whether to say so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be lost in a season if the runners stopped clearing it.

hardConstraints: a saddle with a line to the next saddle
places.hook: A saddle high enough that a runner can see the next saddle — one of the very few places in the province where that is true

places.name: Rockgrove
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 1190 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A Sul-Xan holding in the Blackwood: a staging ground for raids that take souls rather than goods.
why.siteAdvantages: Screened by jungle on three sides, one ravine path in, and a stream that hides the noise of a camp.
why.occupantsMotive: The Sul-Xan raid to feed soul-snares; the site persists because it has never been found twice by the same people.
why.pressures: Stonewastes' Four Winds hunt them; the Empire's old bounty on jade masks is still quoted in Gideon. The Sul-Xan are not alone on this ground: the Ca-Uxith are charged by their Hist with watching the xanmeer, and their stone-talkers hold the ruins against the geyser field beneath it — the raid camp sits on top of somebody else's duty.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move within a season of a serious defeat — the camp is the people, not the ground.

places.hook: Screened by jungle on three sides, one ravine path in, and a stream that hides the noise of a camp

places.name: Sabinus' Claim
places.whySiteWon: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 351 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The Niben crystal workings made two men rich a generation ago, and every year since, someone Nibenese has arrived on the fringe convinced the seam runs east; this is the current one, with a claim mark, a sample pile and about eleven weeks of food.
why.siteAdvantages: A scree slope where the country rock is exposed without digging, close enough to the road that a mule can reach it and far enough that nobody watches what is dug.
why.occupantsMotive: Sabinus believes the seam is here. His two hired locals believe he will pay them and are correct for about another month.
why.pressures: The sample pile is getting bigger and the food is getting smaller, which is the whole story of the place, and both are visible from the path.
why.wouldChangeIf: Will be an abandoned camp within a season either way — either because he was wrong, or because being right brings a hundred people and a licence.

places.hook: A scree slope where the country rock is exposed without digging, close enough to the road that a mule can reach it and far enough that nobody watches what is dug

places.name: Saddle Fair
places.whySiteWon: ravine in upland hills (danger band 2), 213 m from the nearest route; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.onkobra-kwama-mine (+1.18).

why.founding: Gideon's gate tax made it cheaper to trade outside the walls, so the trade went outside the walls.
why.siteAdvantages: The flat saddle floor a kilometre west of the gate: level, drained, and legally nowhere.
why.occupantsMotive: Traders come because there is no tax; the council tolerates it because it can watch the whole field from the wall.
why.pressures: Every few years the council tries to enclose it, and every few years the fair moves two hundred metres.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be inside the city within a decade if the gate tax were dropped.

hardConstraints: level drained ground outside a city's jurisdiction
places.hook: The flat saddle floor a kilometre west of the gate: level, drained, and legally nowhere

places.name: Silver Mouth
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 4), 39 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A Kothringi river town that emptied inside one season in 2E 560 and was never entered again.
why.siteAdvantages: A river mouth on the lake with the only stone quay in the west — the Kothringi built to last, which is why it is still here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the neighbouring villages regard the ground as still infectious, three hundred years on.
why.pressures: The quay is the best landing on the lake and the taboo is the only reason it is unused.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be occupied within a year if a single respected voice said the ground was clean.

hardConstraints: a stone quay at a river mouth
places.hook: A river mouth on the lake with the only stone quay in the west — the Kothringi built to last, which is why it is still here

places.name: Silver Cairns
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 86 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: The Kothringi buried under stone, and this hillside holds a whole community's worth from the last generation before the Flu.
why.siteAdvantages: A stony hill shoulder where cairn stone lay ready to hand — the only reason the site is here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it; Argonian custom has no use for it and there are no Kothringi left to disagree.
why.pressures: Treasure-hunters take the glass beads; the practice is old enough that some cairns have been opened twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be protected if anyone in the province had standing to protect a dead people's graves.

places.hook: A stony hill shoulder where cairn stone lay ready to hand — the only reason the site is here

places.name: Slough Point
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in firm lowland (danger band 2), 6 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, parent.

why.founding: The Empire put its census and excise station where the Blackwood Road first touches navigable water, so goods could be counted twice.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank at the head of a slow reach: carts arrive, boats leave, and the two must be weighed against each other somewhere.
why.occupantsMotive: The excise remains because whoever collects it eats; the census remains because the ledgers are the only proof anyone here exists.
why.pressures: Everything worth taxing now goes by the rim paths instead; the town's takings fall every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would die if the road were abandoned, or become rich again if a state ever taxed the marsh in earnest.

hardConstraints: a place to hold carts overnight
places.hook: A firm bank at the head of a slow reach: carts arrive, boats leave, and the two must be weighed against each other somewhere

places.name: Customs Waiting Shed
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 35 m from the nearest route; no free 'river-mouth' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Slough Point's excise came with a census, and a census in a province that remembers the Knahaten Flu means an inspection shed.
why.siteAdvantages: On the landing, before the weighbridge — nothing passes inland unlooked-at.
why.occupantsMotive: The inspectors keep it because the fee for release is theirs; nobody has been detained in living memory.
why.pressures: The forms still ask questions about a plague that ended two centuries ago, in a script most comers cannot read.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be repurposed as a store the day the excise lapsed.

hardConstraints: at a landing, before the customs point
places.hook: On the landing, before the weighbridge — nothing passes inland unlooked-at

places.name: Stonefoot
places.whySiteWon: spring head in border mountains (danger band 3), 421 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Upland Argonians terrace, because the hills are the only ground in the province where terracing is possible at all.
why.siteAdvantages: A south-facing slope above the ravine head, with spring water at the top and stone to build the terraces from.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because terraces are generational work and abandoning them wastes four lifetimes.
why.pressures: Using stone for the terrace walls is a compromise the lowland villages needle them about constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse literally and socially if the spring at the top failed.

hardConstraints: a south-facing slope with a spring above
places.hook: A south-facing slope above the ravine head, with spring water at the top and stone to build the terraces from

places.name: Stonewastes
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 456 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.swampmoth-town (+0.58).

why.founding: A bogland town that grew around a xanmeer keep its people never stopped using, defended since their ancestors raised their first hut by the hereditary Four Winds.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls that already existed, on the only firm ground in a bog nobody else can cross quickly.
why.occupantsMotive: The Four Winds hold the keep because holding it is who they are; the Sul-Xan raiding out of the Blackwood is why the office never lapsed.
why.pressures: Four hereditary captains and one gate is three captains too many; the Sul-Xan press harder each dry season.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change utterly if the Four Winds ever accepted an outside charter — which is exactly what the Marsh Charter will ask of them.

places.hook: Stone walls that already existed, on the only firm ground in a bog nobody else can cross quickly

places.name: Swampmoth Town
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in upland hills (danger band 3), 658 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.stonewastes (+0.58).

why.founding: A garrison feeds, drinks and buys, so a town grows below its gate whether or not the garrison is legitimate.
why.siteAdvantages: The apron of firm ground below the fort's ridge, inside the arc the fort can protect.
why.occupantsMotive: The town lives off the toll company and is embarrassed about it in public and not in private.
why.pressures: If the tolls fail, the town starves; if the tolls succeed, the town is complicit. It has chosen.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would survive as a road village at a third the size — which is what it was before.

hardConstraints: below a held fort, within its protective arc
places.hook: The apron of firm ground below the fort's ridge, inside the arc the fort can protect

places.name: Abandoned Survey
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 419 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: An Imperial survey party set out to run a level line from Gideon to the pass and stopped, mid-line, forty years ago; the camp is still where they left it because the ground it stands on is worth nothing to anyone.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry knoll on the line itself, chosen for sightlines between stations rather than for any human reason, which is why nobody has taken it over.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The interesting question is why they stopped, and the answer is in the field book still in the tent.
why.pressures: Nothing pressures it; that is its condition. The canopy has closed over two of the survey stations and the third is under water.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the start of a road if anyone ever finished the line — which is precisely the fringe's oldest and least-believed promise.

hardConstraints: a knoll on a survey line
places.hook: A dry knoll on the line itself, chosen for sightlines between stations rather than for any human reason, which is why nobody has taken it over

places.name: Makes-And-Burns
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 333 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Nisswo doctrine holds that a made thing must be unmade, and pilgrims on the sermon road need somewhere to do it.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel spit in a river bend: a flat working floor that the flood clears entirely every year.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims make something here and destroy it; the site's whole content is what has not been destroyed yet.
why.pressures: Collectors have started stealing pieces before they can be unmade, which is theologically catastrophic and commercially excellent.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be spoiled permanently if a piece from here were ever displayed in Gideon.

hardConstraints: a working floor the flood clears annually
places.hook: A gravel spit in a river bend: a flat working floor that the flood clears entirely every year

places.name: The Back Kiln
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A disused pottery kiln outside the clay pits became the place where Gideon does what it cannot do inside the walls.
why.siteAdvantages: A domed brick chamber that holds heat, hides light, and has one door — ideal for exactly one purpose.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper pays the tower clerk to record the site as derelict, and it is, on paper.
why.pressures: Owing enforcers recruit here; so do people organising against them, on different nights.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be burned out by the council the week it became embarrassing rather than useful.

places.hook: A domed brick chamber that holds heat, hides light, and has one door — ideal for exactly one purpose

places.name: The Black Tarn
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 659 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A deep cold tarn in a rim basin holds something old, and the villages' rule about it predates their oldest stories.
why.siteAdvantages: A drowned box canyon: sheer walls, forty metres of cold water, one narrow outlet.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing human lives here. The rule is that you may drink from the outlet and not from the tarn.
why.pressures: Treasure-hunters ignore the rule roughly once a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change. That is what fixed danger means; the province will not soften it.

hardConstraints: deep cold water in a closed basin
places.hook: A drowned box canyon: sheer walls, forty metres of cold water, one narrow outlet

places.name: The Borrowed House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 272 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-cold-forge (+0.50).

why.founding: An Imperial road villa emptied two centuries ago, and one family has been living in three of its rooms for two generations.
why.siteAdvantages: It is dry, roofed, and off the road behind a hedge that has become a wall.
why.occupantsMotive: They live here because it is free; they have built a reed house inside the atrium rather than use the rooms as rooms.
why.pressures: Living in dead stone is a compromise their neighbours mention, and the reed house inside is their answer to it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned without regret the day the roof went.

places.hook: It is dry, roofed, and off the road behind a hedge that has become a wall

places.name: The Buried Spears
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 199 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: When the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War they buried their weapons rather than surrendering them.
why.siteAdvantages: Under a bank of dry sand above the flood line, where iron would keep — chosen by people who expected to come back.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody has come back. The location is passed on as a story with directions in it.
why.pressures: The Owing brokers would pay for the location; so would the Marsh Charter, for opposite reasons.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious political object the day anyone dug it up.

places.hook: Under a bank of dry sand above the flood line, where iron would keep — chosen by people who expected to come back

places.name: The Cold Forge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 576 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-borrowed-house (+0.50).

why.founding: Somebody in the west still works iron, because the road runs on iron tyres and nobody else will touch it.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the bog-iron workings and downwind of everything, because the neighbours insisted.
why.occupantsMotive: The smith is Imperial-trained, Argonian-born, and equally unwelcome in both explanations of himself.
why.pressures: Working metal is a moral error to most of his neighbours; they still bring him their tyres.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close the day the road did, and he would be relieved.

places.hook: Beside the bog-iron workings and downwind of everything, because the neighbours insisted

places.name: The Cold Lights
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1324 m from the nearest route; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on parent, hinterland, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.dreams-in-mud (+0.27).

why.founding: A cold spring feeds one arm of the lake, and whatever lives in it lights when it is disturbed.
why.siteAdvantages: A dead-end arm with no current, where the bloom is never flushed out.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody owns it; the raft village uses it to navigate at night and treats it as a shared instrument.
why.pressures: It is dimmer than it was, and the village argues about whether that is the spring or the lake.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious loss, practically as well as aesthetically, if it failed.

hardConstraints: still water fed by a cold spring
places.hook: A dead-end arm with no current, where the bloom is never flushed out

places.name: The Cordon Stones
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A line of marker stones set across the western approaches during the Knahaten Flu, to say which side of the line the living were on.
why.siteAdvantages: Follows the natural contour where the ground firms up — the line a fleeing population would take anyway.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody has moved a stone in three hundred years, and villages still do not build across it.
why.pressures: The stones are being lost one by one to root-heave, and nobody has a record of where they were.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be forgotten entirely in another century, which is the only thing the villages agree it should not do.

hardConstraints: a contour line of set stones
places.hook: Follows the natural contour where the ground firms up — the line a fleeing population would take anyway

places.name: Counts-The-Dead
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 575 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.bone-road-waystation (+0.77).

why.founding: The Flu killed faster than the dead could be carried home, so the western road villages made one ground and counted into it.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the road, so that anyone carrying bones west has somewhere to stop before the last stage.
why.occupantsMotive: A bone-carrier's office is hereditary here; the current holder keeps the count in her head and on stakes.
why.pressures: The count is still rising, because Owing deaths and burn-country deaths are added to it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close if a court ever ruled that the road's dead had somewhere else to go.

hardConstraints: on a road, on ground that takes bone
places.hook: Beside the road, so that anyone carrying bones west has somewhere to stop before the last stage

places.name: Drowned Furrow
places.whySiteWon: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 4), 104 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.keepers-lodge-of-the-lower-onkobra (+0.66).

why.founding: A second grant, worked by a family who ploughed the way they had at home and drained nothing.
why.siteAdvantages: The site is superb for eight months and under half a metre of water for four.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody is here; the marsh took the fields and the family went back to Leyawiin without selling.
why.pressures: The house is sound and the neighbours will not use it, because a house whose owners may return is not theirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be reoccupied instantly by anyone from outside the local etiquette — which is the hook.

places.hook: The site is superb for eight months and under half a metre of water for four

places.name: The Drowned Mule
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 1261 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings (+0.56).

why.founding: A carters' house at the wet end of the road, named for the animal the flood took the year it opened.
why.siteAdvantages: The last building on firm ground before the drowning gate; carters stop here whether they want to or not.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper survives on the wet season, when the road closes and forty carters are stuck for a week.
why.pressures: In a dry year it nearly starves, so the keeper prays for floods and says so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate if the barrier moved, and the sign would go with it.

hardConstraints: last firm ground before a seasonal closure
places.hook: The last building on firm ground before the drowning gate; carters stop here whether they want to or not

places.name: The Drowning Gate
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 578 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Canon closes the Blackwood Road in the monsoon; something has to close it, and this is where.
why.siteAdvantages: The road's lowest point, where the plain drains across it — the water arrives here first and leaves last.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families are paid by Gideon to swing the barrier and to argue with whoever wants it opened anyway.
why.pressures: Every wet season somebody drives round the barrier and drowns; the tally board says how many.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be unnecessary if the Empire's raised causeway had ever been finished — see the drowned embankment beside it.

places.hook: The road's lowest point, where the plain drains across it — the water arrives here first and leaves last

places.name: The Eight Steps
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 1053 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The Onkobra's upper river drops through eight ledges in a kilometre, which is where boats stop and portage starts.
why.siteAdvantages: A confined reach with rock ledges — the hydrology makes the hazard and the hazard makes the trade.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives in it; the portage families live above and below it and both claim the whole.
why.pressures: Someone runs it every year on a bet and roughly every third one dies.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a route rather than a wall if anyone cut a proper portage path, which is a season's work nobody funds.

hardConstraints: a confined reach with successive ledges
places.hook: A confined reach with rock ledges — the hydrology makes the hazard and the hazard makes the trade

places.name: Drowned Embankment
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 720 m from the nearest route; won on sightline, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: An Imperial scheme to raise the road above the flood, begun with foreign engineering and no local hydrology.
why.siteAdvantages: It runs dead straight across the plain, which is exactly why it failed: it dammed the drainage it crossed.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the villages downstream have been cutting gaps in it for two hundred years.
why.pressures: Each cut gap makes the next flood worse somewhere else, and the arguments about which gap to close are inherited.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a fine road if anyone rebuilt it with culverts — which is what the unfinished culvert line was for.

hardConstraints: a straight raised bank across drainage
places.hook: It runs dead straight across the plain, which is exactly why it failed: it dammed the drainage it crossed

places.name: The Empty Steading
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 308 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A river station built by a family who left for Leyawiin in the last bad flood and did not return.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank at a channel junction with its own landing, a walled yard and a well — everything a holding needs and nobody in it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The neighbours have agreed it can be claimed, and have not agreed by whom.
why.pressures: Two villages and the Owing brokers all have a colourable claim; the question has been open four years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would settle the moment somebody credible moved in and made the case — which is exactly the offer.

hardConstraints: a defensible bank at a channel junction
places.hook: A firm bank at a channel junction with its own landing, a walled yard and a well — everything a holding needs and nobody in it

places.name: The Fig and Ledger
places.whySiteWon: spring head in firm lowland (danger band 2), 124 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.bonded-shed-of-the-onkobra (+0.79).

why.founding: Court business generates waiting, and waiting generates a house that sells wine to people who are waiting.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly outside Gideon's courthouse gate, in the shade of the one old fig on the street.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper sells information as readily as wine and has never been caught selling it twice.
why.pressures: Advocates and fences drink in the same room by unspoken arrangement, and it holds until it doesn't.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close if the courthouse ever stopped sitting — the whole trade is adjournments.

places.hook: Directly outside Gideon's courthouse gate, in the shade of the one old fig on the street

places.name: Fig Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 698 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.burnt-field-village (+1.00).

why.founding: Gideon buys hide and meat and does not ask which side of the village boundaries it came from.
why.siteAdvantages: A dense fig thicket in a ravine head — no sightlines in, water, and three ways out.
why.occupantsMotive: The poachers are village men working a second season's income and would be recognised in daylight.
why.pressures: The village whose ground they work has begun setting its own watch, and there will be a confrontation.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fold immediately if Gideon's market ever asked for provenance.

hardConstraints: dense cover at a ravine head
places.hook: A dense fig thicket in a ravine head — no sightlines in, water, and three ways out

places.name: The Glass Scar
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A gate opened on the Blackwood frontier in 4E 5–7 and the Argonians went through it rather than away from it.
why.siteAdvantages: The scar sits on the flat by the road, because that is where the gate stood and gates did not choose ground.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the villages leave it because the ground has never grown back properly.
why.pressures: The Synod wants to survey it, the villages will not permit it, and the argument is annual.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be entirely overgrown by now anywhere else in the province, which is the disturbing part.

hardConstraints: a sterile circle of fused ground
places.hook: The scar sits on the flat by the road, because that is where the gate stood and gates did not choose ground

places.name: Hackwing Scarp
places.whySiteWon: gorge in border mountains (danger band 3), 808 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A rim scarp with south-facing ledges and thermals is a hackwing colony whether anyone likes it or not.
why.siteAdvantages: Broken cliff ledges above a warm slope; the birds have used it long enough to whiten the rock.
why.occupantsMotive: The birds are here for the updraught; the villages below are here despite them.
why.pressures: Lambing season and hatching season coincide, which is the whole relationship.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change; the colony is older than the villages.

places.hook: Broken cliff ledges above a warm slope; the birds have used it long enough to whiten the rock

places.name: Hollow Pass Station
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 217 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: The rim path from Gideon to the north crosses one saddle where a person caught by weather will die, so there is a station on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle's lee side, in a natural hollow that breaks the wind from three directions.
why.occupantsMotive: Two keepers hold it on a season's rota from the villages below, for food and standing.
why.pressures: The path is used more each year by couriers and smugglers, and the station is provisioned for neither number.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the year the rim path lost its traffic to a safer road, which does not exist.

places.hook: The saddle's lee side, in a natural hollow that breaks the wind from three directions

places.name: The Hollow Under the Figs
places.whySiteWon: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 933 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: The province has almost no rock, so its caves are root galleries — and the fringe's fig-root mats make the westernmost of them.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the root layer runs over a drained hollow, the roots hold a roof and the ground beneath has gone.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing keeps it; the poachers below use its mouth and will not go past the second chamber.
why.pressures: The roots are alive and moving, on a timescale of years, so the gallery's shape changes.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close on itself in a decade if the figs above it were felled.

hardConstraints: a live root roof over a drained void
places.hook: Where the root layer runs over a drained hollow, the roots hold a roof and the ground beneath has gone

places.name: Keeps-The-Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 44 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.onkobra-field-station (+1.26).

why.founding: A Merethic xanmeer at the province's western edge, tended by the nearest village as a monument and not as a dungeon.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise above the flood with a terrace that has never been under water — which is why it was built there.
why.occupantsMotive: The village keeps it swept because keeping it swept is what their office is; entering it to loot is a serious offence and they will tell you so.
why.pressures: Gideon's antiquities trade is two days away and getting closer every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be sealed by its own keepers the first time a theft succeeded.

places.hook: A rise above the flood with a terrace that has never been under water — which is why it was built there

places.name: High Scree Floor
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 251 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A province that distrusts metal still needs edges, and this scree has been worked for stone tools since the Merethic.
why.siteAdvantages: A scree of fine-grained stone below a rim cliff — the only workable lithic source in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families come up each dry season and work it, as their families have for longer than anyone counts.
why.pressures: Gideon's iron is cheaper and worse, and the young increasingly buy it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would go quiet within two generations, and the floor would still be here, which is the point.

places.hook: A scree of fine-grained stone below a rim cliff — the only workable lithic source in the west

places.name: Onkobra Divers' Yard
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 874 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, parent, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: The lake has a drowned Kothringi town in it and three centuries of boats on top of that, and Argonians can simply go down and look.
why.siteAdvantages: A shingle beach with deep water twenty metres out — the shortest swim to the good ground on the whole lake.
why.occupantsMotive: The divers work the wrecks and avoid the town, because the town is prohibited and the wrecks are not.
why.pressures: Two of the younger divers have started working the town at night, and the yard is dividing over it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be rich and finished within five years if the prohibition broke.

places.hook: A shingle beach with deep water twenty metres out — the shortest swim to the good ground on the whole lake

places.name: The Lamp at the Ford
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 406 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A house at an upland ford that keeps a lamp burning all night, because the ford is unmarked and people drowned before it did.
why.siteAdvantages: The ford is the only crossing for two kilometres and the banks are steep enough to hide it.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper's family took on the lamp as a debt to a drowned cousin and has kept it eighty years.
why.pressures: Lamp oil is expensive here and the family is not rich; guests are expected to understand this.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would go dark the year the family fails, and the ford would start killing again.

places.hook: The ford is the only crossing for two kilometres and the banks are steep enough to hide it

places.name: Last Post
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 217 m from the nearest route; no free 'saddle' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Somebody has to stand where the province ends, and after the Empire left it was the Argonians who kept doing it.
why.siteAdvantages: The narrowest point of the road cut, with rock either side — a gate that needs almost no wall.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers are villagers under a rota, and they check for disease and for slavers, in that order.
why.pressures: Cyrodiil's side is unmanned, which the keepers find both restful and insulting.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a real frontier if anything on the other side ever came back.

places.hook: The narrowest point of the road cut, with rock either side — a gate that needs almost no wall

places.name: Leaning Watch
places.whySiteWon: summit in upland hills (danger band 3), 701 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.swampmoth-town (+1.17).

why.founding: The tower's twin, built on ground that turned out to be a peat lens rather than rock.
why.siteAdvantages: It has the same commanding view and is falling into it at about a degree a decade.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; children dare each other up it and a hermit sleeps in the base in winter.
why.pressures: It leans towards the road, which everyone finds ominous and nobody finds urgent.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would come down entirely in one wet season, and the villages have a wager on the year.

places.hook: It has the same commanding view and is falling into it at about a degree a decade

places.name: Ledge of Tallies
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 274 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: There is exactly one legal crossing into Cyrodiil, so every other crossing is on the rim and none of them are level.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench with a ravine below and a saddle above — goods can be lowered to it from one province and lifted to the other.
why.occupantsMotive: The carriers here are village men from both sides who have worked the same ledge for generations.
why.pressures: Fort Swampmoth's company has begun pricing the legal road so high that the ledge is now busier than it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the tolls ever dropped, which would be the cheapest border policy available.

hardConstraints: a bench between a ravine and a saddle
places.hook: A cliff bench with a ravine below and a saddle above — goods can be lowered to it from one province and lifted to the other

places.name: The Marble Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 313 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, sightline.

why.founding: Imperials buried their dead here for two centuries in a province where burial does not work.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry knoll outside the walls, chosen by people who assumed dry knolls stay dry.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it; the Imperial families left, and Argonians will not tend a grave, having other arrangements.
why.pressures: The water table rose; a third of the plots have surfaced, and the city does not discuss it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be cleared if anyone in Gideon were willing to touch it, which nobody is.

hardConstraints: a knoll outside a city wall
places.hook: A dry knoll outside the walls, chosen by people who assumed dry knolls stay dry

places.name: The Month Chapel
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 74 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A Maran mission on the Blackwood Road, whose brothers died of swamp rot inside a month — the same fate as Umpholo, on the road instead of the interior.
why.siteAdvantages: Built on what the surveyors called firm ground and the locals called a wet-season island.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the road villages route around it, and the routing is a hundred and eighty years old.
why.pressures: It is being eaten by fig roots at a rate that can be measured year to year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have been a village if it had been sited fifty metres higher — which is the sermon the locals draw from it.

hardConstraints: off the road on a wet-season island
places.hook: Built on what the surveyors called firm ground and the locals called a wet-season island

places.name: Niben Crystal Workings
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 37 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Niben-crystal comes out of the Blackwood's hills, and the enchanters' benches of two provinces will buy it.
why.siteAdvantages: A ravine wall where the seam is exposed by the water that cut it — the river did the prospecting.
why.occupantsMotive: A family works the seam and sells to whichever side pays; they have no politics and say so.
why.pressures: The seam runs under the ravine floor, which means working in water, which is killing them slowly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be taken over by an outside concession the day the family failed.

hardConstraints: an exposed seam in a ravine wall
places.hook: A ravine wall where the seam is exposed by the water that cut it — the river did the prospecting

places.name: Old Office House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 39 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Some village offices are held by a household rather than a village, and that household lives apart from both.
why.siteAdvantages: Midway between four villages on the only ground none of them claims.
why.occupantsMotive: The holder settles boundary and water disputes for all four, and lives apart so that she can.
why.pressures: Her heir does not want the office, and no other household will take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would leave four villages arguing directly with each other, which none of them wants.

places.hook: Midway between four villages on the only ground none of them claims

places.name: The Old Quarters
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 182 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: The living quarters of a plantation whose crop failed for good when the drainage silted.
why.siteAdvantages: Built as one long row on the driest line available, which is now the only walkable line through the swamp there.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; people walk through it because the row is the path.
why.pressures: The row is being used as a road by the descendants of the people who were housed in it, without comment.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down for materials if the materials were worth anything.

places.hook: Built as one long row on the driest line available, which is now the only walkable line through the swamp there

places.name: Pass Shelter
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 395 m from the nearest route; no free 'headland' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: The upland pass out of the fringe kills people in the wrong month — not with cold but with wind-driven rain and no cover for two hours in either direction — so the road authority built a hard shelter at the worst point and then stopped maintaining it.
why.siteAdvantages: The one place on the pass with a rock back and no run-off channel above it; every alternative is a stream bed in a storm.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. It is occupied by whoever is caught out, which in the bad months is several parties at once who would not otherwise share a fire.
why.pressures: The door is gone and the fire-store is whatever the last party left; the tradition of leaving fuel holds, but only just, and the shelter's book of names is the fringe's only record of who was on the pass and when.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a genuine death trap the first winter the fuel tradition broke, and everyone using it knows the arithmetic.

hardConstraints: a rock back with no run-off above it
places.hook: The one place on the pass with a rock back and no run-off channel above it; every alternative is a stream bed in a storm

places.name: The Quiet Pit
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 77 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Argonians build no prisons, so where the Owing needs to hold someone it uses a pit and calls it waiting.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry storage pit at the back of a broker's yard, roofed and grated, invisible from the road.
why.occupantsMotive: The brokers hold debtors here for a day or two until the Owing is transferred, which is legal and looks like nothing else.
why.pressures: Somebody was held for eleven days last year and the village has not stopped talking about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be filled in the week a court ruled that waiting is imprisonment.

places.hook: A dry storage pit at the back of a broker's yard, roofed and grated, invisible from the road

places.name: The Ravine Doors
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 832 m from the nearest route; no free 'gorge' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.guar-holding-of-the-nine-bells (+0.54).

why.founding: Where the rim rivers cut deep, the only flat ground is on the walls, so a community learned to live sideways.
why.siteAdvantages: A gorge wall with a natural bedding plane running along it at two levels — the shelf is the street.
why.occupantsMotive: They live here because the gorge is defensible against everything except the river, and the river is predictable.
why.pressures: The lower shelf floods in a bad year and the upper shelf cannot hold everyone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move to the rim if the lower shelf were lost, and lose half its people to the lowlands in the process.

hardConstraints: a continuous bedding shelf on a gorge wall
places.hook: A gorge wall with a natural bedding plane running along it at two levels — the shelf is the street

places.name: The Ring of Nine Wells
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 450 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid ring of well stones, built by the exiles who came east out of Cyrodiil and set their wells where the ground was highest.
why.siteAdvantages: A broad low dome of firm ground with sightlines between all nine positions — the only such ground in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the local villages use the ring as a place to meet and refuse to sleep in it.
why.pressures: Three wells still charge at dusk and six do not, and the Synod would very much like to know why.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a Synod compound the week Gideon's council granted a lease.

places.hook: A broad low dome of firm ground with sightlines between all nine positions — the only such ground in the west

places.name: Rests-The-Walkers
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 404 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.cartwrights-cross (+0.94).

why.founding: Nisswo walk, and walking priests need houses at walking intervals along the pilgrim road.
why.siteAdvantages: Half a day from Glenbridge, at the point where the road leaves the firm ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The resident Nisswo hears the road's confessions, which are mostly about money.
why.pressures: The road's Imperial travellers keep mistaking the house for an inn and being fed anyway.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be kept up by the pilgrims themselves if the Nisswo ever left.

hardConstraints: half a day's walk from the shrine
places.hook: Half a day from Glenbridge, at the point where the road leaves the firm ground

places.name: Old Locks
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 313 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger.

why.founding: The Second Empire tried to make the Onkobra navigable to the uplands with a staircase of stone locks.
why.siteAdvantages: At the reach where the river drops fastest — the only place locks would have been needed and the worst place to build them.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the villages downstream fish the pools the ruined chambers make.
why.pressures: The masonry is a millennium older than the Imperial work below and visibly better, which nobody comments on.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worth rebuilding if anyone wanted freight in the uplands, and nobody does.

places.hook: At the reach where the river drops fastest — the only place locks would have been needed and the worst place to build them

places.name: The Second Hearth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 16 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Argonians raised outside a Hist's reach have nowhere to go home to; on the Imperial fringe there are more of them than anywhere but the ports.
why.siteAdvantages: Close enough to Gideon for work, far enough that nobody has to explain themselves twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because the settlement is the only place their gloor-faded skin is unremarkable.
why.pressures: The interior villages call them lukiul and mean it; Hissmir's pilgrimage is a two-week walk they cannot all make.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty towards Hissmir if the League ever funded the journey — a live quest lever.

places.hook: Close enough to Gideon for work, far enough that nobody has to explain themselves twice a day

places.name: Sermon Road Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 919 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-turned-out (+0.51).

why.founding: Glenbridge cannot house everyone who comes for the sermon, so the overflow camps a mile short and walks in at dawn.
why.siteAdvantages: A flat river meadow with water, firewood and no landlord.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims camp here because arriving at dawn is considered better; the innkeepers price the difference.
why.pressures: Foreign pilgrims and Nisswo pilgrims camp at opposite ends and neither will say why.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a village if the sermon ever drew a permanent crowd, and Glenbridge would fight it.

hardConstraints: a mile short of a pilgrimage site
places.hook: A flat river meadow with water, firewood and no landlord

places.name: The Shaking House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 630 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.comes-back-slowly (+0.49).

why.founding: The marsh gives travellers fevers that villages will not risk, so the sick are put somewhere apart and tended anyway.
why.siteAdvantages: Downwind and downstream of the village, on its own spit, with clean water carried in.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper is a survivor of swamp rot who cannot catch it again and knows it.
why.pressures: The village pays in food and never visits; the keeper's own family have not crossed the spit in nine years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be burned and rebuilt fifty metres along at the first sign of anything the keeper does not recognise.

hardConstraints: downwind and downstream of a settlement
places.hook: Downwind and downstream of the village, on its own spit, with clean water carried in

places.name: Door-That-Stayed-Shut
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 444 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on sightline, remote, parent.

why.founding: A xanmeer deliberately closed by its own people, with its traps live and its contents undisturbed.
why.siteAdvantages: Low ground that has since half-drowned, so the sealed door is now at water level and the upper terraces are an island.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it; the nearest village knows it is there and treats knowing as sufficient.
why.pressures: Water is getting in below the seal, which will eventually open it from underneath.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become the west's most dangerous place the day the water finished the job.

places.hook: Low ground that has since half-drowned, so the sealed door is now at water level and the upper terraces are an island

places.name: The Silent Halls
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 462 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, submerged, remote.

why.founding: A Merethic xanmeer opened long ago and taken over by the Sul-Xan, who use its chambers to keep what their snares catch.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep stone below the water table: cool, dark, and quiet enough that the name is literal.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep it because a soul-store needs walls; nobody contests it because the tribes will not enter a xanmeer that has been broken.
why.pressures: The mechanism floor still works, and the Sul-Xan do not understand it; the Four Winds want the place burned.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a tended xanmeer again if a tribe with a claim ever took it back and closed it.

hardConstraints: a lower chamber below water table
places.hook: Deep stone below the water table: cool, dark, and quiet enough that the name is literal

places.name: The Snowline Cell
places.whySiteWon: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 655 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: Above the marsh's ceiling there is cold, dry air and no disease, and one order of ascetics has decided that is the point.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest saddle on the western rim, where snow lies for a few weeks a year — the only cold ground in Argonia.
why.occupantsMotive: Two ascetics winter here to prove that an Argonian can, which is a theological claim, not a boast.
why.pressures: One of them is dying of the cold and both are treating that as evidence.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be empty in a decade unless the practice attracts a third.

places.hook: The highest saddle on the western rim, where snow lies for a few weeks a year — the only cold ground in Argonia

places.name: The Standing Mist
places.whySiteWon: gorge in upland hills (danger band 3), 71 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A cold-air hollow on the rim where the mist forms every night and does not lift until midday.
why.siteAdvantages: A box canyon with a spring in it: cold water, still air, no through-draught.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; two villages graze its edges and neither will take stock into it before noon.
why.pressures: Things are lost in it regularly, including two people in the last decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be ordinary ground if the spring ever failed, and the villages would be sorry.

hardConstraints: a closed hollow with a cold spring
places.hook: A box canyon with a spring in it: cold water, still air, no through-draught

places.name: Holds-The-Stone
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 1018 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: The Ca-Uxith were charged by their Hist with watching the Rockgrove xanmeer, and a duty that specific needs a village next to it; the tribe has held this ground for as long as the charge has existed, which is longer than anyone can date.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm shelf before the geyser field, close enough to see the xanmeer's upper courses and far enough that the ground does not vent under the houses.
why.occupantsMotive: The stone-talkers do the actual work — reading the ruin's stone for the cracks the geysers open and packing them before the ruin comes apart. It is preservation as a religious obligation, done with clay and patience.
why.pressures: The Sul-Xan raid camp sits on the ruin the Ca-Uxith are sworn to keep, and the tribe has no means to remove them; the geyser field is getting louder, and the elders disagree about whether that is the ruin's fault or the tribe's.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the xanmeer collapsed, the charge would end and the tribe would have no reason to be here at all — which is a thing several of the young ones have started saying aloud.

hardConstraints: firm ground clear of the vents
line of sight to the xanmeer
places.hook: The last firm shelf before the geyser field, close enough to see the xanmeer's upper courses and far enough that the ground does not vent under the houses

places.name: The Sunk Lane
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 267 m from the nearest route; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger.

why.founding: The burn country's peat burned out from below in places, and where the roof went the ground simply left.
why.siteAdvantages: One of the province's very few true sinkholes, opened within living memory across an old cart lane.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody uses it; the lane now ends at it, and the ruts run right up to the lip on both sides.
why.pressures: It is still widening, slowly, and the villages measure it with a stake each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would swallow the last of the lane within a generation.

hardConstraints: an open sinkhole with a rim
places.hook: One of the province's very few true sinkholes, opened within living memory across an old cart lane

places.name: The Turned-Out
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 315 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-sermon-road-camp (+0.51).

why.founding: When an Owing is called in against a household's land, the household is not imprisoned — it is simply outside.
why.siteAdvantages: On the verge of the road within sight of the fields they worked, because that is where the brokers put them out.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay in sight deliberately: leaving would be taken as abandoning the claim.
why.pressures: It is the third winter; two families have gone to Gideon and not come back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end tomorrow if the estate voided one ledger — which is precisely why it does not.

hardConstraints: on a public verge in sight of the lost holding
places.hook: On the verge of the road within sight of the fields they worked, because that is where the brokers put them out

places.name: The Two Lamps
places.whySiteWon: summit in border mountains (danger band 3), 779 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on sightline, region, landform.

why.founding: A hermit who wanted to be unreachable and then, having achieved it, hung a lamp out for anyone who tried.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench forty metres up a ravine wall, reachable by one climb and no path.
why.occupantsMotive: He is here to be alone; the second lamp is for a person he expects and who has not come.
why.pressures: He is old, the climb is not getting easier, and the villages below have begun to worry aloud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a shrine within a year of his death, which he knows and dislikes.

hardConstraints: a bench reachable only by climbing
places.hook: A cliff bench forty metres up a ravine wall, reachable by one climb and no path

places.name: Vellum Estate
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 129 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.ninth-milestone-house (+0.44).

why.founding: An Archein-era estate that survived the end of slavery by converting its slaves into Owing debtors on paper.
why.siteAdvantages: Good drained land on the river terrace, held in one block because it was never divided.
why.occupantsMotive: The estate house holds the ledgers, and the ledgers are the only reason anyone still works the land.
why.pressures: The Chainbreakers know the estate exists; so does the courthouse; the ledgers are technically lawful.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would dissolve overnight if a court ever voided inherited Owings — which is a quest, not a rumour.

hardConstraints: one undivided block of good land
an estate house with a strong room
places.hook: Good drained land on the river terrace, held in one block because it was never divided

places.name: The White Throat
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 181 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
