why.founding: Where a rim river drops twenty metres it has cut back into the rock and left a room behind the water.
why.siteAdvantages: The undercut is deep enough to stand in and dry enough to keep things in.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; smugglers and one hermit have both used it and left different rubbish.
why.pressures: The fall's flow doubles after rain and the chamber floods to knee height.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a shrine in a province with fewer waterfalls; here it is simply a good room.

places.hook: The undercut is deep enough to stand in and dry enough to keep things in

places.name: White Hill Camp
places.whySiteWon: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 17 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Where an antiquities market exists, people will camp above the graves that supply it.
why.siteAdvantages: Just over the ridge from the cairn field, out of sight of the valley track and upwind of the smell of their own camp.
why.occupantsMotive: They are here for glass beads, which are small, light, and worth a season's wages in Leyawiin.
why.pressures: The Collections dig pays better and asks questions; two of this camp have already crossed over.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move to the next dead people the month the beads ran out.

hardConstraints: out of sight of a route
within an hour of a robbable site
places.hook: Just over the ridge from the cairn field, out of sight of the valley track and upwind of the smell of their own camp

places.name: Twyllbek Crown
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 849 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, sightline, hinterland.

why.founding: The Barsaebic compound at Twyllbek has one block whose upper courses are still sound and whose collapsed stair has left the outside face climbable — so the ruin's real content is not inside it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: The block stands on the compound's high corner, which is enough elevation to clear the scrub and see the Blackwood road for four kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. Treasure-hunters, couriers cutting a corner and one persistent Collections surveyor all use the top for their own reasons.
why.pressures: The climbable face is climbable because it is failing; two courses have gone in the last decade and the route changes each time.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would stop existing as a place at all if the face came down, and the only people who would notice are the couriers.

hardConstraints: a standing ruin block with a failing climbable face
places.hook: The block stands on the compound's high corner, which is enough elevation to clear the scrub and see the Blackwood road for four kilometres

places.name: Twyllbek Ruins
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 1009 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid compound from the exile centuries, close enough to Gideon that the city's antiquities trade starts here.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry terrace over a spring — Ayleid siting logic, and the reason Gideon's diggers keep coming back.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers want stones with light in them; the Collections chapter wants the same stones back; both are here most months.
why.pressures: Every season of digging takes more of the wall; the Barsaebic layer is being consumed to prove it existed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be protected properly if Gideon's council ever thought a ruin was worth a guard.

places.hook: A dry terrace over a spring — Ayleid siting logic, and the reason Gideon's diggers keep coming back

places.name: Culvert Line
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 35 m from the nearest route; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The correction to the embankment: a line of stone culverts cut and dressed on site, then never laid.
why.siteAdvantages: The stone was dressed where it was quarried, next to the line it was meant to serve.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; squatters took the dressed blocks for foundations until the tribes made stone-taking a quarrel.
why.pressures: Post-Duskfall, building in dead stone is a moral error here, so the blocks sit where they were left.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would vanish in a decade if anyone with a use for stone lived nearby.

hardConstraints: a line of dressed but unlaid stone
places.hook: The stone was dressed where it was quarried, next to the line it was meant to serve

places.name: Weighed Cart
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 346 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: Gideon's council put a tower where the road forks for the clay pits, because the pits' output is the one export it can measure.
why.siteAdvantages: A knoll commanding both forks and the river landing below them.
why.occupantsMotive: The tower's clerk is paid on what he records, so he records everything.
why.pressures: The potters route half their carts round it by night and everyone knows.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pointless if the clay bank moved, which it does every generation.

hardConstraints: a rise with a view of both branches
places.hook: A knoll commanding both forks and the river landing below them

places.name: Westfield
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 44 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: Argonian villagers took up field agriculture from their Imperial neighbours and now grow it better than they do.
why.siteAdvantages: Temperate grassland on the saddle's western apron: the only large stretch of arable in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm because grain sells in Gideon at whatever price they ask in a bad year.
why.pressures: The fields are held in common and the Imperial grants overlap them on paper; nobody has tested it in court.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fight, in court or otherwise, the first time somebody did.

places.hook: Temperate grassland on the saddle's western apron: the only large stretch of arable in the west

places.name: Low Fen House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 55 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The College of Whispers works where nobody watches, and the fen edge is the least watched habitable ground near Gideon.
why.siteAdvantages: A stilt house over standing water, reachable by one pole-punt and no path at all.
why.occupantsMotive: They study Hist-sap chemistry and say they study hydrology.
why.pressures: The village that ferries them has begun to ask what the barrels are for.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be gone overnight, house and all, if the question were ever pressed properly.

places.hook: A stilt house over standing water, reachable by one pole-punt and no path at all

places.name: Xi-Tsei
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 709 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.open-door-at-the-saddle (+1.18).

why.founding: The ground where a whole community was killed in 1E 2820, and where the Sul-Xan trace their grievance from. Lore:Xi-Tsei puts the site on the southern strip of Blackwood, which is administered as Cyrodiil; we place it inside our province deliberately, because the border there has moved more than once and the massacre is Argonian history wherever the line currently runs.
why.siteAdvantages: An open flat between two ridges — the only place in the Blackwood where an army could be made to stand and fight.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the Sul-Xan come annually and leave marks; the Four Winds come annually and remove them.
why.pressures: Two peoples curate the same field in opposite directions, and both editions are visible.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be settled again only if both traditions lapsed, which neither will.

hardConstraints: an open flat with two ridge flanks
places.hook: An open flat between two ridges — the only place in the Blackwood where an army could be made to stand and fight

places.name: Blackrose
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'blackrose' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Built by the Lilmothiit in a lake where three rivers converge; rebuilt by the Empire after 1E 2837 and held since by whoever holds the island core.
why.siteAdvantages: The hinge of the south: Murkwood's water from the north-east, Oliis Bay from the south, eastern Blackwood from the west, and Bramman's concealed river out to Topal Bay.
why.occupantsMotive: Toll and transit revenue, and whatever comes out of the Rose. Many have entered its walls; the city keeps the ones who do not leave.
why.pressures: It remembers raising an army against the Third Empire and remembers a battlemage breaking it with a single spell; it distrusts magic and outsiders in that order.
why.wouldChangeIf: Whoever took the island core would take the whole southern route network with it, which is why the core has changed hands four times.

hardConstraints: island in standing water at a confluence
places.hook: The hinge of the south: Murkwood's water from the north-east, Oliis Bay from the south, eastern Blackwood from the west, and Bramman's concealed river out to Topal Bay

places.name: Speaks-Below-The-Water
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 256 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.lake-submerged-xanmeer (+0.90).

why.founding: Blackrose's Hist stands in the lake rather than in the city, and the lake rose over it — the register's drowned tree.
why.siteAdvantages: It grew on the island's old shore; three centuries of raised lake level put six metres of water over its crown.
why.occupantsMotive: Tenders dive to it. The city has no other tree and will not plant one, because planting one would be a judgement on this one.
why.pressures: An underwater Hist cannot be communed with in any of the usual ways, and the tenders have improvised a practice nobody else recognises.
why.wouldChangeIf: Lowering the lake would expose it — and it is not agreed whether that would save it or kill it.

places.hook: It grew on the island's old shore; three centuries of raised lake level put six metres of water over its crown

places.name: Blackrose Prison
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 140 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Built by Potentate Versidue-Shaie's battlemage Pelladil Direnni out of the rubble of the ancient Lilmothiit city, by an army of stone atronachs, in a single day, a day's march south of Blackrose.
why.siteAdvantages: Marsh on every side and one causeway: the Imperial siting rule for this province, executed perfectly.
why.occupantsMotive: Prison-born families three generations deep who hold it as their inheritance, plus exiles and outlaws; they resent being called a prison and have a real argument that they are not one.
why.pressures: Umbriel left something in the lower levels that nobody has cleared; the Chainbreakers want the place opened; Blackrose wants the toll it takes on the south road.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a genuine settlement, and everybody who benefits from its reputation knows it.

places.hook: Marsh on every side and one causeway: the Imperial siting rule for this province, executed perfectly

places.name: Bramman's Head
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in deep river corridor (danger band 3), 604 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, danger, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.feeder-portage (+0.95).

why.founding: The inland end of the concealed river a First-Era fleet sailed up from near Soulrest: where Bramman's water finally meets the Blackrose lakes.
why.siteAdvantages: A screened lagoon head with just enough depth for a laden hull, and a bank firm enough to tranship on.
why.occupantsMotive: A small permanent crew who keep the head open, charge for the last mile, and have never let the route be charted.
why.pressures: Blackrose's toll authority knows the head exists and has never been able to find its mouth.
why.wouldChangeIf: Charting the river would make Blackrose a sea port and destroy the pilots at both ends.

places.hook: A screened lagoon head with just enough depth for a laden hull, and a bank firm enough to tranship on

places.name: Open House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Blackrose Chainbreakers' shelter for people who have come out of the Rose, an Owing, or a toll pit, and have nowhere that will take them.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the toll line, on water, with two exits and no fixed sign.
why.occupantsMotive: Board, work and legal help; the Chainbreakers' whole practical programme in one building.
why.pressures: Two of the powers they oppose fund half their neighbours, and the shelter is watched constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single violent incident here would let the city close it lawfully.

places.hook: Outside the toll line, on water, with two exits and no fixed sign

places.name: Bare Lake
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 159 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The lake's shallow southern arm empties for six weeks every dry season, exposing four square kilometres of bed that is underwater the rest of the year.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide flat arm barely a metre deep, with an outlet that drops below its sill in the dry.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone. The drawdown is a local event: the whole shore walks out onto the bed and takes what the year has dropped.
why.pressures: Grave-stakes from a drowned burial ground stand exposed during the drawdown, which forces an annual argument about what may be taken.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter cycle would end the drawdown and the whole annual custom with it.

places.hook: A wide flat arm barely a metre deep, with an outlet that drops below its sill in the dry

places.name: The Windlass Reckoning
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 276 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.bramman-head (+0.95).

why.founding: The western feeder has a two-hundred-metre rock narrows no laden hull can pass, so hulls are dragged around it.
why.siteAdvantages: A low saddle beside the narrows where a greased timber slipway can be laid on a workable gradient.
why.occupantsMotive: A drag crew with a windlass, paid by the hull, who also control who goes upstream and when.
why.pressures: The crew's monopoly is total and their maintenance of the slipway is minimal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Blasting the narrows would open the western route and end the crew.

places.hook: A low saddle beside the narrows where a greased timber slipway can be laid on a workable gradient

places.name: Holding Fields, Cordon Three
places.whySiteWon: island in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 546 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: Lilmothiit refugees fleeing the Knahaten Flu in Murkmire fled inland toward Blackrose, and their fate is unclear. This is where Blackrose stopped them.
why.siteAdvantages: On the southern approach at the last narrows before the lake, where a cordon could actually be held.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody now. It was a village-sized pen with a fence, a gate, a ration store and a burial ground that is larger than the village.
why.pressures: This is the answer to the unclear fate of a whole people, and Blackrose has never once discussed it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Anyone who published the ration ledgers would make the city's founding families answer for it.

places.hook: On the southern approach at the last narrows before the lake, where a cordon could actually be held

places.name: Ash-Hand
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 88 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, hinterland, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.vampiric-cloud-ground (+0.49).

why.founding: A Kothringi village of the people canon places in the Blackrose region, emptied by the Knahaten Flu in a single season.
why.siteAdvantages: A river terrace with a landing — good ground, which is why it was never resettled by anyone superstitious.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Argonian villages nearby keep its boundary marked and do not cross it.
why.pressures: The Flu is the founding trauma of half the province's demography, and this is what it actually looks like on the ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: Proof that the ground is safe would put a village back on it within a year.

hardConstraints: coastal and riverine — they were sea-going
places.hook: A river terrace with a landing — good ground, which is why it was never resettled by anyone superstitious

places.name: Lake Meer
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.blackrose-drowned-hist (+0.90).

why.founding: A xanmeer that stood on the lake's old floor before the water rose, now entirely submerged and entirely intact.
why.siteAdvantages: Eighteen metres down in cold clear water, with its terraces stepping up to within six metres of the surface.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing. Its doorways are sealed by silt at the base and open at the third terrace.
why.pressures: It is the deepest reachable structure in the south and the divers who work it treat it as a different profession from lake salvage.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt slump would close the open terrace and seal it entirely.

places.hook: Eighteen metres down in cold clear water, with its terraces stepping up to within six metres of the surface

places.name: Robbed City
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 285 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.kothringi-ruin-basin (+1.50).

why.founding: The ancient Lilmothiit city Blackrose stands on and was quarried out of: canon says the Rose was built from its rubble in a single day.
why.siteAdvantages: A whole vanished city's stone lying within a day of the site that needed it — which is why the Rose exists at all.
why.occupantsMotive: No inheritors: the Lilmothiit died of the Knahaten Flu. Blackrose's own foundations are its remains.
why.pressures: What is left is a robbed-out ground plan, and every carved block in the district can be matched back to a socket here.
why.wouldChangeIf: A systematic survey would reconstruct a lost people's city from the buildings it was stolen into.

places.hook: A whole vanished city's stone lying within a day of the site that needed it — which is why the Rose exists at all

places.name: Longmont
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.lake-submerged-xanmeer (+1.08).

why.founding: Canon-named as Blackrose's south-western neighbour: a lake-shore village on the approach, and the last stop before the city's toll gates.
why.siteAdvantages: A long shallow flat on the lake's south-west shore, poleable all year and outside the city's wall line.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything bound for Blackrose by land is broken to boats here, by people who are not the city and charge less than it.
why.pressures: Blackrose has twice tried to bring Longmont inside its toll regime and twice found the village simply stops handling freight.
why.wouldChangeIf: Absorption into the city's toll regime would move the whole trade to Rockspring in one season.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
places.hook: A long shallow flat on the lake's south-west shore, poleable all year and outside the city's wall line

places.name: Murkwood Verge
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 3), 392 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The forest that ever moves, last located north-east of Blackrose; findable only via the Conclave of Baal at Stormhold reading the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet.
why.siteAdvantages: A stretch of deep marsh north-east of the lake where the tree line is wrong on every survey and no two surveys agree.
why.occupantsMotive: Medusas and fellrunners. Nothing that lives here is from anywhere.
why.pressures: The verge is where the forest is *now*; the villages within a day of it keep a tally of where it has been.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its movement is off-screen lore between visits — the verge is a fixed site whose surroundings tell you it has moved.

places.hook: A stretch of deep marsh north-east of the lake where the tree line is wrong on every survey and no two surveys agree

places.name: Third Generation
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 181 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Prison-born households who left the Rose and cannot join any village, because none of them has ever been near a Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: An island in the marsh two hours off the causeway: defensible, unclaimed, and nobody else wants it.
why.occupantsMotive: They are building a community from nothing, with no tree, no clan and no funeral rite that anyone recognises.
why.pressures: They will not go back to the Rose and cannot go forward to a village; the pilgrimage to Hissmir is a fantasy at this distance.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village willing to sponsor them into tree-access would dissolve the settlement in a season.

hardConstraints: wherever they were allowed to stop
places.hook: An island in the marsh two hours off the causeway: defensible, unclaimed, and nobody else wants it

places.name: Welloc's Lines
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 85 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Thrown up around the city when Blackrose rebelled against the Third Empire and raised an army; abandoned when Empress Morihatha's battlemage Welloc broke the rebellion with a spell instead of a siege.
why.siteAdvantages: Sited on the dry ground commanding all three approaches — competent, complete, and never used.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Grazing now, with the ditch profiles perfectly legible from any rise.
why.pressures: A city that remembers raising an army looks at these lines every day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. The earth stays. That is what makes it a monument.

hardConstraints: dry ground with a view of the target
places.hook: Sited on the dry ground commanding all three approaches — competent, complete, and never used

places.name: Rockspring
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 411 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon-named as Blackrose's north-western neighbour, built along a natural levee on the western feeder around the one hard spring in the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: A levee crest a metre above every recorded flood, with a rock spring that runs clean when the whole basin is brown.
why.occupantsMotive: The spring is the asset; in a bad year the village sells water to boats and does not apologise for it.
why.pressures: Longmont's freight trade is the one they want and cannot get, because the feeder is too shallow for laden hulls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dredged feeder would make Rockspring the western freight village and end Longmont's monopoly.

hardConstraints: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
places.hook: A levee crest a metre above every recorded flood, with a rock spring that runs clean when the whole basin is brown

places.name: Rose Lower Levels
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 491 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Rose's lowest levels flooded when the marsh took the foundations, and what Umbriel left in 4E 48 is still down there.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the water table, sealed by a stair the prison-born families bricked up two generations ago.
why.occupantsMotive: The undead. The families above will confirm nothing and have never opened the stair.
why.pressures: The Chainbreakers' bone claims include people who died down there; the families' claim to legitimacy depends on the stair staying shut.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a settlement and end its reputation — which is exactly what the families are frightened of.

places.hook: Below the water table, sealed by a stair the prison-born families bricked up two generations ago

places.name: Vaunting
places.whySiteWon: ford in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Rose needed feeding for twelve centuries, and the supply town the Empire built for that outlived both the Empire and the prison's official function.
why.siteAdvantages: On the causeway road at the last firm ground before the marsh, with a barge landing and a walled magazine.
why.occupantsMotive: It still supplies the Rose, now on commercial terms, and the arrangement is the town's entire economy.
why.pressures: Half the town is descended from prison staff and half from released prisoners, and the two halves marry but do not forget.
why.wouldChangeIf: Emptying the Rose would end the town within a decade.

hardConstraints: at a crossing or a road
places.hook: On the causeway road at the last firm ground before the marsh, with a barge landing and a walled magazine

places.name: Three Gates
places.whySiteWon: ford in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 106 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Blackrose lives on three-river transit and tolls; the toll town sits at the confluence itself, outside the walls, where all three routes must pass.
why.siteAdvantages: The confluence: no cargo reaches the lake from any direction without passing this point.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian toll-holding families' compact that predates the current city government and has outlasted three of them.
why.pressures: Everyone who trades in the south hates it and pays it; Threewater exists specifically to avoid it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the compact would give the city direct control of its own revenue for the first time.

places.hook: The confluence: no cargo reaches the lake from any direction without passing this point

places.name: Given Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 348 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.kothringi-ruin-basin (+0.49).

why.founding: Where Welloc's vampiric cloud displaced the rebels' strength and skill to their opponents, and the Blackrose army stopped being an army in about a minute.
why.siteAdvantages: The open ground north of the city where the rebel army formed up, chosen by them, which is the part nobody has forgiven.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Grave-singers refuse to work it: they say the dead here are not diminished but *emptied*, which is a different problem.
why.pressures: Blackrose's distrust of battlemages is a policy, not a prejudice, and this field is the reason.
why.wouldChangeIf: A grave-singer willing to stake this field would end a two-century-old civic wound.

hardConstraints: where an army could deploy — rare here
places.hook: The open ground north of the city where the rebel army formed up, chosen by them, which is the part nobody has forgiven

places.name: Threewater
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where the western feeder from eastern Blackwood meets the lake system, a market grew for everyone unwilling to pay Blackrose's gate toll.
why.siteAdvantages: A river junction with firm banks on three sides and enough water for laden hulls in every season but the driest.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists to be cheaper than Blackrose, and its whole civic life is organised around staying that way.
why.pressures: Blackrose has twice sent 'inspectors'; the town has twice paid them and continued.
why.wouldChangeIf: An enforced toll here would collapse the market back into the city within two years.

hardConstraints: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
places.hook: A river junction with firm banks on three sides and enough water for laden hulls in every season but the driest

places.name: Alten Meerhleel
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 186 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, navigable; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's outsider-facing port north-west of Lilmoth: a working two-culture port below city scale, where an Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. With Lilmoth destroyed for a century and a half the bay's outside trade came here, and enough of it stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Slow deep water inside the bar, deep enough for a laden hull to lie off and be worked by lighters, with firm enough margin behind it for a warehouse row — an *alten-* name, meaning outsiders were always the point.
why.occupantsMotive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports; the customs presence is one clerk and a tariff shed nobody staffs, which is the entire commercial proposition.
why.pressures: Now that Lilmoth is rebuilt the two ports are direct rivals, and Meerhleel's whole advantage is that it asks nothing — an advantage that Corimont, the province's actual free port, holds far more securely.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Lilmoth's council ever dropped its tariffs, Meerhleel would lose the only reason anyone sails past a real harbour.

hardConstraints: sheltered navigable water off the legal lanes
places.hook: Slow deep water inside the bar, deep enough for a laden hull to lie off and be worked by lighters, with firm enough margin behind it for a warehouse row — an *alten-* name, meaning outsiders were always the point

places.name: Ashfield
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 368 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Founded on the ash-enriched firm lowland left by the Great Burn, which turned out to grow food better than the forest had.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry firm ground, deep burn ash, and the coast road for a market.
why.occupantsMotive: Mixed Argonian and Imperial-descended households farming the one soil in the district that improved.
why.pressures: The ash is finite; yields have been falling for three generations and nobody says so out loud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exhausted soil would empty it within twenty years.

places.hook: Dry firm ground, deep burn ash, and the coast road for a market

places.name: Ashroot
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 864 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The nearest Hist village to Soulrest, and the reason the burn country still has Argonians in it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise that the peat fire went around, with its tree's roots reaching water the burn never reached.
why.occupantsMotive: They kept the tree alive through the Burn and consider that the defining fact of their village.
why.pressures: Soulrest's four claimants all court them, and the village has learned to answer all four the same way.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the tree would disperse the village into the city within a generation.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
places.hook: A rise that the peat fire went around, with its tree's roots reaching water the burn never reached

places.name: Sees-No-Root
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 266 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.stripped-village-north (+0.55).

why.founding: A village whose Hist died with its mnemic egg unrecovered, and which has organised its entire remaining life around that fact.
why.siteAdvantages: Unchanged good ground — they stayed, which is the unusual decision.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the empty enclosure, keep the offices, and keep telling the memories aloud because there is nothing left to hold them.
why.pressures: The children are leaving for Lilmoth; the recitation takes six days and fewer people can do it each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recovered egg would restore the village at a stroke, and every treasure-hunter in Murkmire knows that.

places.hook: Unchanged good ground — they stayed, which is the unusual decision

places.name: Bramman's Screen
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 88 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The seaward mouth of the narrow winding river Red Bramman escaped the Alessian navy through, encased in dense mangrove.
why.siteAdvantages: Four channel mouths open off the same bay; only one carries water at the top of the tide, and only for about ninety minutes.
why.occupantsMotive: The pilots who know the run sell the knowledge and never write it down; a wrong channel strands a hull until the next tide.
why.pressures: It is a hidden route, not a scheduled lane — placing a marked ferry service on it would destroy the thing that makes it worth anything.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt pulse could close it, or open a second, and the pilots' monopoly would end with it.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water
places.hook: Four channel mouths open off the same bay; only one carries water at the top of the tide, and only for about ninety minutes

places.name: Bright-Throat Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 439 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.root-gallery-murkmire (+0.37).

why.founding: Canon's hospitable, artisan, alliance-brokering tribe, on the cliffs above Oliis Bay — the village that knits the region back together after each catastrophe.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock bench above the bay with a single stair to a beach landing: defensible, dry, and commanding the whole approach to Lilmoth.
why.occupantsMotive: Diplomacy and craft. Their Listening-Tree and its chimes are why other tribes come to them rather than the reverse.
why.pressures: Everyone in Murkmire wants Bright-Throat's endorsement, which makes neutrality expensive to maintain.
why.wouldChangeIf: Taking a side in the Lilmoth–An-Xileel quarrel would cost them the role they are famous for.

places.hook: A rock bench above the bay with a single stair to a beach landing: defensible, dry, and commanding the whole approach to Lilmoth

places.name: Chasepoint
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 38 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Imperial road stage east of Soulrest, canon-named as its neighbour; the Legion built it, the wreck-salvage families kept it.
why.siteAdvantages: Last firm ground before the coast road turns inland; a shingle beach below that catches everything the Southern Sea loses.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage rights are hereditary here and jealously counted; the stage's stable block is now a drying shed for recovered cordage.
why.pressures: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries; the roof is Argonian thatch on Imperial walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A revived coast road under a real toll authority would make it a proper town again.

places.hook: Last firm ground before the coast road turns inland; a shingle beach below that catches everything the Southern Sea loses

places.name: The Paid Arch
places.whySiteWon: ford in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 66 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Imperial stone arch on the coast road that a local family has been collecting on since the Legion stopped.
why.siteAdvantages: The one crossing of a tidal creek that does not require a boat within four miles.
why.occupantsMotive: The toll is small, consistent and entirely without legal basis; it buys maintenance that genuinely happens.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council would like the revenue and has no way to take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapsed arch would end the family, the toll and the road in one night.

hardConstraints: spans a channel at its narrowest
places.hook: The one crossing of a tidal creek that does not require a boat within four miles

places.name: Cold Light
places.whySiteWon: islet in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 39 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Imperial harbour works lit the Topal approach for four centuries; the oil contract ended with the province.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest headland on the bay approach, and one of the few structures in the province that breaks the canopy line.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. A Soulrest chandler still bills the council for lamp oil that is never delivered.
why.pressures: The lantern glass is gone; the stair is sound; whoever relights it decides who profits from the bar.
why.wouldChangeIf: Relighting it kills the Long Bar and makes Soulrest's harbour honest.

places.hook: The highest headland on the bay approach, and one of the few structures in the province that breaks the canopy line

places.name: Lights-From-Under
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 170 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A still fen where the water plants light from below all year, which is why the pilgrim route runs through it at night.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow, warm, flow-free basin — the conditions the glow needs, and rare.
why.occupantsMotive: Gatherers take the plants for lamp-jelly; pilgrims cross at night because the fen lights the way.
why.pressures: Harvesting dims it; the villages ration the take by an argument nobody enjoys having.
why.wouldChangeIf: Over-harvest would end both the trade and the route in the same season.

places.hook: A shallow, warm, flow-free basin — the conditions the glow needs, and rare

places.name: Four-Hands Crown
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 55 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A raised hammock's crown given over entirely to the ancestors of the villages around it — the only ground high enough to stay dry in any flood.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest dry ground in a wide floodplain, which makes it the only permanent burial terrace available.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages bury here in four sectors, and the sector boundaries are the oldest agreed lines in the district.
why.pressures: The hammock is running out of terrace and no village will yield an inch of its sector.
why.wouldChangeIf: A flood high enough to reach the crown would be read as a judgement on all four.

hardConstraints: above the flood on a tree-island
places.hook: The highest dry ground in a wide floodplain, which makes it the only permanent burial terrace available

places.name: Tzelvei
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; no free 'island' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village on a tree-island hammock, reached only by water, with its fields on smaller hammocks around it.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry wooded island in permanent marsh, with a ring of satellite hammocks at poling distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Island living gives them the safest ground in the district and the longest journey to market, and they have chosen the former for centuries.
why.pressures: Every child leaves for Lilmoth for a season; roughly half return, and the number is falling.
why.wouldChangeIf: A poling route improvement would connect them to the city and change everything about them.

places.hook: A dry wooded island in permanent marsh, with a ring of satellite hammocks at poling distance

places.name: Head of Tide
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 640 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon puts a river starting just south of Soulrest and running north-east into the interior; this is the last point a sea-going hull can reach on it.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel sill across the channel: deep water below it, poling water above it, and firm banks for transhipment.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything going inland is broken down into canoe loads here, by people who charge for it.
why.pressures: Whoever controls this sill controls the whole interior trade of the south-west, and four parties know that.
why.wouldChangeIf: Dredging the sill would destroy the transhipment trade and enrich the city.

places.hook: A gravel sill across the channel: deep water below it, poling water above it, and firm banks for transhipment

places.name: Hereguard Plantation
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 74 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.teeba-enoo-court (+2.21).

why.founding: Canon's rice estate north of Lilmoth and one of the few places Bretons still live in Argonia; rice is the one crop that works here because it wants the flood.
why.siteAdvantages: A flooding river terrace that ruins any other crop and suits this one exactly.
why.occupantsMotive: A Breton family and Argonian tenant households, bound by a share arrangement that both sides describe differently.
why.pressures: Lilmoth depends on Hereguard rice, which gives the tenants more leverage every year and the family less.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tenant refusal at planting would starve the city, and everyone has done that arithmetic.

hardConstraints: controls a crossing or a landing
places.hook: A flooding river terrace that ruins any other crop and suits this one exactly

places.name: High Junction
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 30 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where four elevated walkways meet above the mangrove, a platform grew that is now a place in its own right.
why.siteAdvantages: The one point at which the whole upper network of this district connects, twelve metres above the water.
why.occupantsMotive: A tea-seller, a chime-relay peg board and a toll nobody formally imposes but everybody pays.
why.pressures: The junction's timbers carry more traffic than they were built for and everybody can feel it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would sever the district's upper network into four dead ends.

places.hook: The one point at which the whole upper network of this district connects, twelve metres above the water

places.name: Waits-For-A-Cutting
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 152 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Lilmoth has a Hist but no native tribe, and a fourth of the people who arrive here have no tree at all; the Fringe is where they end up.
why.siteAdvantages: Just outside the wall on ground the city does not tax and the villages will not claim.
why.occupantsMotive: Mutual aid without kinship — the households here are organised by arrival date, not by clan.
why.pressures: Hissmir is two provinces away in practical terms; most people here will never make the pilgrimage and know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A city grant of tree-access would empty half of it in a month.

hardConstraints: wherever they were allowed to stop
places.hook: Just outside the wall on ground the city does not tax and the villages will not claim

places.name: Root-Sakka
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 624 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.keshu-grove (+1.05).

why.founding: A Murkmire village whose tree speaks clearly and often, which makes it the region's arbiter whether it wants to be or not.
why.siteAdvantages: A river terrace on the Keel-Sakka with deep root-water and a defensible bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Their tree-minder is consulted from three days' travel away, which is a burden the village debates constantly.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's tree does not speak to anyone but its minders; this one speaks to everybody, and the comparison is politically loaded.
why.wouldChangeIf: If their tree fell silent the region would lose its only uncontested voice.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
places.hook: A river terrace on the Keel-Sakka with deep root-water and a defensible bend

places.name: Chuxeth
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 269 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribe that never left its xanmeer, and therefore holds the strongest fortification in southern Murkmire without having built anything.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls, a single water approach, and ancient defences that still work — in a region where everything else is timber.
why.occupantsMotive: They are polite, immovable, and entirely uninterested in Lilmoth's politics or the An-Xileel's.
why.pressures: Every faction in the south has wanted their walls at some point; the working defences are why none has taken them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the vakka mechanisms ever failed, the village would be ordinary overnight.

places.hook: Stone walls, a single water approach, and ancient defences that still work — in a region where everything else is timber

places.name: Xel-Nahkta
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 268 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village in the jungle belt that has refused every outside contact since 4E 48 and enforces the refusal at the boundary.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise with one approach, three days from Lilmoth and unreachable by water.
why.occupantsMotive: They lost a village to something that came from outside and have drawn the obvious conclusion.
why.pressures: Their boundary now crosses a route the guides need, and the guides have started going around.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single successful parley would open the shortest route across the belt.

hardConstraints: defensible approach, often a single crossing
places.hook: A defensible rise with one approach, three days from Lilmoth and unreachable by water

places.name: Ixtaxh Xanmeer
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 846 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The xanmeer the An-Xileel pumped out room by room and held dry with magicks; with them gone the magicks lapsed and the silt returned.
why.siteAdvantages: Sits in standing water west of Lilmoth; only the topmost chamber stands above the silt, exactly as canon first found it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it. Divers go in for what the An-Xileel left behind when the water came back fast.
why.pressures: The lower rooms are silt, not water — a diver can enter them and not find the way out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Another pumping effort would reopen it, and there is no faction left with the will or the singing to do it.

places.hook: Sits in standing water west of Lilmoth; only the topmost chamber stands above the silt, exactly as canon first found it

places.name: Keel-Sakka Landing
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 12 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The first village up the Keel-Sakka river from Lilmoth, where the rainforest road meets poling water.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm channel edge with deep water alongside, on the road out of Lilmoth's north gate.
why.occupantsMotive: They take Lilmoth's freight off the road and put it on the river, and charge for the change of medium.
why.pressures: Bright-Throat's chime-relay reaches here and Lilmoth's writ does not, which suits everyone locally.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cart road up the river would end the village's whole function.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
places.hook: A firm channel edge with deep water alongside, on the road out of Lilmoth's north gate

places.name: Black Fin Grove
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 813 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.hist-village-keel-sakka (+1.05).

why.founding: A grove kept for Keshu the Black Fin, Murkmire's national hero — a hero-Hist grove is what a village does with a person it cannot let go of.
why.siteAdvantages: A stand of old Hist-kin trees on the ground where the story says she mustered, with a spring at the centre.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by rota from four villages, none of which will concede that the grove is any one of theirs.
why.pressures: The story has four incompatible versions and the rota is how the villages avoid resolving it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A definitive account would give the grove to one village and start a feud.

hardConstraints: spring or still water at the root
places.hook: A stand of old Hist-kin trees on the ground where the story says she mustered, with a spring at the centre

places.name: Lighter Flotilla
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 6 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: Lilmoth is built over shallow water and large ships cannot dock, so goods are lightered ashore — and the lighter crews live afloat, between the anchorage and the quay.
why.siteAdvantages: A permanent moored ground in the estuary, half a mile off the quay, out of the tariff line and inside the sheltered water.
why.occupantsMotive: The crews control the only link between deep-water hulls and the city, and they know precisely what that is worth.
why.pressures: A council attempt to license lightering triggered a two-week stoppage that nobody wants to repeat.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dredged deep-water channel would end both the flotilla and the city's leverage over its own trade.

hardConstraints: sheltered saltwater with a reef or bar
places.hook: A permanent moored ground in the estuary, half a mile off the quay, out of the tariff line and inside the sheltered water

places.name: Lilmoth
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'lilmoth' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: A river estuary into Oliis Bay over shallow water; big hulls anchor out and lighter in, which is the whole economy.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; nobody wants a ruler, and the last party that had one killed the city.
why.pressures: Politically hostile to the An-Xileel successor state; commercially essential to a bay that must trade somewhere; built over its own mass grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once — which is why the rules forbid it.

places.hook: A river estuary into Oliis Bay over shallow water; big hulls anchor out and lighter in, which is the whole economy

places.name: Under-Yard
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 322 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Lilmoth stands on a drowned city and salvage from underneath it is a licensed, taxed, entirely respectable trade.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay directly above the deepest of the sunken villas, with a stair down to a landing at water level.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews work the drowned quarter by permit, in pairs, and hand everything to the yard for valuation.
why.pressures: Some of what comes up belongs to families still living, and the yard has to decide that daily.
why.wouldChangeIf: A find of An-Xileel material would turn a trade into a political incident.

places.hook: On the quay directly above the deepest of the sunken villas, with a stair down to a landing at water level

places.name: Long Bar
places.whySiteWon: islet in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 302 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.wraxu-stacks (+1.11).

why.founding: A shoal bar off the salvage coast where a false light has been shown for longer than anyone will admit.
why.siteAdvantages: Two miles of breaking bar on the Southern Sea approach, invisible from the coast road, hidden from Soulrest by the islands.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage families who decided that waiting for wrecks was inefficient; they take the low-profile Southern Sea traders nobody reports missing.
why.pressures: Khajiit crews keep the same lane and have begun to notice; the Soulrest harbour office would have to act if it were ever proved.
why.wouldChangeIf: A working lighthouse on the headland would end it in one season.

places.hook: Two miles of breaking bar on the Southern Sea approach, invisible from the coast road, hidden from Soulrest by the islands

places.name: Moonmarch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 456 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Khajiit moon-sugar landing on the Murkmire coast — the province gazetteer's only Khajiiti place-name, and it is here for a reason.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered landing far enough west of Lilmoth to be outside its tariff and close enough to sell into it.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families left of a dozen; the sugar still lands, in less of it and less often.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's rebuilt council taxes what Moonmarch used to handle untaxed; the trade has moved to Alten Meerhleel.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tariff rise at Lilmoth would refill Moonmarch in a season.

places.hook: A sheltered landing far enough west of Lilmoth to be outside its tariff and close enough to sell into it

places.name: Mudfoot
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A fishing and cockle village on the Topal tidal flat, close enough to Soulrest to sell into it daily.
why.siteAdvantages: Two metres of tide over a firm cockle flat; stilts keep the floors dry and the flat is walkable at low water.
why.occupantsMotive: Sell fresh to the city, sell salted to the coast road, and never owe the council anything.
why.pressures: The city's price is set by buyers who all know each other; the village's answer is to sell early and low.
why.wouldChangeIf: A harbour road extension would turn it into a suburb.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
places.hook: Two metres of tide over a firm cockle flat; stilts keep the floors dry and the flat is walkable at low water

places.name: Xul-Hakka
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 132 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Naga village on the inner channels that raids the Lilmoth road in the dry season and trades with it in the wet.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep channel water on three sides, one poled approach, and reach to both the road and the estuary.
why.occupantsMotive: Raiding here is seasonal economics, not war; the same households trade with the people they robbed four months earlier.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's council has started paying for road escorts, which changes the arithmetic for the first time in a century.
why.wouldChangeIf: A permanent armed escort would force the village into either full trade or full war.

places.hook: Deep channel water on three sides, one poled approach, and reach to both the road and the estuary

places.name: Xul-Vaat
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 86 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village whose whole trade is the dead: staking, tending, reading and repatriating for the whole southern coast.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm peat that holds a stake, central to a dozen villages, and far enough from all of them.
why.occupantsMotive: Every household here holds a grave-office; children learn to read stakes before they learn anything else.
why.pressures: The Owing's dead, Umbriel's dead and White Rose's dead all arrive here eventually, and the ground is filling.
why.wouldChangeIf: A refusal to accept more dead would force a dozen villages to solve the problem themselves.

hardConstraints: soft ground that holds a stake, downwind of everyone
places.hook: Firm peat that holds a stake, central to a dozen villages, and far enough from all of them

places.name: Breathing-Stone
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A maintained air chamber on the submerged route between the estuary and the inner channels — somebody built the bench in it.
why.siteAdvantages: Halfway along a flooded passage too long to swim in one breath, in a natural dome that holds air.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by the divers who use the route: a bench, a slate, a lamp bracket and a rule about leaving oil.
why.pressures: The air is finite and shared; the slate records who is currently below.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the chamber would close the route to everyone but the very best swimmers.

places.hook: Halfway along a flooded passage too long to swim in one breath, in a natural dome that holds air

places.name: Walks-The-Mangrove
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 43 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A mangrove village that grew as a walkway first and a settlement second: the path came, then the houses hung off it.
why.siteAdvantages: A mangrove belt too soft to build on and too dense to boat through, where a raised deck is the only viable form.
why.occupantsMotive: Every household maintains its own span of deck, and the village's shape is the record of who has been diligent.
why.pressures: Three spans are failing and their households have left; the village is branching around the gaps rather than repairing them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A concerted repair would reconnect two halves that are drifting into separate villages.

hardConstraints: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
places.hook: A mangrove belt too soft to build on and too dense to boat through, where a raised deck is the only viable form

places.name: Estuary Stage
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 89 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The estuary is half a mile wide at the road crossing and the ferry is older than the rebuilt city.
why.siteAdvantages: A narrows with hard landings on both sides and slack water twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: A council concession, farmed out annually to the highest bidder, which explains the fare.
why.pressures: The fare rises every year and the boats do not improve.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rival free crossing upstream would break the concession and the council's revenue with it.

hardConstraints: across water too deep or wide to ford
places.hook: A narrows with hard landings on both sides and slack water twice a day

places.name: Half-Day Flat
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 25 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.quinrawl-anchorage (+0.43).

why.founding: Two miles of Oliis Bay flat that can be walked at low water and must be sailed at high, and the difference is ninety minutes.
why.siteAdvantages: It cuts hours off the coast route for anyone who reads the tide correctly; how much flat it uncovers is a consequence of Oliis Bay's tidal amplitude, not a fixed distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Local carriers use it daily; strangers use it once.
why.pressures: The tide comes in across the flat faster than a person walks, from behind.
why.wouldChangeIf: A marked causeway would make it safe and pointless.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water
places.hook: It cuts hours off the coast route for anyone who reads the tide correctly; how much flat it uncovers is a consequence of Oliis Bay's tidal amplitude, not a fixed distance

places.name: Xal-Meht
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 20 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer with no surviving clan, tended instead by the pilgrims who pass it on the way to the Teeth of Sithis.
why.siteAdvantages: On the pilgrim line, with a spring at its foot — the reason the route goes this way at all.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintenance as devotion: each party clears one terrace and moves on.
why.pressures: Pilgrim tending is uneven and sentimental; the terraces nobody likes are being lost.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rerouted pilgrimage would leave it to the forest within thirty years.

places.hook: On the pilgrim line, with a spring at its foot — the reason the route goes this way at all

places.name: Quin'rawl Anchorage
places.whySiteWon: cove in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 104 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.screen-watch (+0.92).

why.founding: Southern Sea crews — a large share of them Khajiit — keep a low profile to avoid Altmer and Maormer warships, so they anchor where no state looks.
why.siteAdvantages: A deep cove behind a headland with two exits, sand holding ground and a freshwater run at its head.
why.occupantsMotive: Half the hulls here carry a Soulrest charter, and all of them carry cargo the charter does not mention.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council both licenses and disowns them, which is a stable arrangement everyone resents.
why.wouldChangeIf: A Dominion sweep of the Southern Sea would scatter it to the mangroves in a week.

hardConstraints: deep approach, hidden from the lane
places.hook: A deep cove behind a headland with two exits, sand holding ground and a freshwater run at its head

places.name: Rockpark
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 714 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.root-gallery-murkmire (+0.37).

why.founding: Canon empties Rockpark of every business and guild through pestilence, plague and a curse; nobody returned because its Hist died.
why.siteAdvantages: Good firm ground on the north-east road out of Lilmoth — which is why its emptiness is so conspicuous.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Unearthed Equipment Store still blocks the palace gate and the palace still holds what the royal family became.
why.pressures: It is a day's walk from a living city and stocked with five centuries of untouched goods, and still nobody goes in.
why.wouldChangeIf: A confirmed cure for whatever is in the palace would strip the town in a week.

places.hook: Good firm ground on the north-east road out of Lilmoth — which is why its emptiness is so conspicuous

places.name: Under-Root
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 413 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on landform, parent, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.rockpark (+0.37).

why.founding: A walkable gallery under a great root mass, dry above the flood, and occupied by people who wanted somewhere no one would look.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hundred metres of natural passage with three entrances and a permanent air flow.
why.occupantsMotive: Whoever is currently in it — the tenancy changes and the fittings do not.
why.pressures: The gallery floods to chest height in the deep wet season, on about a week's notice.
why.wouldChangeIf: A root collapse would close the middle and split it into two dead ends.

hardConstraints: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
places.hook: Two hundred metres of natural passage with three entrances and a permanent air flow

places.name: Customs Suburb
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 214 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Imperial customs suburb outside Lilmoth's north gate, looted by the An-Xileel when they took the city from the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: Astride the north road where every cargo had to pass, which is why it was built and why it was sacked.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody rebuilt it; Lilmoth's rebuilt council collects at the quay instead and prefers not to be reminded.
why.pressures: Its record room survived the fire and nobody has read it in two centuries.
why.wouldChangeIf: The records would establish who owned what before 4E 48, which several families would prefer stayed unknown.

hardConstraints: in a port or a city
places.hook: Astride the north road where every cargo had to pass, which is why it was built and why it was sacked

places.name: Screen-Watch
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.quinrawl-anchorage (+0.92).

why.founding: A village of the people who pilot Bramman's river, built inside the mangrove wall a mile above its mouth.
why.siteAdvantages: Invisible from the bay; every house sits on the channel it watches; the mangrove is both wall and roof.
why.occupantsMotive: Piloting fees, and a strict internal rule that no two families ever teach the same reach of the river.
why.pressures: Blackguards want the river as a road, Soulrest wants it as a customs problem, and the village wants it to stay a rumour.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the channel were ever charted publicly the village would have no reason to exist.

places.hook: Invisible from the bay; every house sits on the channel it watches; the mangrove is both wall and roof

places.name: Shut-From-Within
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 538 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Sealed by its own people when its Hist chamber was emptied, so that whatever remains inside stays inside.
why.siteAdvantages: A low xanmeer on a rise, unremarkable except that its door was closed from within.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing tends it. Its traps are intact and its Hist chamber is not empty in the way the sealers believed.
why.pressures: Two villages disagree about which of them did the sealing, and therefore about who may open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: An agreement between the two villages would open it legitimately for the first time in centuries.

places.hook: A low xanmeer on a rise, unremarkable except that its door was closed from within

places.name: The Slaughter Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 50 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where Lilmoth buried the dead of 4E 48 — its own residents, killed first, by their own city's tree and its party.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the rebuilt wall on the only firm ground large enough, because inside the wall is the mass grave the city stands on.
why.occupantsMotive: A rotating vigil, maintained by the same rule as the tree-minders': never one faction, never one person.
why.pressures: The An-Xileel successor state denies the causation; Lilmoth's whole civic identity depends on it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A reconciliation with the successor state would require abandoning the inscription, and it will not happen.

places.hook: Outside the rebuilt wall on the only firm ground large enough, because inside the wall is the mass grave the city stands on

places.name: Soulrest
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'soulrest' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Third-Era provincial capital at the one sheltered deep-water landfall where Topal Bay meets the Southern Sea.
why.siteAdvantages: Peninsula wrapping the bay; a river mouth just south opening a route north-east into the interior; islands screening the approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Four powers hold pieces of it: a merchant council, an orphaned Imperial apparatus, interior tribes, and the river interests who control Bramman's water.
why.pressures: Its gold-and-timber hinterland was burned by the tribes in 3E 427 and never rebuilt; the capital moved; the offices remain, administering nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the mines reopened, or if one of the four claimants finally won, the city would stop being a stalemate and start being a capital again.

hardConstraints: bay port at a concealed river's mouth
places.hook: Peninsula wrapping the bay; a river mouth just south opening a route north-east into the interior; islands screening the approach

places.name: Breaking Hard
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on bound, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where the Expeditionary Force's transports were cut up for their iron when the Empire stopped paying for them.
why.siteAdvantages: A hard shingle slope inside the mole with deep water at its foot — the only place on the coast a hull can be laid over.
why.occupantsMotive: Breakers who make more from Imperial fastenings than any local trade makes from anything.
why.pressures: The supply of Imperial hulls is finite and nearly finished; the yard has started buying wrecks off the Long Bar and asking nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Soulrest ever built ships again, the same slope would serve.

places.hook: A hard shingle slope inside the mole with deep water at its foot — the only place on the coast a hull can be laid over

places.name: Long Table
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 64 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The quayside house where cargo is contracted, crews are hired and the council's tariffs are argued about.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay, between the harbour office and the divers' yard.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper sells information at the same table as beer and considers both a single trade.
why.pressures: Everyone who matters in the port drinks here, which makes it the least private room in the city.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council monopoly on brokerage would empty it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing
places.hook: On the quay, between the harbour office and the divers' yard

places.name: Ganthil's Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.bereaved-village-murkmire (+0.55).

why.founding: Umbriel passed over this village on its way from Lilmoth in 4E 48 and took everyone in it; what stood up afterwards is still standing.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly under the recorded track of the shadow, on ground that was good enough to hold a village and is now avoided entirely.
why.occupantsMotive: The dead here do not leave the village bounds, which is the only reason it is not a regional catastrophe.
