why.pressures: It sits between two working villages and forces every journey between them to take an extra half-day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would restore a road that has been broken for a hundred and fifty years.

places.hook: Directly under the recorded track of the shadow, on ground that was good enough to hold a village and is now avoided entirely

places.name: Sunken Causeway
places.whySiteWon: ford in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 175 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Imperial causeway across the salt marsh, built to carry ore carts and abandoned when the carts stopped.
why.siteAdvantages: The only straight line across four kilometres of marsh, and still the driest one.
why.occupantsMotive: Used by anyone crossing; maintained by nobody.
why.pressures: Three spans are gone; the gaps are swum, waded or jumped depending on the tide.
why.wouldChangeIf: Repairing the spans would restore the fastest route between Soulrest and the burn country.

places.hook: The only straight line across four kilometres of marsh, and still the driest one

places.name: Teeba-Enoo Court
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 88 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.hereguard-plantation (+2.21).

why.founding: Canon: the tribes tolerate Alten Meerhleel because of its Teeba-Enoo court — the ball game is the price the port pays for existing.
why.siteAdvantages: A floored court on the landward margin of the port, where tribal parties can come without entering the trading water.
why.occupantsMotive: The port fields a team and loses politely; the tribes take the result seriously and the trade continues.
why.pressures: A port team that won convincingly would create a diplomatic problem nobody wants.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending the games would end the tolerance, and the port knows exactly what that costs.

places.hook: A floored court on the landward margin of the port, where tribal parties can come without entering the trading water

places.name: The Teeth of Sithis
places.whySiteWon: summit in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 593 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's largest Sithis temple in Murkmire, tended by the Clutch of Nisswo though it no longer serves its original purpose.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep in the marsh at the end of a pilgrim route, with a natural rock formation the temple was built to frame.
why.occupantsMotive: The Clutch maintain it precisely and preach that its loss of purpose is the sermon.
why.pressures: Nobody can now say what the original purpose was, and at least one faction claims to have found out.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rediscovery of the temple's function would split the Clutch.

places.hook: Deep in the marsh at the end of a pilgrim route, with a natural rock formation the temple was built to frame

places.name: Tempers-The-Young
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, hinterland, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: in Lilmoth people look to their elders, including retired Shadowscales — and retired Shadowscales trained somewhere.
why.siteAdvantages: An enclosed water-and-root ground an hour outside the city, with three approaches and no sightline into it.
why.occupantsMotive: Two retired scales still keep the ground and still take the occasional sign-born child, which is now illegal in every sense.
why.pressures: The Cheydinhal succession wants the tradition back; Lilmoth's council would rather it did not exist near their walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single public execution of a trainee here would force the council to act.

places.hook: An enclosed water-and-root ground an hour outside the city, with three approaches and no sightline into it

places.name: White Fields
places.whySiteWon: natural harbour in ocean (danger band 0), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Salt is the one export the burning of the mines did not touch, and the bay's shore evaporates well.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide, gently shelving salt-marsh shore with a dry season long enough to crystallise.
why.occupantsMotive: Pan-holders who pay Soulrest a share and sell the rest to fish-curers along the whole south coast.
why.pressures: A wet-season overtop ruins a year; the sea walls are rebuilt by owed labour every spring.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Owing gangs stopped coming, the pans would silt in three years.

hardConstraints: tidal salt water, sun and wind
places.hook: A wide, gently shelving salt-marsh shore with a dry season long enough to crystallise

places.name: The Villa Cellars
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 31 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, submerged, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Imperial villas outside the rebuilt wall sank with their cellars intact, and the cellars are connected.
why.siteAdvantages: A continuous flooded undercroft running two hundred metres, entered from three collapsed floors.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage crews work the near end under permit; the far end is beyond the permit line and not empty.
why.pressures: The passage is head-height, silt-floored and disorients completely; there is no natural light after the second room.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse at the middle would cut the far cellars off for good.

places.hook: A continuous flooded undercroft running two hundred metres, entered from three collapsed floors

places.name: White Rose Prison
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 167 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: One of the prisons canon says the Empire built after 1E 2837, sited by the Imperial rule for this province: put it where the marsh is the wall.
why.siteAdvantages: An island of firm ground in burn-country marsh with one causeway, serving the convict-worked mines behind Soulrest.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty of the living. Full of Argonian dead who died away from their Hist and whose bones were never brought to the dirt.
why.pressures: The Blackrose Chainbreakers want the dead repatriated; the structure is sound enough that somebody will eventually want it back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reoccupation by any armed party would make the repatriation impossible and the grievance permanent.

places.hook: An island of firm ground in burn-country marsh with one causeway, serving the convict-worked mines behind Soulrest

places.name: The Wraxu Frieze
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 57 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Sithite work-and-unmake ground where the local xanmeer carvings of the extinct wraxu are copied in clay and destroyed each year.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered clay bank under a xanmeer face that carries the original wraxu etchings canon records here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo and their students make an exact copy of the frieze, exhibit it for one night, and break it before dawn.
why.pressures: Outsiders keep trying to buy the copy; the Clutch keeps having to explain that the destruction is the work.
why.wouldChangeIf: A copy surviving a year would be a theological crisis, and someone is trying to arrange one.

places.hook: A sheltered clay bank under a xanmeer face that carries the original wraxu etchings canon records here

places.name: Wraxu Stacks
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 108 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.long-bar-wreckers (+1.11).

why.founding: Named for the extinct wraxu birds whose colonies canon puts on this coast; the birds that nest here now are not them.
why.siteAdvantages: Vertical sea stacks off the islands, unclimbable from three sides, thick with guano and eggs.
why.occupantsMotive: Egg-takers come twice a year by rope and take the ledges in a fixed order.
why.pressures: Everyone here knows what happened to the wraxu, and the taking rules are stricter than any law Soulrest ever wrote.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single greedy season would be remembered for a century.

places.hook: Vertical sea stacks off the islands, unclimbable from three sides, thick with guano and eggs

places.name: Xinchei-Konu Monument
places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 2), 377 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's ancient calendar in the lowlands east of Lilmoth, with a hereditary keeper — a jekka-wass — and a function: it is called a catalyst of change and can alter the weather.
why.siteAdvantages: An open lowland with a clean southern horizon, because the instrument needs one.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper's whole office is not to use it, and to explain that to everyone who arrives wanting it used.
why.pressures: Every party with a weather problem eventually comes here; the keeper has refused emperors' agents and antiquarians alike.
why.wouldChangeIf: A successful use would be the largest single event in the province's recent history, which is the argument for and against.

places.hook: An open lowland with a clean southern horizon, because the instrument needs one

places.name: The Poler's Breath
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 218 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A maintained air pocket on the flooded shortcut under the narrows.
why.siteAdvantages: The midpoint of a dive that cannot be made on one breath.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; maintained by the guides who use it. The guides keep it because a pocket nobody maintains is a pocket that drowns the guild's next apprentice, so the upkeep is charged into every crossing fee whether the client uses the pocket or not.
why.pressures: Silt is filling the pocket from below. Two guiding families disagree about who is responsible for clearing it, and each has spent a decade waiting for the other to admit the duty.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its loss would close the shortcut and add two hours to every crossing. Its loss would also break the guides' price against the portage crews, who would take the traffic within a season.

places.hook: The midpoint of a dive that cannot be made on one breath

places.name: The Unmaking Yard
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 395 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A ground where Nisswo commission works of art and destroy them as the sermon.
why.siteAdvantages: A clearing with a landing, so patrons can attend and leave.
why.occupantsMotive: A resident maker and a rotating congregation. The maker is paid to make well and then watch it burn; the fee is for the making, and a maker who flinches at the destruction is not commissioned again.
why.pressures: Foreign collectors have begun buying the works before the destruction, which is heresy and lucrative. The buyers pay in coastal coin the congregation has learned to want, so the heresy is funding the rite that condemns it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single sale being made public would split the congregation. A split would put a second, tolerant unmaking-yard on the coast within a year, and this one would become the strict house by contrast.

places.hook: A clearing with a landing, so patrons can attend and leave

places.name: Teeth-Pens
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 214 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.legendary-deep-feather-serpent (+1.24).

why.founding: A village that keeps crocodiles — for hide, for meat, and because a penned ring of them is the cheapest wall in the swamp.
why.siteAdvantages: A creek that can be gated at both ends to make the pens.
why.occupantsMotive: Keepers whose stock is also their defence. Keeping is hereditary because the stock knows its keepers by scent, and a village that sold its line of keepers would have to kill its wall and start again.
why.pressures: The pens have failed twice and the village rebuilt them larger. Larger pens need more meat than the creek yields, so the village now buys fish it used to sell, and the wall is quietly eating the economy it protects.
why.wouldChangeIf: A pen failure in the wet season would be catastrophic. A wet-season failure would not just cost the herd: the loose stock would take the surrounding reaches for a decade and cut the village off from its own landings.

places.hook: A creek that can be gated at both ends to make the pens

places.name: Since-The-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 449 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, ring; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village whose Hist was killed during the Umbriel passage and which has stayed put ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: Their ground is good and their reason for staying is that leaving would be a second death. Their ground also carries the stump, which is a relic and a grave and the only thing they own that no neighbour will contest.
why.occupantsMotive: People with no hatching, no naming and no soul-return, keeping a village going anyway.
why.pressures: Their young are Hist-less by birth — a whole generation the province has no category for. The neighbouring tribes will trade with them and will not marry them, so each generation is smaller than the last while the village itself is unchanged.
why.wouldChangeIf: Adoption by a neighbouring tree would dissolve them into someone else's tribe, which they have refused twice. A hero Hist consenting to hatch their young without taking their name would solve it, and no tree has ever been asked to do that.

places.hook: Their ground is good and their reason for staying is that leaving would be a second death

places.name: Nine-Stakes Field
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 335 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A grave-stake field that rose after a flood disturbed it, not after a theft.
why.siteAdvantages: Low ground beside a channel that changed course.
why.occupantsMotive: Blights that were not raised by anyone's fault. Because no theft raised them, the risen have no wrongdoer to blame, which in local law makes them the whole village's debt rather than one family's.
why.pressures: The village that owns the field cannot afford to restake it and cannot afford not to. The stake-setters price by the night and the village pays in rice, and the two rates have drifted so far apart that the work has stopped mid-field.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking would settle it; the labour is the obstacle, not the danger. Restaking would settle it; the labour is the obstacle, not the danger, and any outsider who supplies the labour buys a permanent claim on the village.

places.hook: Low ground beside a channel that changed course

places.name: The Old Cordon
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 31 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.drowning-narrows-tidal-gate (+0.28).

why.founding: A plague cordon's burial line that was never staked at all, because the buriers were foreign.
why.siteAdvantages: The line of an Imperial-era cordon across the zone's neck.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever a century of unstaked burial produces. Nobody inherits the duty because nobody inherited the burial: the Legion dug the line, the Legion left, and the ground has been legally ownerless since.
why.pressures: The route the cordon guarded is the route people still use. The route the cordon guarded is the route people still use, and each generation's accidents are blamed on the last generation's cowardice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Staking the line would take a season and end a century of accidents. Staking the line would take a season and end a century of accidents — and would also settle, publicly, that the plague dead here were Argonian and not Kothringi.

places.hook: The line of an Imperial-era cordon across the zone's neck

places.name: The Carriers' Camp
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 47 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-firm-ground' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A seasonal camp of bone-carriers gathering the zone's distant dead for the walk inland.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the poling routes converge before the walking route begins. It is also the last point a laden carrier can be resupplied by boat, which is why the camp holds and the route inland does not branch.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, in season. Carrying is a debt-work: most carriers are repaying a family's unreturned dead rather than earning, which is why the season is worked to exhaustion.
why.pressures: The Umbriel-era backlog reaches this camp too, and it is visible in the stacks. The Umbriel-era backlog reaches this camp too, and it is visible in the stacks — bundles labelled for villages that no longer exist and cannot receive them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A carriers' strike would leave a season's dead unreturned.

places.hook: Where the poling routes converge before the walking route begins

places.name: Dead-Water Village
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 774 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.naga-village-raiding (+1.09).

why.founding: The Naga-Kur's seat: the tribe built for surviving the worst thing in the swamp, around the tree that made them.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise in the inner swamps with black water on every side and one poling approach. The single poling approach is also the tribe's toll: nothing reaches the inner swamp's eastern reaches without being counted here first.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe whose whole discipline — grave rite, watch, blight-craft — is organised around the dead not staying down.
why.pressures: Umbriel's legacy is exactly their enemy, and they have not stopped preparing; their kin on the roads are tribeless and their reputation suffers for it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for the discipline that defines it. If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for the discipline that defines it — and the stake-setters, the night necropolis and three subordinate villages would lose their trade with it.

places.hook: A defensible rise in the inner swamps with black water on every side and one poling approach

places.name: Deepmire, the Refuge
places.whySiteWon: flood high in interior swamp (danger band 4), 568 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's shelter of last resort: an all-but-inaccessible plateau in the north-north-east that even the tribes avoid, where the presence of Sithis is said to be strong, holding pre-Duskfall xanmeers and the skeletons of swamp leviathans. It is not to be visited except to shelter, and it is tended by a caretaker few.
why.siteAdvantages: High, dry, defensible ground in a province that has almost none, with one approach that can be walked and no approach that can be poled.
why.occupantsMotive: The caretakers do not live here so much as keep it fit to be lived in — stores turned, shelters re-roofed, the memorial swept — against a need they hope never comes.
why.pressures: In 4E 48 the need did come: Murkmire's survivors fled up onto the plateau while Umbriel passed overhead, and the caretakers have been feeding that memory ever since. The Umbriel Witness Society wants the memorial catalogued, the Nisswo want it let go, and the caretakers want it left exactly as it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the argument over the memorial is settled by anyone but the caretakers, the plateau stops being a refuge and becomes a destination — which is the one thing its whole custom exists to prevent.

hardConstraints: upland ground above the flood by 40m+
places.hook: High, dry, defensible ground in a province that has almost none, with one approach that can be walked and no approach that can be poled

places.name: The Chimney
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 380 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, submerged, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A natural shaft from the swamp floor into the root layer.
why.siteAdvantages: Where a root gallery's roof gave way under water.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever uses a vertical connection between two systems. Whatever uses a vertical connection between two systems uses it in both directions, which is why the villages date their worst years by what came up it.
why.pressures: Divers use it as a shortcut and it does not always let them back. Divers use it as a shortcut and it does not always let them back; the guides charge double to name it and will not enter it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would seal the connection. A collapse would seal the connection and add half a day to every stake-field circuit on this side of the zone.

places.hook: Where a root gallery's roof gave way under water

places.name: The Moving Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 361 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village on rafts that moves with the season, because in the inner swamp no ground is reliable for a decade.
why.siteAdvantages: Whichever mooring the year requires; the village site is a route, not a point. Their moorings are chosen for what is spawning, not for what is safe, so the village's calendar is a fish's calendar.
why.occupantsMotive: People who own no land and consider that a strength.
why.pressures: Every fixed village disputes their fishing and their claim to anything. Every fixed village disputes their fishing and their claim to anything, and the settled Naga have begun charging them for water they used to take freely.
why.wouldChangeIf: A land grant would end the practice and probably the culture. A land grant would end the practice and probably the culture, and the tribes that want them settled want it precisely for that reason.

hardConstraints: sited as a mooring SET (3-4 alternates), not a point — quests 20 fixed-alternative-mooring pattern
places.hook: Whichever mooring the year requires; the village site is a route, not a point

places.name: Under-Piles
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A stilt village drowned when the channel changed and the water rose two metres in a season.
why.siteAdvantages: It was correctly sited for the water level of the time. It was correctly sited for the water level of the time, which is the standing local argument against building on any firm-looking flat.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; fish, and salvage divers.
why.pressures: The families who left are three villages away and still claim the goods in it. The families who left are three villages away and still claim the goods in it, and have hired divers twice rather than let the dredgers take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drawdown would expose it and start a legal fight. A drawdown would expose it and start a legal fight that three villages have quietly agreed to hope never happens.

places.hook: It was correctly sited for the water level of the time

places.name: The Gate Narrows
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on danger, parent, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.bog-blight-ground-old-cordon (+0.28).

why.founding: A flood-pulse pinch where the whole zone's outflow squeezes through in the hours after rain.
why.siteAdvantages: The single outlet of the inner swamp.
why.occupantsMotive: None; a timing post is kept by the nearest village. The timing post is manned by whichever village most recently lost a boat, a rota that guarantees the keeper takes it seriously and never lasts.
why.pressures: Boats that mistime it are lost, and the village profits from salvage, so the gauge post has never been improved and the drawdown timings are memorised rather than written.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cut second channel would end both the danger and the salvage income. A cut second channel would end both the danger and the salvage income, which is why the village has twice blocked the survey.

places.hook: The single outlet of the inner swamp

places.name: The Hire Stage
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 2), 113 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The stage where outsiders hire a poler, because the inner swamp cannot be navigated without one.
why.siteAdvantages: The last point reachable without local knowledge.
why.occupantsMotive: Polers, a broker, and a price list that is not the real price list. The broker is not a poler and takes a cut of every hire, which the polers resent and tolerate because he is the one who deals with foreigners.
why.pressures: Unguided travellers go in anyway and their craft come back empty. Unguided travellers go in anyway and their craft come back empty, and each such loss is used to justify the next rise in the hire price.
why.wouldChangeIf: A published chart would destroy the trade, which is why none exists. A published chart would destroy the trade, which is why none exists — and why the two surveyors who tried were poled home very slowly.

places.hook: The last point reachable without local knowledge

places.name: The Sunk Corridor
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 516 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, remote, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer service corridor now full to the ceiling.
why.siteAdvantages: It connects two parts of a ruin that are otherwise a day apart. It connects two parts of a ruin that are otherwise a day apart, and the far half is the half the looters never reached.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing. Nothing lives in it; the silt is undisturbed, which is how the divers know nobody has been through in years.
why.pressures: It is the only connection and it is a hundred metres long.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drawdown year makes it walkable and everyone waits for one. A drawdown year makes it walkable and everyone waits for one — including the tending clan, who intend to be first through and have said so.

places.hook: It connects two parts of a ruin that are otherwise a day apart

places.name: The Polers' Camp
places.whySiteWon: islet in interior swamp (danger band 4), 72 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A night camp for poling guides crossing the inner swamp.
why.siteAdvantages: The one rise at the midpoint of the longest crossing.
why.occupantsMotive: Guides and their clients, overnight only. Guides sleep between their clients and the water, a courtesy that is also a guard against clients who decide at midnight that they can find their own way.
why.pressures: The rise is small and the crossings have got busier. The rise is small and the crossings have got busier, so arrival order now decides who sleeps dry, and the older guides arrive early on principle.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second rise would have to be built, and building it is a project nobody owns. A second rise would have to be built, and building it is a project nobody owns — the guides are rivals, and no village claims ground this far out.

places.hook: The one rise at the midpoint of the longest crossing

places.name: The Held Tree
places.whySiteWon: flood high in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 719 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Hist held by a crew who feed it, tend it, and will not let its tribe near it.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible island the crew took and fortified.
why.occupantsMotive: Occupiers who claim they are protecting it and may believe it. They tap it, and what they draw is worth more than anything else in the zone, which is the part of the protection story they do not tell.
why.pressures: The tribe camps within sight and has done for eleven years. The tribe camps within sight and has done for eleven years, feeding a standoff that the surrounding villages now depend on: while it holds, nobody else can claim the island.
why.wouldChangeIf: Either party breaking the standoff resolves it violently. Either party breaking the standoff resolves it violently, and the tree itself is the likeliest casualty of the resolution.

places.hook: A defensible island the crew took and fortified

places.name: The Horwalli Cut
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 71 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'confluence' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Waterworks built by a vanished people who managed this swamp instead of living with it.
why.siteAdvantages: The zone's natural drainage pinch — the one place engineering would pay.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the works run themselves, badly. Nobody; the works run themselves, badly, and the villages downstream have built their calendars around its faults rather than its intent.
why.pressures: The half-working sluices still divert water, and two modern villages flood because of a decision made by a dead civilisation. The half-working sluices still divert water, and two modern villages flood because of a decision made by a dead civilisation — which each village blames on the other's failure to clear its own channel.
why.wouldChangeIf: Repairing or breaking the works would redraw the zone's hydrology. Repairing or breaking the works would redraw the zone's hydrology, making one village's rice ground and drowning another's, so any repair is a political act before it is an engineering one.

places.hook: The zone's natural drainage pinch — the one place engineering would pay

places.name: The Feather Deep
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 252 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.beast-keeper-crocodile (+1.24).

why.founding: The deepest hole in the inner swamps, named in the tribes' recitation and entered by nobody.
why.siteAdvantages: A drowned sinkhole in the swamp floor, far deeper than anything around it. A drowned sinkhole in the swamp floor, far deeper than anything around it — the only place in the zone where the root layer does not close overhead.
why.occupantsMotive: Something the recitation names and does not describe. Something the recitation names and does not describe, and the omission is deliberate: the naming tribes hold that describing it is an invitation.
why.pressures: Divers who go for the treasure at the lip do not go past it. Divers who go for the treasure at the lip do not go past it, and the lip has been picked over often enough that the good salvage now starts below the point where people stop.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing.

places.hook: A drowned sinkhole in the swamp floor, far deeper than anything around it

places.name: The Nine Ribs
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 25 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, parent, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon says swamp-leviathan skeletons litter Deepmire; this is the largest of them, and a bone-and-hide works grew up beside it because the material is free, enormous and already dead.
why.siteAdvantages: Beached in shallow water at a channel bend, so the carcass could be worked from boats and the ribs stayed standing while the rest went.
why.occupantsMotive: A handful of bone-cutters and one family living inside the rib cage, who regard the arrangement as ordinary.
why.pressures: The cause of death is still legible in the skull, and it was not old age; whatever did it has not been seen since, which the neighbours find less reassuring than the cutters do.
why.wouldChangeIf: The bone runs out in a generation, and the works has already started arguing about the second skeleton downstream.

hardConstraints: shallow water a hull can work from
standing ribs that break the canopy line
places.hook: Beached in shallow water at a channel bend, so the carcass could be worked from boats and the ribs stayed standing while the rest went

places.name: The Kaju Ground
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 427 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.sinkhole-mouth-deeps (+0.50).

why.founding: The trial by which the deep-swamp young take an adult name: a kill, alone, in water.
why.siteAdvantages: A reach that reliably holds the right animal. A reach that reliably holds the right animal, and shallow enough at the margins that the families can watch without being able to help.
why.occupantsMotive: Trial-keepers and, in season, the candidates' families waiting at the bank.
why.pressures: The animal population is down and the trial is getting harder, which some read as a judgement. The animal population is down and the trial is getting harder, which some read as a judgement, and which has already pushed two families to send their young to the coastal trials instead.
why.wouldChangeIf: A failed season would force a change to a rite nobody wants to change. A failed season would force a change to a rite nobody wants to change, and the deep-swamp tribes would rather import animals than admit the reach is finished.

places.hook: A reach that reliably holds the right animal

places.name: The Open Ward
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 214 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A miregaunt standing in open water with nothing behind it to guard.
why.siteAdvantages: Open shallow water on no route to anywhere. Open shallow water on no route to anywhere — which is itself the evidence, because a ward implies the route existed once.
why.occupantsMotive: One miregaunt, guarding nothing anybody can find.
why.pressures: Its presence implies something here worth guarding, and nobody has found it. Its presence implies something here worth guarding, and nobody has found it; the standing theory is that the ward outlived a Horwalli work now under the silt.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. It returns. Nothing. It returns — and it returns to the same stance and the same bearing, which is the detail scholars pay for.

places.hook: Open shallow water on no route to anywhere

places.name: The North Cut Camp
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in interior swamp (danger band 4), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribeless Naga camp working the northern poling route.
why.siteAdvantages: A blind bend where craft must slow.
why.occupantsMotive: Tribeless Naga who take cargo and rarely lives. Tribeless Naga who take cargo and rarely lives, on the calculation that a robbed poler comes back next season and a dead one brings his tribe.
why.pressures: The settled tribes are blamed for them, which suits nobody. The settled tribes are blamed for them, which suits nobody, and the settled hold has begun paying the camp not to work its stretch — a fact that would ruin it if known.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settlement between settled and tribeless would end the camp. A settlement between settled and tribeless would end the camp, and the province's toll rates would fall with it.

places.hook: A blind bend where craft must slow

places.name: Cut-Rope
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 12 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.dead-water-village (+1.09).

why.founding: A Naga village that took up the roads openly and now lives on them.
why.siteAdvantages: A creek head that reaches three routes and hides a fleet of poling craft. A creek head that reaches three routes and hides a fleet of poling craft, none of which can be counted from the water.
why.occupantsMotive: Raiders who consider it work, and their families, who consider it income.
why.pressures: The settled tribes have disowned them; the province's tolls have doubled because of them. The settled tribes have disowned them; the province's tolls have doubled because of them, and the coastal brokers who buy the takings are the same brokers the settled tribes sell rice to.
why.wouldChangeIf: A season of failed raids would starve or scatter them. A season of failed raids would starve or scatter them, and scattering is the outcome the settled Naga fear most — a hundred tribeless families with no village to negotiate with.

places.hook: A creek head that reaches three routes and hides a fleet of poling craft

places.name: Long-Water Hold
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 280 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.voriplasm-chamber-breached (+1.42).

why.founding: A settled Naga tribe with a tended Hist, villages, fields and a quarrel with their own tribeless relatives.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground on the inner swamp's main poling route. Firm ground on the inner swamp's main poling route, with a landing deep enough for laden craft — the reason they can trade at all.
why.occupantsMotive: People who want the road trade and are undermined by kin who rob it.
why.pressures: Every outsider arrives assuming they are brigands, which is exhausting and occasionally fatal. Every outsider arrives assuming they are brigands, which is exhausting and occasionally fatal, and the hold now pays the northern camp for quiet rather than fight a war it would win and could not afford.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settlement with the tribeless would change how the whole southern interior travels. A settlement with the tribeless would change how the whole southern interior travels, and would cost the coastal escort trade its best market.

places.hook: Firm ground on the inner swamp's main poling route

places.name: The Staking Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 319 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that services the grave-stake fields of the deep swamp and works them only after dark, when the blights are readable.
why.siteAdvantages: Central to nine fields, on the one rise that stays dry. Central to nine fields, on the one rise that stays dry — which also makes it the only place in the zone that can store stakes in quantity.
why.occupantsMotive: Stake-setters who work nights and sleep through the day.
why.pressures: Since Umbriel there is more work than there are setters, and the backlog is measurable in risings. Since Umbriel there is more work than there are setters, and the backlog is measurable in risings; villages now bid against each other for a night's work and the poorest fields go unstaked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing a generation of setters would let the fields go. Losing a generation of setters would let the fields go, and the Naga-Kur's whole grave discipline runs through this village's rota.

places.hook: Central to nine fields, on the one rise that stays dry

places.name: The Egg Camp
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 216 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Egg-poachers working the zone's nesting grounds for a coastal buyer.
why.siteAdvantages: Between three nesting sites, on a creek with a fast exit.
why.occupantsMotive: Poachers who take clutches the villages are counting. Poachers who take clutches the villages are counting, working for a coastal buyer who sells the eggs as a delicacy and never sees the marsh.
why.pressures: Taking eggs here reads as close to taking children, and the villages respond accordingly. Taking eggs here reads as close to taking children, and the villages respond accordingly; two poachers have been staked alive and the practice has not stopped.
why.wouldChangeIf: One caught crew would end the trade for a season. One caught crew would end the trade for a season, and would give the villages a name to send to the coast — which is the outcome the buyer has paid to prevent.

places.hook: Between three nesting sites, on a creek with a fast exit

places.name: The Drag
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 422 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A slipway where craft are dragged past the narrows rather than run them.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest crossing of the neck between two channels.
why.occupantsMotive: A drag crew who charge by the hull and keep the rollers greased with fish oil they buy from the drawdown village they are competing with.
why.pressures: The crew and the drawdown village compete for the same traffic, and each has an interest in the other's accidents being talked about.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cut channel would end both trades. A cut channel would end both trades, which is why the two rivals have twice sent a joint delegation against the survey.

places.hook: The shortest crossing of the neck between two channels

places.name: The Lashing
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Households who lash their rafts together for the wet season and separate for the dry.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered backwater with no current. A sheltered backwater with no current, and no owner — the water is too poor for a fixed village to have claimed it.
why.occupantsMotive: Families who are neighbours six months a year and strangers the other six.
why.pressures: Every year the lashing order is renegotiated and every year it causes a row. Every year the lashing order is renegotiated and every year it causes a row, because the outer rafts take the weather and the inner ones take the smell.
why.wouldChangeIf: A permanent lashing would make them a village and they have voted against it twice. A permanent lashing would make them a village and they have voted against it twice, chiefly because a village can be taxed and a raft cannot be found.

places.hook: A sheltered backwater with no current

places.name: The Raided Camp
places.whySiteWon: island in interior swamp (danger band 3), 342 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that ran from the raiding Naga and has not gone back.
why.siteAdvantages: The first defensible ground they reached. The first defensible ground they reached, which is nobody's ground, which is why no tribe has had to decide what they are.
why.occupantsMotive: People waiting to hear whether their village still stands.
why.pressures: It has been two years and the camp is becoming a settlement nobody will admit to founding. It has been two years and the camp is becoming a settlement nobody will admit to founding; the children have started calling it by a name the adults refuse to use.
why.wouldChangeIf: News either way ends the camp. News either way ends the camp — and the news exists: a poler has seen the village and has been paid by two different parties not to say what he saw.

places.hook: The first defensible ground they reached

places.name: The Warren
places.whySiteWon: flood high in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 544 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A gallery beneath a burial ground.
why.siteAdvantages: The roots reach the graves, which is the whole problem. The roots reach the graves, which is the whole problem: the gallery is fed by the burial ground it undermines.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights, in numbers, working steadily upward. Bog blights, in numbers, working steadily upward — and, unusually, staying below by day, which is the only reason the village above still exists.
why.pressures: The village above is driving a stake ring and losing ground each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing and restaking it is the zone's defining deed. Clearing and restaking it is the zone's defining deed, and the Naga-Kur would owe whoever did it a standing that no amount of trade buys.

places.hook: The roots reach the graves, which is the whole problem

places.name: Root-Whisper Village
places.whySiteWon: enclosed clearing in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 272 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids destroyed the tribe here and harvested its souls into the Remnant of Argon; the Hist did not die but slept, and was called the Dreaming Tree for as long as it slept. At the end of the Second Era the souls were returned and the village was re-founded on its own ground, between the twin xanmeers Xul-Thuxis and Vakka-Bok.
why.siteAdvantages: East Deepmire ground the tribe never technically left, held between two pre-Duskfall xanmeers that mark it from a distance and keep the approach to one line.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe rebuilt out of returned souls, living on the exact ground it was killed on, because the tree is here and the tree is the only reason any of them exist.
why.pressures: The Hist is elder in years and young in voice — it speaks like a hatchling and is treated by its own tree-minder as convalescent — and Cyrodilic Collections, which helped resurrect the tribe, has never quite stopped treating the village as its find.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Dreaming Tree failed a second time there would be no second Remnant; the tribe knows this and organises its whole year around not finding out.

places.hook: East Deepmire ground the tribe never technically left, held between two pre-Duskfall xanmeers that mark it from a distance and keep the approach to one line

places.name: The Black Eye
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 525 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.maturity-trial-kaju-kill (+0.50).

why.founding: One of the province's few sinkholes, drowned, in the middle of a reed flat.
why.siteAdvantages: A rare karst collapse the swamp has flooded rather than filled. A rare karst collapse the swamp has flooded rather than filled — one of only a handful in the province, so the landform itself is a landmark.
why.occupantsMotive: Divers, occasionally. Divers, occasionally, and always the same three, who will not take passengers and will not say what they bring up.
why.pressures: It goes into the root layer and nobody has mapped where it comes out. It goes into the root layer and nobody has mapped where it comes out, though a body put in here has twice surfaced two zones away.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry cycle would expose the rim and make it enterable on foot.

hardConstraints: sinkhole landform (11 province-wide — budgeted: 1 in this zone)
places.hook: A rare karst collapse the swamp has flooded rather than filled

places.name: The Emptying House
places.whySiteWon: flood high in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 491 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Sithis temple in the deep swamp where the doctrine is practised at its least metaphorical.
why.siteAdvantages: Black water on all sides and no neighbour close enough to object. Black water on all sides and no neighbour close enough to object, and one landing that can be watched from the house itself.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo who preach a sermon the coastal Nisswo will not repeat.
why.pressures: The interior tribes tolerate it and do not attend; the settled Naga forbid their young to go. The interior tribes tolerate it and do not attend; the settled Naga forbid their young to go, and the forbidding has made attendance a way for the young to make a point.
why.wouldChangeIf: A closure would need someone with authority nobody in the deep swamp recognises. A closure would need someone with authority nobody in the deep swamp recognises — and the coastal Nisswo who could claim that authority will not come this far in.

places.hook: Black water on all sides and no neighbour close enough to object

places.name: The Still-Walking Village
places.whySiteWon: flood high in interior swamp (danger band 4), 151 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village under the Umbriel track whose dead did not lie down afterwards.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the shadow's path, which nobody could have chosen. Directly on the shadow's path, which nobody could have chosen, and on ground that was the best rice land in the zone before it.
why.occupantsMotive: The village's own dead, still in their own houses.
why.pressures: This is precisely the enemy the Naga-Kur's discipline was built for, and they have contained rather than cleared it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it is a deed the Naga-Kur would owe the player for permanently. Clearing it is a deed the Naga-Kur would owe the player for permanently — and would free the rice ground, which four neighbouring villages have already privately divided.

places.hook: Directly on the shadow's path, which nobody could have chosen

places.name: The Split Cistern
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 255 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.naga-village-settled (+1.42).

why.founding: A sealed cistern that a subsidence cracked open twelve years ago.
why.siteAdvantages: Under a xanmeer floor, in ground that is still moving. Under a xanmeer floor, in ground that is still moving, so any seal put back would have to be built to shift with it.
why.occupantsMotive: What was sealed in it, now not sealed in it.
why.pressures: It is spreading through the flooded lower halls and out into the swamp. It is spreading through the flooded lower halls and out into the swamp, and the dredgers working two channels away have started finding it in their spoil.
why.wouldChangeIf: Sealing it again is possible and nobody has the nerve. Sealing it again is possible and nobody has the nerve; the tending clan has priced the work three times and each price has been higher than the last.

places.hook: Under a xanmeer floor, in ground that is still moving

places.name: The Standing Charge
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 309 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An adult wamasu holds a pond on the zone's main poling route.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep still water directly on the route — the worst possible place for it.
why.occupantsMotive: One adult, resident for years. One adult, resident for years, and the villages have begun leaving offerings at the bank in the old Shadowfen manner rather than treat it as vermin.
why.pressures: Traffic detours two hours around it and the detour is itself dangerous. Traffic detours two hours around it and the detour is itself dangerous, running past the reed narrows where the southern camp works.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing it reopens the route and the tribes disagree about whether it should be killed. Killing it reopens the route and the tribes disagree about whether it should be killed — the offering-makers hold that a wamasu on a route is a toll, not a problem.

places.hook: Deep still water directly on the route — the worst possible place for it

places.name: The Withdrawn Tree
places.whySiteWon: island in interior swamp (danger band 4), 639 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on remote, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A wild Hist that has cut itself off from the collective — the rare, catastrophic condition, visible in one place.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep swamp, no tribe, no witnesses to argue about it. Deep swamp, no tribe, no witnesses to argue about it — which is also why it has been left alone long enough to be studied.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing speaks for it and nothing tends it. Nothing speaks for it and nothing tends it; the nearest tribe sends no one and will not explain the omission to outsiders.
why.pressures: It is the physical demonstration of the main quest's premise, standing in the world before the quest names it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reconnection is possible in principle and nobody knows how. Reconnection is possible in principle and nobody knows how, and the tribes that could try are the same tribes that will not go near it.

places.hook: Deep swamp, no tribe, no witnesses to argue about it

places.name: The Sunk Barge
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Imperial-era cargo barge that went down in the narrows with its load aboard.
why.siteAdvantages: It sank in the deep of the bend and has never shifted. It sank in the deep of the bend and has never shifted, so the hull is intact and the holds are still closed.
why.occupantsMotive: Fish, and divers who take a little at a time. Fish, and divers who take a little at a time, on the reasoning that a wreck emptied all at once is a wreck somebody comes to look at.
why.pressures: The cargo is bonded goods and a company that no longer exists still legally owns them. The cargo is bonded goods and a company that no longer exists still legally owns them, which makes selling any of it on the coast a question rather than a sale.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry cycle would expose the deck and end the slow looting.

places.hook: It sank in the deep of the bend and has never shifted

places.name: Alten Corimont
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'alten-corimont' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: A river port ESE of the Hatching Pools that grew into a small town by being institutionally neutral about cargo: it sits on the northern trunk between Stormhold and Thorn, on water deep enough for a laden hull and far enough from any customs regime that both of them use it.
why.siteAdvantages: The last reach of navigable river below the northern rim, with an oxbow that makes a natural basin, firm banks for warehousing and a rim road behind it that crosses to Morrowind without passing a post.
why.occupantsMotive: A captain of the port whose only law is a nailed-up price list, freeholder crews with no tribe and no tree, Dunmer factors from the Morrowind trade and Nord hands off the northern hulls.
why.pressures: There is no Hist here — the register is explicit — so nothing binds anyone to anything except the list; Stormhold's vicecanons would like the trade and cannot reach it; Rockpoint downriver still resents losing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either Stormhold or Thorn made the port lawful, its whole reason to exist is gone; if the river silted below the oxbow, the town is a village in five years.

hardConstraints: navigable water for a laden hull
sheltered basin off the legal lanes
no Hist within the settlement — canon
places.hook: The last reach of navigable river below the northern rim, with an oxbow that makes a natural basin, firm banks for warehousing and a rim road behind it that crosses to Morrowind without passing a post

places.name: Bundle Racks
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 72 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Argonians who die away from a Hist can still return if their bones are brought to the dirt — and this zone has no Hist at all, so every death here starts a journey south.
why.siteAdvantages: On the trunk route at the point where the southbound road and the river both leave the freeholds.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers who take the dead of a town that cannot bury them, for a fee they are ashamed of.
why.pressures: The house is always full, because the freeholds produce more Hist-less dead than any comparable ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Hist were ever planted at the free port, this house closes and the carriers lose a trade.

places.hook: On the trunk route at the point where the southbound road and the river both leave the freeholds

places.name: Chasecreek
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 354 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, route.

why.founding: A fishing hamlet on the one dry rise at a creek mouth, which discovered that a boat can wait here unseen while the free port is being watched, and has lived off that ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A single flood-high rise with a creek deep enough to hide a hull and shallow enough that nobody follows.
why.occupantsMotive: Fisher households who are also, on about four nights a month, a lay-by with a fee.
why.pressures: The lay-by trade is worth more than the fish and everyone under sixteen already knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port's list ever covered waiting time, Chasecreek loses its niche and becomes a fishing hamlet again.

hardConstraints: a dry rise that never floods
a creek mouth deep enough to lie in
places.hook: A single flood-high rise with a creek deep enough to hide a hull and shallow enough that nobody follows

places.name: No-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 412 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent.

why.founding: The register is explicit that the free port has no Hist, and that is not an omission — it is the reason the freeholds exist. Everyone here is Hist-less by choice or by accident, and the camp on the town's edge is where that is admitted out loud.
why.siteAdvantages: The town's landward fringe, on ground the port does not administer.
why.occupantsMotive: Argonians with no tree to return to, plus outsiders who find that easier to be around.
why.pressures: The tribal villages upriver will not visit; Hissmir's reconnection rite is a two-week journey and a hard conversation.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Hist cutting were successfully planted here, the free port stops being a freehold and starts being a town.

places.hook: The town's landward fringe, on ground the port does not administer

places.name: The Quay Room
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 43 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A port whose social hall is a beached hull still needs somewhere you can pay for a bed and a locked door.
why.siteAdvantages: On the basin front, one door from the hull hall and two from the gambling house.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who sells beds and rents silence.
why.pressures: Four languages in one room, and the guest book is worth more than the takings.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port were made lawful, the guest book becomes evidence and the keeper burns it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a mooring
places.hook: On the basin front, one door from the hull hall and two from the gambling house

places.name: The Old Pens
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 183 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: House Dres took Argonians out of this river country for centuries, and the pens they used to hold and count them are still standing on the bank they loaded from.
why.siteAdvantages: A river landing with hard standing, sited for loading rather than living.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The free port will not use the ground and will not explain why to outsiders.
why.pressures: It is the one thing in this zone nobody makes a joke about.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Dunmer factors in town were ever formally associated with it, the freehold's trade with Morrowind ends overnight.

hardConstraints: a river landing built for loading
places.hook: A river landing with hard standing, sited for loading rather than living

places.name: Andrano Hold
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 341 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.veterans-holding (+1.25).

why.founding: A House holding left over from the Dres trade, now a Dunmer village on the wrong side of the border that stayed because going home was worse.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible upland shelf on the pass road, with its own water and a walled core.
why.occupantsMotive: Dunmer families three centuries settled, who factor for the free port and are not liked for it.
why.pressures: They are the largest concentration of the zone's 22% Dunmer minority and they live beside the pens their ancestors filled.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Morrowind reasserted a claim here, the free port's northern trade becomes a diplomatic asset instead of a crime.

places.hook: A defensible upland shelf on the pass road, with its own water and a walled core

places.name: Five-Sixty Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The people who died in the Flu here were not Argonian and had no Hist to go to, so they were cairned where they fell, by whoever was left.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm dry ground above the village, with loose stone to hand.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the cairns are re-stacked by passing travellers, which is a custom nobody can explain.
why.pressures: It is the largest visible evidence in the zone that a whole people used to live here.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a scholar counted them properly, the district's population history changes.

places.hook: Firm dry ground above the village, with loose stone to hand

places.name: The Open Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 158 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: The price list has to be applied somewhere, and the stall row under the list board is where the zone's economy actually happens.
why.siteAdvantages: Level ground below the list board, one street from the basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Traders working in septims, Dunmer coin, barter and obligation at adjacent stalls.
why.pressures: The board is a public document that names contraband, which makes it the province's best commercial intelligence.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the list were withdrawn, the row would still meet and nobody would know what anything was worth.

places.hook: Level ground below the list board, one street from the basin

places.name: The Anomaly
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 598 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.rim-keystone-chamber (+0.47).

why.founding: A province with almost no metalworking has one here, because a free port that steals fastenings needs somewhere to reuse them.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the careening hard, on the only ground in the zone with a permanent forge.
why.occupantsMotive: A Nord smith who came off a hull twenty years ago and never re-embarked.
why.pressures: His stock is entirely other people's ship iron and everyone pretends not to know.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the fastening supply were cut, the forge goes cold and the boatwrights lose their hulls.

places.hook: Beside the careening hard, on the only ground in the zone with a permanent forge

places.name: Nine Sockets
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 224 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.freehold-smithy (+0.47).

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids left keystone mechanisms across the fringe of this country, and one of them is cut into the rim rock above the river.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry chamber in the ravine wall, above the flood and below the snow.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the mechanism is the occupant.
why.pressures: The sockets are empty and the keystones are elsewhere, which is exactly the problem the type poses.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the keystones were returned, whatever the chamber does would start doing it again.

places.hook: A dry chamber in the ravine wall, above the flood and below the snow

places.name: The Snowline Stage
places.whySiteWon: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 424 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The one legal crossing of the northern rim needs a staged shelter, because the pass is above the snowline for part of the year and people die on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle at 226 m: the lowest crossing of the wall for many kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who is nominally the state's and is paid by the free port, which he does not advertise.
why.pressures: The pass closes seasonally, and when it closes the ledge trade doubles.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the state funded it properly the rim would be policed and this zone's economy would change entirely.

hardConstraints: at the lowest crossing of the rim
places.hook: The saddle at 226 m: the lowest crossing of the wall for many kilometres

places.name: The North Traverse
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 233 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The free port's cargo has to leave the province somehow, and the legal crossings into Morrowind are few — so the illegal ones are the rim itself.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench two-thirds of the way up the border wall, out of sight from below and from the pass, with a traverse line rather than a path.
why.occupantsMotive: Two or three men who move consignments and mark which side each one is going.
why.pressures: It is a four-hour climb with a load and the weather on the rim turns without warning.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pass station below were properly manned, the ledge becomes the only route and the price triples.

hardConstraints: a rim ledge out of sight of the pass
no water — this is the dry route
places.hook: A cliff bench two-thirds of the way up the border wall, out of sight from below and from the pass, with a traverse line rather than a path

places.name: Exile's Roof
places.whySiteWon: summit in border mountains (danger band 3), 604 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Somebody was put out of an order and went as high as there is to go in this province, which is the northern rim.
why.siteAdvantages: Above the snowline on the border wall, with a spring that does not freeze.
why.occupantsMotive: One or two, keeping an observance nobody else keeps.
why.pressures: It is the coldest inhabited place in Argonia and reaching it is a genuine expedition.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the order that exiled them collapsed, the observance here becomes the only surviving version of it.

hardConstraints: a spring that does not freeze
places.hook: Above the snowline on the border wall, with a spring that does not freeze

places.name: Rockpoint
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 52 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A rival landing founded downriver to undercut Alten Corimont's list, which lost — because the river bar below it will not take a laden hull and the list will not be undercut.
why.siteAdvantages: A stone-footed landing, a warehouse shell and a defensible bank, all standing, on ground nobody now claims.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The bar that killed it also keeps casual squatters away, and Alten Corimont makes sure the story of why it failed is well told.
why.pressures: It is intact, empty, freehold ground with a river frontage — which in this zone is the most valuable unowned thing there is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If anyone repaired the landing and dredged the bar, Alten Corimont would have a competitor again, and would act.

hardConstraints: a standing landing and at least one roofed shell
downstream of the free port, below a bar
places.hook: A stone-footed landing, a warehouse shell and a defensible bank, all standing, on ground nobody now claims

places.name: The Trunk Span
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 270 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, route.

why.founding: The northern trunk road crosses the river at its narrowest point, and the crossing has an owner — as every crossing here does.
why.siteAdvantages: A water narrows with hard banks, on the Stormhold-to-Thorn line.
why.occupantsMotive: Four toll-takers working for a freehold syndicate that bought the span outright.
why.pressures: The Owing operates at this crossing, as it does at every tolled crossing in the route graph, and the ledger is kept in the open.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port bought the span, Stormhold's road trade would be paying Alten Corimont directly, which is why it has not happened.

hardConstraints: spans the channel at its narrowest
places.hook: A water narrows with hard banks, on the Stormhold-to-Thorn line

places.name: Blacklight Holding
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 371 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.dunmer-frontier-holding (+1.25).

why.founding: Argonians who went north into Morrowind in the 4E came back and would not settle in ordinary villages, so they made their own holding on the border they had crossed.
why.siteAdvantages: High firm ground with a view of the pass, chosen for the sightline rather than the soil.
why.occupantsMotive: Veterans and their children, armed, organised, and not answerable to the free port.
why.pressures: They are the only armed force in the zone and everyone is careful about what they are asked to do.
why.wouldChangeIf: If they were ever hired by the port, the freeholds become a power rather than a market.

hardConstraints: a view of the border crossing
places.hook: High firm ground with a view of the pass, chosen for the sightline rather than the soil

places.name: Archon
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'archon' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: A deep, sheltered estuary mouth on the Padomaic was the one place on this coast a foreign hull could lie safely, so the Second Empire and then the East Empire Company built a stone quay here and the Saxhleel town grew landward of it.
why.siteAdvantages: Estuary with a landable stone shore, a river road into the interior, and the only stretch of the east coast where the jungle wall breaks for more than a kilometre.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian-majority harbour population who work the water as amphibians and run the port authority out of dead Company offices, alongside state customs and a long-settled Dunmer merchant minority from the Morrowind trade.
why.pressures: The lawful port is the province's only functioning customs choke, so everything that wants to avoid it goes round it; the jungle behind the city is D4 within a kilometre of the gate; the sealed Shadowscale sanctuary is a thing nobody will discuss and everybody knows about.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line stopped running, or if the harbour authority lost its claim to the Company buildings, Archon would become a large fishing town in a month.

hardConstraints: deep water at the quay line at the highest seasonal level
places.hook: Estuary with a landable stone shore, a river road into the interior, and the only stretch of the east coast where the jungle wall breaks for more than a kilometre

places.name: Reaches-The-Low-Branch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 51 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, bound, parent.

why.founding: The register fixes a small Hist landward of the harbour — the city's own tree rather than a grove capital's, planted or tended where the salt does not reach.
why.siteAdvantages: The first freshwater ground behind the estuary: a low rise the tide never covers, inside the city's cleared apron.
why.occupantsMotive: Tree-minders keep it; dockworkers touch it going out and coming in; the Dunmer quarter does not.
why.pressures: Salt intrusion is rising with the quay works, and the tree is smaller than it was a century ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the estuary silts or the harbour cuts a deeper channel, this Hist dies and Archon becomes a Hist-less city with a port.

places.hook: The first freshwater ground behind the estuary: a low rise the tide never covers, inside the city's cleared apron

places.name: The Closed Sanctuary
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 313 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, region, parent.
