why.founding: Children born under the Shadow were given up to the Dark Brotherhood here under the old compact; the compact lapsed and the sanctuary was closed by order in 4E 187.
why.siteAdvantages: Deliberately unremarkable ground within an hour of a major city and its hatchery, with a concealed approach and no sightline from the river road.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. A watcher is paid to sit where he can see the path, by someone who has not visited in fourteen years.
why.pressures: The Cheydinhal Listener wanted it back; the harbour authority would rather it stopped existing; the birth-sign roll inside names living adults who do not know what they were promised to.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the roll were made public, or if the door were opened, half the Shadowscale line's premise collapses at once.

hardConstraints: concealed approach — no sightline from any route
places.hook: Deliberately unremarkable ground within an hour of a major city and its hatchery, with a concealed approach and no sightline from the river road

places.name: The Ashen Towers
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 709 m from the nearest route; no free 'headland' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, danger, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.terrace-village-ridge (+0.99).

why.founding: A Velothi offshoot came down this seaboard toward Morrowind, built in shapes nobody here has built before or since, and did not last — the culture zone's whole name rests on the layer they left.
why.siteAdvantages: A high headland with fresh water and a defensible neck, chosen for the same reasons Velothi always chose: it looks out toward home.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Dunmer families in Archon know the house mark and will not discuss it.
why.pressures: Salt has eaten the render for two thousand years; the ancestor niches are empty and the reason is not recorded.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a living House claimed descent, the Archon Dunmer quarter's standing in the city changes overnight.

hardConstraints: on the seaboard facing east toward Morrowind
a headland or islet with a neck
places.hook: A high headland with fresh water and a defensible neck, chosen for the same reasons Velothi always chose: it looks out toward home

places.name: Two-Marks-One-Rope
places.whySiteWon: cove in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 105 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland.

why.founding: Productive open water lying exactly between two villages that both claim it.
why.siteAdvantages: A shelf where cold water rises — reliably full of fish and reliably indefensible.
why.occupantsMotive: Both fleets work it, on alternate days when relations are good.
why.pressures: Claim buoys carry two marks on the same rope; gear has been cut adrift twice this year.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Archon's harbour authority licensed it, both villages would unite against the licence.

places.hook: A shelf where cold water rises — reliably full of fish and reliably indefensible

places.name: Nine Fathom
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 307 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.cantemir-headland (+1.30).

why.founding: A deeper bank out on the lane, worked by whoever has the hull to reach it.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep water, no shelter, a long run from any shore.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews from three settlements who do not meet ashore.
why.pressures: It is a day's sail from help and the weather here turns fast.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a storm shelter existed on the nearest islet the bank would be worked twice as hard.

places.hook: Deep water, no shelter, a long run from any shore

places.name: The Dusk Island
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in tidal delta (danger band 3), 402 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.mangrove-reef (+0.54).

why.founding: A low island in the lagoon where an enormous number of birds roost, worked for eggs and down under a rota.
why.siteAdvantages: An island with no predators, ringed by water too shallow for boats at low tide.
why.occupantsMotive: Egg-harvesters from two villages under a rota that limits the take.
why.pressures: The rota exists because they emptied it once; the harvesting frames are older than anyone using them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the rota broke, the column stops and the coast loses its one living landmark.

hardConstraints: island or stand surrounded by water
places.hook: An island with no predators, ringed by water too shallow for boats at low tide

places.name: The Estuary Mouth Station
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The Pass-1 transport compile already puts a rootworm terminus on the east estuary; this record fixes it as a real place with a reason — the coast's only fast link inland, at the one point where the root layer reaches tidewater.
why.siteAdvantages: Where a rootland arm runs out under firm ground within reach of the estuary landing.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who read the worms' movement and sell passage they cannot guarantee.
why.pressures: The worms are alive and seasonal; a standing station is a claim, not a timetable.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the root arm died back, the coast loses its only fast transit and Archon becomes a week from the interior.

places.hook: Where a rootland arm runs out under firm ground within reach of the estuary landing

places.name: Carves-All-Winter
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 72 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'headland' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.lagoon-storm-shelter (+0.62).

why.founding: A light needs a keeper, and a keeper needs a house within carrying distance of the fuel store.
why.siteAdvantages: The only sheltered hollow on the lighthouse headland.
why.occupantsMotive: Four generations of one family, contractually stuck with it and quietly expert.
why.pressures: The fuel account is paid late, every year, and the family has learned to hoard.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the light were automated or abandoned, the family would still be here, keeping nothing.

places.hook: The only sheltered hollow on the lighthouse headland

places.name: The Gap
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, submerged, hinterland.

why.founding: A bar across the estuary approach that every hull entering the province's principal legal port must thread.
why.siteAdvantages: Broken water over a shallow bar with a single buoyed gap, in otherwise navigable water.
why.occupantsMotive: Divers work the harvest lots; the wrecks on it are worked by everyone.
why.pressures: Three hulls are impaled on it at three different dates, and the buoys are moved by people who profit from that.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the lighthouse went dark, the count would be four within a season.

places.hook: Broken water over a shallow bar with a single buoyed gap, in otherwise navigable water

places.name: Eleven-Berth
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.estuary-keepers-lodge (+0.62).

why.founding: A second shelter on the lagoon crossing, because the crossing is two hours and the squalls are shorter than that.
why.siteAdvantages: A low islet with the only firm standing in the crossing.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; boat crews waiting out weather.
why.pressures: It floods in the worst storms, which is the joke everyone makes about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were raised a metre it would be the safest place on the lagoon.

places.hook: A low islet with the only firm standing in the crossing

places.name: The Standing Corner
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 782 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on remote, submerged, danger.

why.founding: A coastal xanmeer whose ground subsided with the delta; the terraces went under over centuries and only the topmost chamber still breaks the surface.
why.siteAdvantages: A lagoon deep enough to swallow six terraces, clear enough to see the geometry from a boat.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives in it that anybody has come back to describe.
why.pressures: It is a tended monument that can no longer be tended, which the nearest village finds unbearable.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water dropped a metre the tribe would reclaim it and it would stop being a dungeon.

hardConstraints: fully submerged but for one chamber
clear enough water to read the geometry
places.hook: A lagoon deep enough to swallow six terraces, clear enough to see the geometry from a boat

places.name: One-Chest
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Somebody furnished a trapped air space inside a flooded structure, and whoever they are they chose this.
why.siteAdvantages: Enclosed by water on all sides; the only approach is a dive of about twenty metres.
why.occupantsMotive: One or two occupants, or their belongings.
why.pressures: Everything in it is too heavy to swim out with, which is deliberate.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water level fell the room becomes an ordinary cellar and worthless.

places.hook: Enclosed by water on all sides; the only approach is a dive of about twenty metres

places.name: Black-Cut Teeth
places.whySiteWon: islet in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 60 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.dusk-bird-colony (+0.54).

why.founding: Where the mangrove wall meets open water a shell bar has built up and been farmed for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow, sheltered, walkable at the lowest tides.
why.occupantsMotive: Two villages work alternate lots by an agreement nobody has written down.
why.pressures: The agreement is one bad season from being a fight.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either village lost its boats, the other would take the whole bar in a month.

places.hook: Shallow, sheltered, walkable at the lowest tides

places.name: Lost-The-Ospreye
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 187 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: The outer bar the shipping lane keeps clear of, which is why it is still alive.
why.siteAdvantages: Clear water over a healthy reef, far enough offshore that nobody works it daily.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Divers come out for a day and go home.
why.pressures: It is the healthiest thing on the coast and the least defended.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harvest lots moved out here, it would look like the Gap in fifteen years.

places.hook: Clear water over a healthy reef, far enough offshore that nobody works it daily

places.name: Portdun Mont
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 213 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, ring.

why.founding: A watch station on the headland that every hull must round to enter Archon; the village grew on the bench behind the watch.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench above deep water, sightline down the whole estuary approach, and a beach landing below the stair.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilot families who take fees to bring hulls in, and who remember when the fee was collected differently.
why.pressures: Archon's authority stops at the headland; the pilots' monopoly is customary, not legal, and the anchorage below the cliff has a past.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harbour authority licensed its own pilots, Portdun Mont would be a fishing hamlet in a year.

hardConstraints: a bench above water with a landing below
places.hook: A cliff bench above deep water, sightline down the whole estuary approach, and a beach landing below the stair

places.name: The Three Tongues
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 62 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A port needs paid lodging with a fire, a bed and a room full of people who know things.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay front, one door from the mooring line.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who trades in information as her actual business.
why.pressures: Three languages in one room and two of them are lying.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port trade fell away this becomes a village inn and the coast loses its densest hook node.

hardConstraints: on a route with a landing
places.hook: On the quay front, one door from the mooring line

places.name: Seafalls
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A river drops to the sea in a set of falls a loaded boat cannot pass, so every cargo moving between the coast and the interior is unloaded here — and a town grew on the transfer.
why.siteAdvantages: The furthest point upriver a laden boat can reach, with landings above and below the drop and firm ground between.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, transfer clerks and hauliers whose entire livelihood is that the falls exist.
why.pressures: The navigable limit moves with the season and this year's board does not match last year's; the porters price accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the portage slipway above the falls were ever mechanised, the town's whole labour economy evaporates.

hardConstraints: landings above and below the drop
places.hook: The furthest point upriver a laden boat can reach, with landings above and below the drop and firm ground between

places.name: Seven-Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 657 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: Deliberately closed by its own people, with its traps live and its vakka-stone mechanisms intact.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep in D4 jungle with no tending path, which is why nobody reopened it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the mechanisms count as occupants.
why.pressures: The tending clan a valley away knows the door and will not open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were opened, whatever it was closed against becomes everyone's problem.

places.hook: Deep in D4 jungle with no tending path, which is why nobody reopened it

places.name: Haj-Mota Wallow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 318 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The animals that supply the shell trade have to live somewhere, and they live where the mud is deep and the water shallow.
why.siteAdvantages: Churned shallow mud at the delta edge, warm and food-rich.
why.occupantsMotive: A small number of very large animals and one abandoned set of cutter's tools.
why.pressures: The yard needs them and the villages fear them, in the same week.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the wallow were worked out the shell yard closes and the district's shields become imports.

places.hook: Churned shallow mud at the delta edge, warm and food-rich

places.name: Climbs-The-Long-Back
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 320 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.cantemir-headland (+0.99).

why.founding: Above the flood line the ground rises, and a village that wanted to be above the water built up a ridge in steps.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge shelf with drainage, a spring head above and a defensible single approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Households who grow on terraces and trade downhill.
why.pressures: The spring is the whole settlement and it is one collapse from failing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the spring failed, the village would be on the coast within a season.

places.hook: A ridge shelf with drainage, a spring head above and a defensible single approach

places.name: The Two-Hour Flat
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A delta flat that shortens the coast journey and is crossable only while the basin's tidal amplitude leaves it dry - in practice a short morning, and not the same morning twice.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm sand under shallow water at low tide, marked by a stake line laid generations ago.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it; six people are usually waiting at the head.
why.pressures: The tide does not negotiate, the window is never the same length twice, and the body count is carved on the waiting shelter's post.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a causeway were ever built here, the whole district's travel times change and the shelter dies.

hardConstraints: firm bed under the marked line
places.hook: Firm sand under shallow water at low tide, marked by a stake line laid generations ago

places.name: Four-Eight
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 189 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Umbriel crossed this coast in 4E 48 and the bodies it left had to go somewhere the Hist could not be blamed for.
why.siteAdvantages: A tidal flat above the village line where the ground could be opened quickly and in quantity.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers still call here on the way south; nobody else does.
why.pressures: The dead here were stripped, so there is nothing to repatriate, which is the whole grievance.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a way were found to return even one of them, the Umbriel Witness Society gains its first real relic.

hardConstraints: ground that can be opened in quantity
places.hook: A tidal flat above the village line where the ground could be opened quickly and in quantity

places.name: Still-Water Sleeping-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 342 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The Argonian majority of this coast lives behind the port, not in it: a tribal village around its own Hist, an hour inland of the road.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise inside the jungle wall with fresh water and a canopy break the Hist made itself.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe who trade with Archon and have no interest in living there.
why.pressures: The port wants their timber and their labour; the village supplies exactly as much as it chooses.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Hist stopped speaking, the village disperses and Archon gains a hundred Hist-less households.

hardConstraints: a living Hist with a canopy break
places.hook: A firm rise inside the jungle wall with fresh water and a canopy break the Hist made itself
